name: Mia
description:
Meet Mia!  Mia is a beautiful girl who is looking for a patient, understanding and experienced home where she can learn that the world isn’t such a scary place.  Mia is a very timid and nervous girl who is still finding her feet with us.  Since arriving 3 months ago, very emaciated and in a bad state she has started to come around with our staff, and has put weight on nicely and we are beginning to see the sweet girl hiding behind all that uncertainty.  Mia is still a bit wary when the staff enter her kennel and will often retreat to the back.  Having her harness put on can also be a worrying experience for her, so she needs gentle handling, reassurance and plenty of time to feel comfortable.  With calm encouragement and a kind approach, Mia responds well and is slowly learning to trust the people around her.  One thing Mia does enjoy is a good brush!  It’s lovely to see her discovering little moments of comfort, and we are celebrating every small step she takes towards building her confidence.  When out in our secure compound, Mia isn’t particularly interested in toys just yet.  She would much rather take her time having a good sniff around and exploring her surroundings at her own pace.  For Mia, it’s all about taking things slowly, without pressure or expectations.  Mia will need an experienced Dogue De Bordeaux owner who understands the breed and is prepared to give her time, patience and the consistency she needs.  She will need someone who can read her body language, respect her boundaries and allow her confidence to grow at her own pace.  She may take time to settle into her new home, but with the right person by her side, we know she will continue to blossom.  Mia isn’t a girl who will rush up to you looking for a fuss just yet.  She’s a girl who needs you to gain her trust, gently and patiently.  But beneath that nervous exterior is a very sweet dog who deserves the chance to feel safe, secure and loved. Mia will need a private secure garden.

Mia has had a heart scan and echo cardiogram done and has a minor mitral valve issue, which currently isn’t causing her any problems.  This will be discussed in detail with the successful applicant.

Mia has interacted with other dogs while in our care, and is very nervous and unsure around them, so we feel she would be best rehomed as the only dog in the home where she can take her time gaining her confidence around other dogs with the full support and gentle guidance of her new adopter.

As Mia came into the home as a stray, we have no previous history on her and as she is very timid we would prefer any children/visiting children to be 16+ years.

Please only apply if you have the experience and commitment to work with Mia and give her the time and space she will need.

name: Lily
description:
Lily is a young girl who has spent some time in a racing environment. She is very nervous around people, especially new people so is going to need a family that is willing to be patient and give her time to settle down. Lily needs to learn that new people mean no harm and build up her confidence. Lily will need all of the basic training once she goes home, as she has never lived in a home before. We feel that once she has settled down in a home and built up her confidence she will make a great companion who will enjoy going on adventures and having plenty of cuddles. Greyhounds can have cheeky personalities and are quite playful dogs once they come out of their shell. Lily just needs a family that will give her the chance to become this and with her young age still has her whole life ahead.

We feel that Lily would benefit from a calm, quiet adult household. No children visiting. Experience with the breed or nervous rescue dogs would be beneficial.

Lily can be nervous around dogs but is paired in a kennel with another greyhound. We feel that she could potentially live with another dog of the same breed to help bring her out of her shell, as she does seem more confident when her kennel mate is around- subject to a successful meet.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3 months.

name: Hayley
description:
Hayley is an ex racing greyhound who has spent all of her life in kennels. She is now looking for a loving comfortable home to call her own. She will need training to help her settle into life in a home environment as this will all be new for her. She is an affectionate girl who likes to do a little dance every time someone goes into the kennel with her. She is food motivated and loves her treats which will help with her training. She has plenty of potential to be a great companion for the right home.

We feel that Hayley can be rehomed with dog savvy children who are 16 years and over – Subject to a successful meet.

Hayley would be best suited to being the only dog in the home. She is currently paired with another greyhound but can be very unsure around dogs that she doesn’t know. Continued positive training will be needed to help build up her confidence in this area.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3 months.

name: Tommy
description:
Tommy is an ex racing greyhound who has spent his life in kennels. He is now looking for a comfortable and loving home to call his own. He will need a family that is happy to introduce and train him around everything that is involved in living in a home environment. Tommy is a very affectionate boy and has been described as a velcro dog by the kennel staff. He is after a home where he can get plenty of attention and cuddles throughout the day. He is a big foodie and is motivated by treats, which is a bonus to help with training.

Tommy is confident around staff and volunteers but due to his size we believe that he would be best suited to an adult only home.

Tommy is a little unsure around most dogs so will need further positive training to help build up his confidence in this area. He is currently paired with another greyhound in the kennel and has has no issues with her, so we believe that he could be rehomed with another calm greyhound or sighthound – subject to a successful meet.

No cats or small furries for Tommy due to his racing background.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3 months.

name: Derby
description:
Derby is a sensitive, gentle soul who is still finding his feet and learning that the world doesn’t have to be a scary place. A lot of things at the moment are frightening for him, but we are beginning to see small glimpses of his confidence growing. Although he can be very nervous, underneath his worries is an incredibly affectionate boy who absolutely loves human company. He really enjoys cuddles and gentle strokes, if you dare to stop fussing him, he will reach out with his paw and ask for more. It is impossible not to fall in love with his sweet personality. He spends much of his time curled up on his comfy bed, where he feels safe and secure, but he will pop out to say hello when a familiar face visits his kennel. He enjoys a run around to stretch his legs in compound area, but isn’t sure about toys yet so would much rather stay close his his handler.

He’s had positive, friendly interactions with other dogs so we believe that he could potentially be re homed with a dog of a calm temperament and similar size – subject to a successful meet.

Due to his nervous nature we believe that Derby would be best suited to living in a calm house with children who are 16 years and over – subject to success meet. It is likely that he would need multiple meets to get to know his new family before he goes home.

If you feel that you could provide Derby with a peaceful, patient and understanding forever home please apply for Derby today!

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3 months.

name: Amanda
description:
Amanda came into our care as a stray so we don’t have any background information on her. She was a little unsure and nervous when she first arrived but has slowly started to come out of her shell. She can be affectionate once she knows you. She is a typical cheeky Frenchie who likes to have her own way. She is looking for a home with a family that has previous experience or knowledge of the breed and is happy to work with her until she is more settled. We believe that Amanda may need some basic training to help her improve her manners in the home.

Amanda has socialised well with dogs whilst in our care, so we feel that she could potentially be rehomed with a dog of similar size and temperament – subject to a successful meet.

We feel that Amanda would be best suited for an adult only home, no visiting children.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3 months.

name: Pumba
description:
Meet Pumba! Pumba is a gorgeous boy who was a little nervous when he first arrived with us, but it didn’t take him long to realise he was safe.  Before long, his lovely personality started to shine through, and he has blossomed into a very sweet, friendly and affectionate boy.  Pumba loves a fuss and is happiest when he is getting attention from his people.  He is a very vocal lad and certainly isn’t shy about letting you know what he wants – especially if there is a ball involved.  And speaking of toys … Pumba LOVES his toys! in fact, toys are his life!  His favourite part of the day is getting off-lead in our secure compound, where he can race around, play and chase after his favourite toys.  While he does enjoy a tasty treat, if you gave him the choice between a snack and a toy, we are pretty sure the toy would win every time.  Pumba is an active and energetic boy who will need a home that can keep up with his enthusiasm.  He new family should enjoy getting out and about and be prepared to give him plenty of exercise, playtime and mental stimulation.  A home where he can continue to enjoy lots of games, and, of course plenty of toys would be ideal.  Pumba will need someone who is willing to continue basic training and help him learn the routines and manners expected in a home.  He does sometimes urinate in his bed, so his new family will need to be patient and understanding while working on his toilet habits.  Pumba is a fun-loving boy with a big personality, plenty of energy and an even bigger love for his toys.  Pumba would benefit from a private secure garden.

Pumba has socialised well with other dogs while in our care, but he can be very full-on.  We do feel he could potentially live with another dog that would tolerate his boisterous play style following a successful meet and greet.

As Pumba came into the home as a stray, we have no previous history on him, so would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Nemo
description:
Meet Nemo!  Nemo is a lovely boy with a big personality and plenty of love to give.  He can be a little nervous when he first meets you, but once he gets to know you, his true character really shines through.  When Nemo sees someone he knows, he gets incredibly excited and happy to see them – his whole body tells you just how pleased he is!  He is a very affectionate boy who absolutely loves fuss, attention and being around his people.  He enjoys plenty of affection and will happily soak up all the attention you’re willing to give him.  Like many young, energetic dogs, Nemo can get a little over-excited.  He does jump up for attention and become a bit mouthy when he is over stimulated, so his new owner will need to be patient and willing to help him learn appropriate ways to manage his excitement.  Positive, reward-based training and consistency will be important for him.  Nemo is a very active and energetic boy and will need an active home where he can get plenty of exercise, enrichment and mental stimulation.  He would love a family who enjoys long walks and can give him opportunities to use both his body and his clever Cockapoo brain.  He will need more than just a quick walk around the block!  Nemo can be vocal when he is in kennels, so his new family should be prepared for him to need some time to settle into a home environment and feel secure.  One thing adopters will also need to be aware of is that Nemo currently urinates on his bedding.  This may be related to his current environment, routine or stress, but his new family will need to be prepared to work patiently with him on his toileting habits and not expect everything to be perfect immediately.  Nemo has so much potential to be a wonderful companion.  Once he feels comfortable with you, he is an incredibly affectionate and happy boy who loves nothing more than seeing his people and getting lots of fuss.  He would benefit from a private secure garden.

Nemo has socialised well with other dogs while in our care, so we feel he could potentially be rehomed with another dog of similar size and energy levels following a successful meet and greet. (must be neutered).

As Nemo came into the home as a stray, we have no previous history on him, so would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Albie
description:
Meet Albie!  Albie is a lovely boy with a big personality and lots of love to give.  He is a very friendly, affectionate and excitable boy who loves being around people and getting plenty of attention.  He can be a real giddy lad and, when he’s excited, he does jump up for attention and can be a bit mouthy.  He is also very vocal in his kennel.  With his high energy levels, Albie will need an active home where he can enjoy plenty of exercise, long walks and adventures.  He absolutely loves getting out and about, exploring his surroundings and taking in all the interesting smells.  He is quite strong on the lead so will need continued lead training.  He also enjoys playing with his toys, although he prefers to play on his own with them and will chase around our compound proudly showing you what he has got. Albie does know some basic commands, but will benefit from further training and guidance to help him develop into the best version of himself.  His new adopter will need to continue working on his manners, particularly around jumping up and mouthing when over-excited.  Ongoing socialisation will also be important for him.  As well as physical exercise, Albie will need plenty of mental stimulation to keep his clever and energetic mind occupied.  Enrichment, training games, interactive toys and learning new skills would all be great ways to help him burn off some of that enthusiasm.  Albie is looking for an active and committed home that will enjoy his fun-loving personality, give him plenty of exercise and enrichment, and be willing to continue his training and socialisation.  In return, he has plenty of affection, enthusiasm and fun to offer.  Albie will need a private secure garden.

Albie has interacted with other dogs while in our care and we have found him to be very under-socialised.  He can be very unsure around some and will bark and others he will have a sniff but still a little uncomfortable. We feel he would be best rehomed as the only dog in the home where his new adopter can continue building up his confidence around other dogs with plenty of positive reinforcement in a controlled environment and they must go at Albie’s pace.

As Albie came into the home as a stray, we have no previous history on him so would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Frank
description:
Meet Frank!  Frank is a sweet-natured boy who absolutely loves people and enjoys being the centre of attention.  He is a very giddy and excitable character, and his enthusiasm can sometimes get the better of him!  Frank loves treats and is always keen to show off what he knows.  He has his basic commands and is eager to learn, especially when there’s a tasty reward involved.  He can be quite vocal in his kennel, and when excited he can become a little mouthy.  He also loves attention and will jump up to say hello, so his new adopter will need to be comfortable helping him learn some calmer ways to greet people.  Frank is a strong boy on the lead and will need continued training and guidance with his lead manners.  He is an active dog who needs plenty of exercise as well as mental stimulation to keep his busy mind occupied.  Frank is looking for an active and committed home where his new family can give him the exercise, enrichment, training and attention he needs.  His ideal home will be one where his adopters understand that he is an excitable, energetic boy and are prepared to work with him on his manners and impulse control.  In return, Frank has so much affection and enthusiasm to give.  He will need a private secure garden.

Frank has socialised well with other dogs while in our care, so we feel he could potentially live with another dog of similar size following a successful meet and greet.

As Frank came into the home as a stray, we have no previous history on him so would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years

name: Milo
description:
Meet Milo!  Milo is an absolute sweetheart and a real people-lover.  This lovely boy is happiest when he has your undivided attention and, if he had his way, he’d spend his days right by your side soaking up cuddles and affection.  He really is a needy cuddle bug.  Milo enjoys having some off-lead time in our secure compound, where he loves to stretch his legs and have a good run around.  But it doesn’t take him long before he comes trotting back to your side, ready for some more fuss.  He can be a little mouthy when he gets over-excited, especially when he desperately wants your attention, so he’ll need someone who can help him learn to manage that excitement and give him some positive guidance.  He is just a gorgeous boy with a huge love for people.  If you are looking for a loyal companion who will happily follow you around, and shower you with affection and make sure you never feel lonely, Milo could be the boy for you.  As Milo is a real people dog and thrives on having company, he would be best suited to a home where someone is around most of the day.

Milo has interacted with other dogs whilst in our care, and he doesn’t seem too interested in them so we feel he would be best rehomed as the only dog in the home where he can get 100% of the fuss and cuddles.

As Milo came into the home as a stray, we have no previous history on him, so we would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Merlin
description:
Meet Merlin!  Merlin is an energetic, cheeky character of a dog half his age!  Don’t let Merlin’s age fool you – this boy is very active and full of life.  He’s a giddy, playful Terrier who absolutely loves having fun and will happily keep you entertained with his antics.  Merlin loves toys and balls and is always ready for a game.  Like many Terriers, he can get rather enthusiastic during play and can be a little mouthy, so his new adopter will need to understand his play style and help him learn appropriate boundaries.  He is also a vocal boy and isn’t afraid to let you know what he thinks!  Merlin is a real character with plenty of Terrier spirit and a cheeky personality.  Merlin is a bit of an escape artist, so his new home will need to be secure and his adopters will need to be mindful of his ability to find an opportunity to make an exit.  He also enjoys digging up grass, so anyone hoping for a perfectly manicured lawn may need to rethink their expectations.  Merlin can be quite jumpy, particularly when excited, and his new family will need to work with him calmly and consistently on this behaviour. He is very unsure about being brushed and does not like his back end being touched.  Merlin has been checked over by the vet and there are no health concerns identified, but this is something his adopters will need to be aware of and respect.  He may need time, patience and positive experiences to build up his confidence around grooming and handling.  Merlin also doesn’t particularly enjoy visiting the vets and has needed to be muzzled during veterinary handling.  His future family should therefore be prepared to continue using sensible precautions and work at his pace when it comes to handling.  Merlin needs an experienced, understanding home who appreciates the wonderful – and sometimes challenging qualities that come with a feisty Terrier.  He will need plenty of exercise, play, mental stimulation and a secure outdoor space, along with people who are prepared to put the time into helping him with his manners and handling.  In return, Merlin will give you bags of personality, fun and affection.  He is a lively, cheeky old boy who clearly hasn’t realised he’s supposed to be slowing down!  If you are looking for a quiet, sedate 10 year old, merlin probably isn’t your man.  But if you love giddy, playful, vocal, mischievous Terriers with big personalities, merlin could be the boy for you.

Merlin has socialised well with other dogs whilst in our care, so we do feel he could be rehomed with another older small dog following a successful meet and greet.

As Merlin came into the home as a stray, we have no previous history on him and as he can be touch sensitive we would prefer any children/visiting children in the home to be 16+ years.

name: Rafi
description:
Rafi is a lively, happy boy with a cheeky personality. Rafi is still just a young boy who is in need of a stable and loving home. He is after a family that is happy to put in a lot of time and effort into his training to help him improve his manners. Dobermans are a breed that need to be worked with for their entire life so we are after someone who is fully committed to taking on this responsibility. Experience with this breed or similar is also a must.

Rafi is going to need a large fully enclosed garden that he can have off lead time in, to burn off energy and to help with his training. Rafi will need plenty of walks and mental stimulation to keep him occupied so he doesn’t cause too much mischief. Rafi would benefit from a home where someone is around a lot and has plenty of free time to focus on him and his training.

Rafi is best suited to an adult only home, with no visiting children.

Rafi needs to be the only dog in the home, no visiting dogs either. Rafi is currently under going socialisation training with dogs to help improve his reactivity. This is something that will need to be continued when he goes home and into the future.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3 months.

name: Daisy
description:
Meet Daisy! She is a friendly, sweet-natured girl who absolutely loves her cuddles and enjoys being around people.  Daisy has a lovely playful side too and can often be found having a good old run around our secure compound, chasing after her favourite toys and enjoying some classic Greyhound zoomies!  Daisy walks nicely on the lead and is a pleasure to take out.  She also loves being groomed, happily enjoying all the attention and fuss.  Like many ex-racing greyhounds, Daisy has never lived in a home before, so her new adopter will need to give her time, patience and understanding while she learns all about home life.  House training, new routines, household noises and settling into a new environment will all be a completely new experience for her, with kindness, consistency and plenty of reassurance, Daisy can begin to discover just how wonderful life as a much-loved pet can be.  When she gets over excited, Daisy can be a little mouthy, so her new adopter will need to help her learn appropriate ways to express her excitement.  Daisy is a fun-loving, affectionate girl with plenty of personality.  She loves to play, enjoys cuddles and is ready to leave her racing days behind and start the next chapter of her life.  Daisy has so much love and fun to give and is looking forward to finding a special family she can call her own.  Daisy will need a private secure garden so she can safely have off lead time.

Daisy has socialised well with other dogs whilst in our care, so we feel she could potentially live with another dog of similar size following a successful meet and greet.

As Daisy can be a little nippy when she is over excited we would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Todd
description:
This handsome boy is Todd!  Todd is a sweet, friendly and very lively boy with plenty of energy to spare!  He is a typical hound in many ways – full of enthusiasm, curious about the world around him and always ready for his next adventure.  He absolutely loves his off-lead time in our secure compound where he can stretch his legs, explore, have a sniff and have fun with his favourite toys.  Watching Todd enjoy himself is a real pleasure! As you would expect from a Fox Hound, Todd is high-energy and needs a very active home that can provide him with plenty of daily exercise.  Walks alone may not be enough to keep his body and mind satisfied, so he would really benefit from additional activities such as scent work, tracking games, enrichment and other opportunities to use his wonderful Hound brain.  Todd is also a vocal boy – hounds are known for their voices, and Todd is certainly not shy about using his!  His new family will need to appreciate that hound singing, baying and general commentary are part of the package.  Hounds are also known for being escape artists so he will need secure, hound-proof fencing and careful management, particularly when he is outdoors. A home that understands the determination and curiosity of a scent-driven hound would be ideal.  Todd has so much character and has all the makings of a fantastic companion in the right home.  He needs someone who understands that a Fox Hound is a lifestyle, not just a pet – but for the right home, Todd will bring plenty of fun, affection and adventure.

Todd has socialised well with other dogs whilst in our care and is very playful and full-on.  We do feel he could potentially live with another dog of similar energy levels that would tolerate his play style following a successful meet and greet.

As Todd came into the home as a stray, we have no previous history on him so would prefer any children in the home to be 16+ years.

name: Shadow
description:
Shadow is a very affectionate boy who has been super friendly to our staff and volunteers since he came in to our care. With him being an ex racer, he does have a high prey drive so can try to chase squirrels whilst out for his walks! He absolutely loves chasing his toys around our secure compound.  He is a really affectionate boy who loves lots of fuss and attention.

Shadow will have spent most of his life in kennels with his racing background, so he may feel a little nervous going in to a home environment. We also do not know if he is house trained or toilet trained due to this. He loves to lie in his comfy beds after his walks – we sometimes catch him upside down showing his belly off!

Shadow has now been in our care for 237 days and is desperately searching for his forever home.

We think Shadow would prefer to be the only dog in the home as he can sometimes be a little unsure around them and isn’t too interested in interacting with them.

He could also potentially live with children 14+ years  – subject to a successful meet.

Shadow would love a home where he could relax and enjoy his retirement years and rest on a comfy bed (or couch) of his own!

name: Oscar
description:
Meet Oscar! He is a lovely boy with a huge personality and plenty of puppyish energy!  Oscar is a very lively, energetic and friendly boy who is always ready for his next adventure.  He is a big puppy at heart – giddy, playful and full of enthusiasm and he loves being around people.  Oscar can be quite an excitable boy and does jump up, particularly when he is happy or excited.  He is also very vocal, so his new family should be prepared for a dog who likes to make his presence known!  Oscar has a very playful side.  When staff are cleaning his kennel, he thinks the hose pipe and brushes are fantastic toys and will chase them around.  His enthusiasm can sometimes get the better of him, so he will need patient guidance to learn more appropriate ways to channel his energy.  On walks, Oscar does pull on the lead and will need continued training to help him develop his loose-lead walking skills.  He would really benefit from an owner who enjoys training and can provide consistent positive reinforcement.  Oscar is looking for an active home where he can enjoy plenty of exercise, enrichment and mental stimulation.  He is not a couch-potato kind of boy!  His ideal family will enjoy getting out and about with him and be prepared to give him the time and training he needs to mature into a well-mannered adult.  His new adopter should be willing to work on his impulse control, socialisation and general training.  As a young Lurcher, Oscar will need patience, consistency and plenty of appropriate outlets for his energy.  Underneath all that excitement is a loveable, friendly and very giddy young boy who is still learning about the world.  He will need a private secure garden.

Oscar has socialised well with other dogs whilst in our care and is very playful.  We do feel he could potentially be rehomed with another lively and energetic dog of similar size following a successful meet and greet.

As Oscar came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on him so would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Rudy
description:
Meet Rudy!  Don’t let his age fool you, this lively, energetic boy has plenty of energy and enthusiasm. Rudy is a friendly, excitable and affectionate boy who absolutely loves attention and fuss.  He has a big personality and is not shy about letting you know when he wants you to interact with him!  Rudy can be quite vocal when he wants your attention or, more importantly, when he thinks it’s time for you to throw his ball.  One of Rudy’s favourite things is chasing his toys, and he could happily spend plenty of time playing and having fun.  He also enjoys his long walks and would love an active home who can provide him with plenty of exercise and opportunities to explore.  Rudy is a strong boy on the lead, so his new adopters will need to be confident handling him and willing to continue on his lead manners.  He does know his basic commands and, with the right guidance, could continue to build on these.  Rudy is looking for an active home where he can enjoy lots of walks, playtime and mental stimulation.  He would suit someone who enjoys getting out and about and is looking for a fun, lively companion with a larger-than-life personality.  Rudy will need a private secure garden.

Rudy has interacted well with other dogs whilst in our care, so we feel he could potentially be rehomed with another lively dog of similar size following a successful meet and greet.

As Rudy came into the home as a stray, we have no previous history on him so would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Pumpkin
description:
Pumpkin came into our care as a stray, at first she was unsure and a little worried, but with time and patience Pumpkin has well and truly come out of her shell. Her big beautiful personality is shining through and she has become a lovely confident girl. Pumpkin enjoys meeting new people and adores a good cuddle. She likes going out on her walks as well as a good run around in our enclosed exercise area – she can at times be very strong when walking on a lead.

When Pumpkin first arrived, she was carrying a little extra weight, but with a little love, a healthy diet and plenty of care, she has made fantastic progress. She has worked hard to lose the weight she needed to be ready for adoption, and we couldn’t be happier with her transformation. Her new family will need to continue supporting her healthy lifestyle, helping her stay happy, healthy and thriving in her forever home!

We do believe she would be best suited to an adult only home, where she can also be the only dog, as she would prefer to have her own space. Pumpkin does still like socialising with other dogs and does enjoy saying hello whilst out on her walks.

Pumpkin wouldn’t be suitable to live with a cat or any other small animal.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3 months.

name: Hero
description:
Hero is an ex racing greyhound who is now looking for his forever home with a family that can help him settle into life beyond the kennels. He is a confident, lively boy with plenty of personality. He gets very excited when it’s time for a walk and can jump around on the lead, so will need someone who is comfortable handling a tall strong greyhound. With a little training and consistency this is something that can be worked on. Although he is confident in many ways, he does need help building his confidence when it comes to being touched and handled as he can get a little worried.  Hero deserves the chance to learn, grow and discover just how good life can be outside of kennels.

Hero can be rehomed with mature children who are 16 years and over, due to his size and bouncy nature. This will be subject to a successful meet.

Hero is currently paired with another greyhound and has interreacted well with dogs whilst in our care, so we believe that he would be rehomed with another dog- subject to a successful meet and greet.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3  months.

name: Brie
description:
Meet Brie!  Brie is a very friendly, playful and sweet girl who is an absolute pleasure to have around.  She gets incredibly excited when you go into her kennel and will happily show you just how pleased she is with a few adorable zoomies!  She has a fun, cheeky personality and one of her favourite things is chasing the scrubbing brush around her kennel when the staff are cleaning – she certainly knows how to keep you entertained!  Brie is a lovely girl who enjoys human company and has plenty of character.  She would benefit from continued training, socialisation and positive guidance to help her build on the progress she has already made.  If you are looking for a fun-loving affectionate Frenchie with a big personality and plenty of love to give, Brie could be the girl for you.  She deserves a caring, committed home where she can continue to learn, grow and enjoy life.

Brie has socialised well with other dogs whilst in our care, so we feel following a successful meet and greet she could live with another calm dog (must be neutered).

As Brie came into the home as a stray, we have no previous history on her so would prefer any children in the home to be 10+ years.

name: Mischief
description:
Meet Mischief!  This lovely girl is looking for a very special home.  Mischief is a very timid and nervous girl who has slowly started to come out of her shell.  She will need patient, understanding adopters who are willing to give her the time and space she needs to build confidence and learn that she is safe.  Once Mischief trusts you, you get to see the sweet girl underneath.  She is affectionate and loving, enjoys giving kisses, and absolutely loves a good belly rub.  Seeing her begin to relax and show her gentle personality is incredibly rewarding.  Mischief does have a cheeky side to her name!  She is a talented escape artist and has been known to jump the kennel walls, so her new home will need secure fencing and adopters who are prepared for her Houdini tendencies.  Extra care will be needed to make sure the doesn’t escape open doors or fences.  Mischief is not looking for a busy or rushed home.  She needs someone who understands that trust takes time and is willing to let her progress at her own pace.  Any potential adopters will need to commit to several regular meet and greets before the adoption can take place.

Mischief has socialised well with other dogs whilst in our care, although she does prefer a calmer dog.  We do feel she could be rehomed with another calm dog following a successful meet and greet (must be neutered).

As Mischief came into the home as a stray, we have no previous history on her and as she can be very nervous we would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Ripley
description:
Meet Ripley!! He is a gorgeous boy looking for an active, committed home where he can continue to learn and thrive.  He’s a friendly, affectionate boy with a fun-loving personality and is always ready for a game with his favourite toys.  He is full of energy and loves to play, so he will need an active family who can provide plenty of exercise, enrichment, and ongoing training.  Like many young dogs, he can become a little mouthy and nippy when he’s excited, so he will benefit from patient guidance and positive reinforcement to help him learn appropriate manners.  He is still working on his basic commands and will need someone willing to continue his training.  He can also occasionally rag his lead, so further lead training will be important.  Previous experience with Shar-pei’s would be a real advantage, as they can have their own unique characteristics and training needs.  He currently has a cherry eye, which will be surgically repaired before he goes to his new home, so he’ll be ready to start his next chapter feeling his best.  If you’re looking for a playful, lively young dog and have to time and commitment to help him become the wonderful companion we know he can be, Ripley could be the boy for you.

Ripley has socialised well with other dogs and is very playful with them.  He can sometimes get frustrated and bark if he can’t get to them straight away.  We feel he could potentially be rehomed with another playful dog of similar size following a successful meet and greet.

As Ripley came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on him and as he can be a little nippy when over-excited we would like any children in the home to be 16+ years.

name: Arlo
description:
Meet Arlo! Arlo is a gorgeous, sweet-natured boy who is very friendly and absolutely loves lots of fuss.  He’s a real people dog and enjoys getting plenty of attention and affection.  He is a very energetic and boisterous lad who can get extremely giddy when he’s excited.  He sometimes forgets just how big he is and will jump up to say hello, so he would benefit from some basic training to help him learn his manners and channel all that enthusiasm.  Arlo recently had a bath, and although he was a little nervous to begin with, he was a very good boy.  Once it was all over, he celebrated in true Arlo style with a case of the zoomies!  He also has a funny habit of rearranging his bed and moving it to wherever he thinks it should be.  Arlo is a loveable, fun, lively character with bags of personality.  He would thrive in a very active home with someone who can give him plenty of exercise, long walks and consistency with his training.  He would need a private secure garden so he can practice his zoomies!

Arlo has socialised well with other dogs whilst in our care and is very playful, so we feel following a successful meet and greet he could live with another dog of similar size and energy level.

As Arlo came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on him so would prefer any children in the home to be 16+ years.

name: Lyra
description:
Meet Lyra!  This beautiful girl is looking for an active, experienced home where she can thrive.  She is a lovely, sweet-natured girl with a very giddy and playful personality.  Lyra absolutely loves attention and fuss and is always happy to be involved in whatever is going on.  She has lots of enthusiasm for life and certainly isn’t shy about showing it! Lyra can jump up quite a lot when she gets excited, so this is something her new adopter will need to be prepared to work on.  She is also very strong on the lead and will need someone confident and capable of handling her while they continue training.  As you would expect from a Malinois, Lyra is an active, energetic dog who will need plenty of physical exercise, mental stimulation and ongoing training and socialisation.  Due to the needs and characteristics of the breed previous knowledge and experience of the breed or similar high-drive working breeds is required. Underneath all that energy is an incredibly sweet girl who loves affection and companionship. She will need a private secure garden.

Lyra has socialised well with other dogs, and is very giddy and playful with them.  We do feel she could potentially live with another dog of similar size and energy levels following a successful meet and greet. (must be neutered).

As she came into the home as a stray, we have no previous history on her so would prefer any children in the home to be 16+ years.

name: Elias
description:
Elias is a very sweet and friendly boy. He came into our care as a stray so we don’t have any background information on him. He has always been friendly with staff and volunteers whilst here. Elias can be a little strong on the lead due to his size so some basic lead training would be beneficial for him. We are looking for an active home for Elias as he has a lot of energy and would enjoy going on lots of adventures. Elias is a calm boy in his kennel and loves to have some down time with a tasty chew.

Elias is a friendly boy but due to his size we believe that it would be best for him to be rehomed with children over 14 years and over – Subject to a successful meet.

Elias needs a little more training around dogs since his castration as he has become a little unsure, therefore we believe that Elias would benefit from being the only dog in the home as he would prefer all the attention on him.

name: Jasper
description:
Jasper is an ex-racing greyhound that has spent all of his life in kennels. Jasper is now ready for a comfortable and cosy forever home to call his own. Jasper is a friendly and loveable boy who likes attention and a cuddle. Jasper has a high prey drive still so does pull when he sees ducks, birds and wildlife when out on walks. Jasper has never lived in a home before so he will need time to settle and get used to unfamiliar sounds and objects.

Jasper has interacted well with dogs and is currently paired with another greyhound so we believe that he can be rehomed with another dog of a similar size – Subject to a successful meet.

Jasper is a sweet boy so can potentially be rehomed with children who are 12 years and over – Subject to a successful meet.

name: Jax
description:
This stunning boy is Jax! we are looking for an experienced home for this fantastic lad.  He is a friendly and affectionate boy who absolutely loves attention and enjoys a good fuss.  He has a wonderful nature and is always happy to spend time with his people. This clever lad is exceptionally well behaved at the vets, taking examinations and handling in his stride, which is a testament to his temperament and trainability.  Like many dogs, he has his own little quirks – one of his favourites is enthusiastically ragging his blankets and rearranging them to his liking!  As a typical Belgian Malinois, he is highly intelligent, energetic and thrives on both physical exercise and mental stimulation.  He loves charging around our compound and would be happiest in a home where he has plenty of opportunities to stay active and engaged.  Because of his breed traits, he will need an owner who has previous experience with Belgian Malinois and understands their needs.  He is not a dog that will be content with a short walk around the block, he requires ongoing training, enrichment and a lifestyle that allows him to use both his body and brain.  He will need a private secure garden.

Jax was rehomed but sadly has been returned to us as his prey drive was too much for his new owners. He cannot be rehomed with cats or small furries.  He will need an owner that has previous experience with large breed high prey dogs.

He has socialised well with other dogs whilst in our care, so we feel he could possibly be rehomed with another dog (similar size) following a successful meet and greet.

As Jax came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on him so would prefer any children in the home to be 16+ years.

name: Sam
description:
Sam is a very loveable boy who just wants to give out hugs to everyone he meets, he does sometimes forget how big he is though. He’s a big hit with volunteers here and they all love taking him out for his walks as they get to have lots of cuddles. He can be strong on the lead though due to his size. He’s a very sweet boy who has a big heart and is looking for someone to show him lots of love! Sam has enjoyed his walks around the woods, watching the ducks and wildlife around him. Sam would appreciate an enclosed garden that he can spend his time in relaxing and enjoying the sun. Sam loves his treats, nothing is too big or small for him – he isn’t fussy!

Sam is super friendly with everyone he meets but due to his giddy jumpy nature we believe that it would be best to rehome Sam with children over the age of 16 – subject to a successful meet and greet.

Sam needs to be the only dog in the home, he can be vocal around dogs so needs a family that has experience to help build his confidence and manners.

If you think that you could provide a comfortable home with lots of treats for Sam please apply now!

name: Cali
description:
Cali was a very nervous girl when she first arrived at the home, which was over 200 days now! It has taken a lot of time for staff and volunteers to get to know Cali and bring out her excitable, bubbly personality. Cali loves going for walks and off lead runs in our compound area, she will always be found with a football in her mouth. She loves to dodge past you whilst you try and catch her, her tail never stops wagging. Cali loves her treats and sits nicely whilst you give them to her. She has been toilet trained whilst in our care, which is a bonus for when she goes home.

Cali can be strong on the lead at times due to her excitement to get outside and enjoy the fresh air but can walk nicely after her initial excitement is over, especially on a harness. Cali would love a fully enclosed garden with someone around most of the time so that she can come and go as she pleases. Cali spends most of her day relaxing on a comfy bed watching people come and go. She can be a little barky in her kennel at first but this is due to her wanting to say hello to everyone.

Cali isn’t a cuddly kind of girl but would love a family that is willing to keep her entertained and will play with her toys. We believe that Cali needs to be in an adult only home, with a family that has experience with rescue dogs or bull breeds.

Cali was nervous of dogs when she first came into our care so we think that it is best that she is the only dog in the house. With a lot of socialisation she now is a friendly girl that is happy to say hello to most dogs that she meets.

We think that it would be best for Cali to not be in a house with cats.

If you think you can give this gorgeous girl her forever home please apply!

name: Tails
description:
This stunning girl is Tails.  We are looking for a committed and knowledgeable home for her where she can truly thrive.  As a typical Husky she is full of energy and very intelligent so will need an owner who understands the unique needs of this incredible breed. She is very high energy and an independent thinker with a typical Husky stubborn streak. She will need a home that has an active lifestyle where she can have plenty of exercise, enrichment and ongoing training.  Tails has so much potential and will make a loyal, fun and rewarding companion in the right home.  We are looking for someone patient, understanding and ready to invest time into building a strong bond with her.

Tails has socialised well with other dogs whilst in our care so can potentially be rehomed with another dog of a similar temperament – subject to a successful meet.

As Tails came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on her, so we think it would be best for her to go to an adult only home.

name: Pearl
description:
This talkative girl is Pearl.  She is a very affectionate, confident and friendly girl that is always up for lots of fuss and strokes.  She can be very vocal when she wants your attention so probably not suitable for an apartment/flat.  She enjoys her walks everyday having a sniff about and saying hello to everyone she meets.  She is very strong on the lead so will need an experienced owner that is used to powerful dogs. Pearl would benefit from a private secure garden.

Pearl has socialised with other dogs whilst in our care, she can be a little unsure at first but does come around after a bit, so we feel she may be best suited as the only dog in the home where she can take her time getting used to other dogs with lots of positive reinforcement from her new adopter.

As Pearl came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on her so would prefer any children in the home to be 12+ years.

name: Willow
description:
This stunning girl is Willow.  Willow was very nervous and unsure for the first few weeks she was with us.  She was very vocal when the staff went in her kennel and would hide in the back.  The staff have worked hard with her to gain her trust and she has come out of her shell now and is showing her playful friendly side.  We are looking for an experienced owner for Willow that have had nervous large breed dogs previously and will work with her on her confidence, doing this at Willow’s pace and not too rushed.  She is a very independent girl who will come to you when she wants some attention, her toys are her number 1 priority in life.  Willow is very food orientated and will sit nicely for her treats.  This said she is a little bit chunky at the moment so is on weight management food to help her loose a few pounds, and well done to Willow and the staff as she has managed to lose 3kg up to now!  She will need continued training and socialisation. Willow will benefit from a private secure garden where she can have off lead time to relax and have a sniff about.

Willow has socialised ok with other dogs whilst in our care but we feel she would be best rehomed as the only dog in the home as she does prefer her own space.

As Willow came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on her so would prefer an adult only household.

name: Bruce
description:
Bruce is a very active and playful boy who absolutely loves chasing around our compound with his toys.  He can be quite boisterous and bouncy when he is excited so would definitely benefit from continued training and socialisation. He can be quite a strong boy on his lead too.

He will need an active home where he can get all the exercise and mental stimulation he will need every day. Bruce would benefit from a private secure garden where he can have off lead time with his toys in between his walks.

Bruce has interacted well with most dogs whilst in our care but can be very dominant with them so we feel he would be best suited to be the only dog in the home.  The new adopter will need to continue his socialisation with other dogs to improve his interactions with them.

As Bruce can get nervous and overwhelmed meeting new people, especially men, we feel that it would be best for him to go to an adult only home. He will need time to get to know you before going home. His new family will need to be able to commit to multiple meets.

Bruce is a wonderful, vibrant boy with lots of love to give to his new family! He has spent a while in kennels now so would love to find his forever home and someone to be the person to throw his ball endlessly! Do you think this could be you?

name: Dodger
description:
Energetic dog that will walk for hours, he is looking for an active home who’ll include him in all their adventures, Dodger is a young dog (2 years 9 months) and will benefit from a family who enjoy training, he can be strong on the lead, he knows sit, lie down. He loves his treats, he prefers to be with people, He’d be suited to older children who are not fazed by energetic, bouncy dogs secondary school age is preferable.

In the short time we have known Dodger, he appears to be very food motivated and picked up some training. Loves to destuff a fluffy toy, he is sharing his foster home with a cat, no concerns. They are not mixing with each other, yet in the same house. We feel Dodger could have dog walking friends as has been good when passing dogs on assessments. Pending successful meet at the centre Dodger could live with another neutered dog.

name: Pippin
description:
Pippin is a good boy who can live with children of upper secondary school ages and above. He also has the potential to live with all other pets, including dogs and a dog-savvy cat. As Pippin can be worried by strangers in his new home he would ideally have the ability to be separate from the front door and would be introduced to strangers outside of the door. Pippin is looking for a family that is happy to keep him on a lead when out and about and so would also love a home with a private, secure garden to run around in.

This dog is sure to make you feel merry - meet Pippin! He is our 2-year-old American Bulldog who has a whole lot of love to give to his new family. Pippin can be underconfident in new situations and around new people and so he would suit a loving and calm home who are happy to give this big softie lots of fuss and attention to help him to settle in. Once Pippin feels safe, he is a massive cuddle bug and will be your best friend for life.

name: James
description:
James is recently retired from the racing and ready to start the next chapter in his life. He has been really friendly with everyone here, so although we don’t have any history of him around children we think he’ll be fine to live with those of primary school age. James likes spending time with other dogs and could live with one as long as they get on well during meets in centre. James has a historic injury in his leg, and he is on some pain medication to help with this.

James is 3 years old and, as an ex-racer, we’re not sure whether he’s ever been in a home before. He might appreciate an introduction to some of the basics like housetraining and car travel. He does settle well in his kennel though, so hopefully shouldn’t mind being left home alone  for a little while once settled in.

name: Lucy
description:
Lucy is a bright, playful dog who forms strong bonds with people she trusts. She can be worried by new people and environments and so is looking for an adult only home to set her up for success. Lucy can live with another dog as long as they get on well together during meets in centre. She can be a bit of a scavenger when out and about and so wears a muzzle. A secure garden of her own is absolutely essential for Lucy, as she needs the direct access to a space where she can be outside off-lead and without her muzzle on. As you can see, Lucy does have cherry eye in both of her eyes, there is no further treatment required for this and all details will be discussed with any potential adopters.

Lucy, our 2yr old Rottweiler, is full of energy and charm and just loves to play! She has spent a couple of weeks in a home so may need some extra support with settling in, including things like housetraining and being left alone. Lucy really struggles with the car and will want a home where she can have quiet walks from the doorstep while she works on this. If you like to throw a tennis ball or play tuggy then Lucy will make firm friends with you in no time. You’ll know when she trusts you as this is when she will start to approach and ask for fuss too.

name: Sherbert
description:
Sherbert is looking for active adopters who want to take him on lots of adventures and do fun training with him. He has the potential to live with another, specific dog although can’t live with any other pets. Sherbert could live with older children but would need adopters who are around for most of the day initially.

Sherbert is a gorgeous, goofy boy who doesn’t always know his own strength! He is super friendly and loves a fuss once he knows you. Sherbert enjoys interacting with other dogs and being out & about—he has bags of potential and will flourish in the right home!

name: Saint
description:
Saint is a 5 year old Greyhound who has found himself with us after retiring from a racing career. He is as his name suggests, a total angel and he adores being made a fuss of! Saint is looking to have someone who can help him settle in to a home and spoil him rotten, as he deserves. As he has a high prey drive, we'd recommend keeping him on lead and muzzled in public spaces.

Saint is super happy and friendly and he loves to play chase, but he's still working on making fetch happen! This handsome chap enjoys walking with other dogs, and would be able to live with other dogs, as well as children of secondary school age. He has had some medical needs whilst in our care, which may be ongoing, but our veterinary team can discuss this in more detail. Our Animal Welfare licence number is AWE02, as licenced by Glasgow City Council.

name: Dahlia
description:
Wordsworth is a 7 year old Italian Greyhound and Dahlia is a 4 year old Lurcher. They are a bonded pair and are looking for a home together. They have been social when meeting other dogs at the Centre so have the potential to live with another dog pending meets at the centre. They are a friendly pair, Wordsworth can be nervous so a home where any children are of Older Primary School age and above, where the children can be understanding that he may find fast movements and loud noises worrying, would be best. Wordsworth & Dahlia would like access to a secure garden to play in and help with housetraining but they could cope if this were to be a communal space. Once settled, they would be ok to be left for short periods of time.

Wordsworth and Dahlia are a lovely leggy pair who love meeting new people, having fuss and going on interesting walks. They will make wonderful companions for their new family.

name: Priscilla
description:
Priscilla can live with upper primary aged children and other suitable dogs. She is house trained and has been good when left alone for a few hours. Priscilla has some pain in her hips and is currently on minor relief that she may need long term.

Little Priscilla finds herself in need of a new home as her owner could no longer care for her. She loves to lounge, especially outside if the sun is out, and is happy to explore and say hello to people. Priscilla is a playful girl and loves interacting with toys and her handlers at the same time. She's also great at making doggy friends and happily says hello to all breed and ages. She's such a sweet and happy little thing, we don't think her stay will be a long one.

name: Krypto
description:
Krypto is a 1 year old Crossbreed looking for an active home. He is a friendly boy and could join a home with children of Older Primary School age who are confident around big bouncy dogs. Krypto will need to be the only pet in the home as he is undersocialised around other dogs; he will need to be kept on lead when outside of the home and will benefit from ongoing training around other dogs to help built his confidence and socialising skills. Krypto is a high energy boy and would like access to his own secure garden to provide and easy, regular off lead outlet and space to run around and play, this will also be useful to settle him into his new home and assist with housetraining.

Krypto came into our care having been found as a stray. At 1yr old he is still very much a pup at heart and is looking for an active home that can help him learn new skills. He walks nicely on lead and knows “sit”. He will make a lovely addition to home that can give him the time and love he deserves.

name: Kenya
description:
Kenya is a 9 year old Neopolitan Mastiff crossbreed. She is a friendly girl who could join a home with children of Secondary School age and older and has the potential to live with another dog pending meets at the centre. Kenya has been on a weight loss programme since coming into our care and would benefit from having her own garden to help with this and provide easy toilet access as she is housetrained. She is people and dog friendly so could cope if this were a communal space. Once settled, leaving hours could be introduced.

Kenya is a gentle soul who came into our care having been found as a stray. She did not come into us in the best condition and has been receiving ongoing vet care for her skin and this may need to continue once in her new home. She has done a great job on her weight loss journey but still has a way to go to reach her ideal weight so her exercise levels will need to be built up gradually as she gets into shape. Kenya is a real sweetheart who has won the hearts of all the staff and volunteers at the Centre and we are all hoping we can help her find her furever family who can provide her with the love and care this angel deserves.
