name: Bailey
description:
Bailey is a handsome 2-year-old Dachshund who is looking for a calm, loving home where he can continue to build his confidence and feel safe in new surroundings. He loves people and enjoys spending time outdoors, although sudden loud noises can sometimes cause him to alarm bark. Bailey is currently enjoying life in his foster home, where he has settled in beautifully, often following his foster carers around and asking for cuddles. He is a very affectionate boy who loves human company and forms strong bonds with his favourite people. He also loves showing off his tricks, especially when there are a few tasty treats on offer! Bailey can be nervous when meeting other dogs, but he is friendly and could potentially share his home with a calm, well-matched canine companion following a successful introduction. Having shown some guarding behaviours in his previous home, we feel Bailey would be best suited to a household with secondary-school-aged children who can understand and respect his boundaries.

Bailey is looking for someone who can offer him patience, reassurance and plenty of affection as he continues to grow in confidence. He thrives on human companionship and would love a home where he can spend lots of quality time with his people. As he finds being left alone difficult, any time apart will need to be introduced very gradually, at a pace he is comfortable with. A calm, understanding home that can provide consistency, gentle encouragement and a predictable routine will help Bailey feel secure and flourish. In return, you can expect a loving little companion who enjoys cuddles, outdoor adventures and showing you just how clever he can be! Bailey has so much love to give and is ready to find his special someone who will help him feel safe, cherished and confident for the rest of his life.

name: Buddy
description:
Buddy is a 2 year old Collie cross. He is a friendly boy looking for an active home that can keep him mentally and physically occupied. Buddy has the potential to live with another dog pending successful meets at the centre. Any children in the home should be of older Secondary School age and above (14+) as he has been known to show some frustration related behaviours such as jumping up, humping and mouthing if overstimulated or frustrated. He is not suitable to live with cats or small furries. Buddy is a high energy boy and would like access to a secure garden to provide space for play, this could be communal. Buddy is not used to being left and will need someone with him most of the time initially, any leaving hours will need to be built up slowly once settled in the home

Buddy is a lovely boy who likes a fuss and enjoys his walks and opportunities to play. He is currently worried by car travel and will need direct access to walks from his new home without the need to travel in a car and will need his new family to continue his training around cars which he has been doing well with at the centre.

name: Randal
description:
Randal needs to live with another dog as he really enjoys their company and seeks reassurance from them. He can also live with older secondary school children. Randal is a very sensitive soul and needs exposure to the world gradually & at his pace once settled in.

Beautiful Randal is a very sweet boy and will often lean into you for a fuss. Randal loves food so would enjoy further training once settled into a home! He will need his leaving hours built up slowly as he is an ex racer, so home life will be very new to him.

name: Zephyr
description:
Zephyr's ideal home would be with a loving family who enjoy plenty of cuddles, companionship and little adventures together. As a slightly older dog, she would love a home that understands she may not manage long walks but still enjoy a gentle wander, exploring new places and sniffing all the wonderful smells along the way. A cosy home, comfy beds, lots of affection and a family who will cherish her would be perfect. Most of all, she's looking for a family to share life’s simple pleasures with, from peaceful strolls to snuggles on the sofa

She would be a wonderful addition to a loving family who enjoy affection, cuddles and spending time together. Although she may be a little shy at first, with patience, kindness and reassurance, she will grow in confidence and show her loving personality. She also enjoys having some quiet time to relax and recharge, alongside gentle adventures and exploring the world at her own pace. A family who understands her need for both companionship and calm, and who will give her the time and space to settle in, could be the perfect match for this lovely girl.

name: Freya
description:
Freya (1 yr old) and Archer (3 yrs old)  are the cutest, friendliest Beagle duo! They are the best of friends who love to play, run and sniff about exploring! Because of the strong bond they have we would ideally rehome them together. Freya and Archer could potentially live alongside cats and other small furies.

This sweet and social pair have the potential make wonderful family pets, they could live with children as long as parents kept in mind that Freya can sometimes be a little sensitive and worried during interactions. They do love human company, are really affectionate and would ideally live in a home where they are not left alone much.
If you’re looking for a fun and adorable duo to have a lifetime of adventures with then make sure to add Freya and Archer to your favourites!

name: Alice
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have been spayed & am ready for my forever home!

03-10-26 Alice has come to us from a breeder to find the loving forever home she deserves. She is a very sweet girl who is understandably feeling quite worried and overwhelmed to find herself here with us. Alice is nervous about being handled and when she becomes worried, she can start to shake. However, she is already beginning to learn that human hands can be kind and that she doesn't need to be afraid of gentle attention.

Alice will be looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and understand that she will need time, patience and reassurance as she learns to trust. Her new family will need to allow her to settle in at her own pace. We would consider a home with gentle, dog-savvy teenagers aged 13+.

Alice relies on other dogs for comfort and reassurance and having another kind and confident resident dog in her new home will be very important for her. A canine friend will help her to feel safe, settle into her new surroundings and hopefully give her the confidence to start coming out of her shell.

Alice has never lived in a home before, so everything about family life will be completely new to her. Her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she learns about home life and new skills like house training. She will also need to learn all about walking on a lead and harness, first by practicing around the garden.

Alice is a gentle and very sweet girl who is only just beginning to discover that people can be kind and that she is safe. With the right home, plenty of patience and a kind canine friend by her side, we hope she will slowly find her confidence and blossom into the happy little girl we know is hiding underneath her worries.

Alice has been given the Gift of Life by Emma Walsh

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Parker
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

Please be patient with me, I'm nervous and learning everything from scratch.

I will be neutered before finding my forever home!

01-10-26 Parker is a nervous boy who has come to us from a breeder. He is fine to handle but can be very unsure and will often try to hide away when he is approached. He is trying so hard to be brave, and we are sure that with the right person willing to take a chance on him, he will slowly learn that he has nothing to be afraid of.

Parker will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home and would benefit from adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and will allow him to settle in at his own pace. He will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in his new home who can take him under their wing and show him the ropes.

Parker has never lived in a home before, so his adopters will need to be kind and patient as he learns all about home life, including house training and walking on a lead. These things may take some time, and his adopters will need to understand that he will need to progress at his own pace without being rushed.

Parker is a nervous boy at the moment, but underneath that uncertainty is a lovely boy who is trying his very best. With time, patience and a loving home willing to give him a chance, we hope to see Parker blossom into the wonderful companion we know he can be.

Parker has been given the Gift of Life by Margaret Hunter

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Crispin
description:
I would like a calm and quiet home where I can settle in.

I could live with other dogs, or be the only dog. I don't mind. I don't mind cats!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I walk well on a lead and love being out and about!

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

Crispin originally came to us from a breeder last October. He was adopted for a few months but returned to our care after his adopters sadly realised they were not the right match for him. Although they gave him every opportunity to settle, Crispin remained very worried whenever the male in the household was home and struggled to relax in his company.

Since returning to us, Crispin has moved into foster and has settled beautifully. He is an incredibly loving, cuddly little boy who simply wants to be close to his people. While he can initially be worried by some men, his foster carer has found that once visitors give him some attention, he quickly relaxes and happily cuddles up with them. He does the same with female visitors. He has adult grandsons in his foster home and, after an initial bark, is very happy to settle down with them.

Crispin does get on with other dogs, but he can be quite keen to push his way in for attention and may grumble if another dog gets in the way. He is not aggressive and, having no teeth, cannot bite, but he would be best suited to either being an only dog or living with a very laid-back dog who is happy to share their space and attention. His foster carer feels he would particularly enjoy being the centre of his person's world, as he simply loves being with his human, male or female.

Crispin absolutely loves his walks and this is his favourite pastime. He gets wonderfully excited when it is time to go out and walks beautifully on both a lead and harness. He is sociable with other dogs he meets, enjoys exploring new places and travels well in the car. He particularly loves visiting the coffee shop and is happiest when he can be out and about with his people.

As Crispin has now experienced life in a home, he has settled well into a routine and sleeps soundly through the night. He has had the occasional wee indoors first thing in the morning, although this has been improving, so his adopters should continue his house training with patience and consistency.

Crispin forms incredibly strong bonds with his favourite people and loves to be close by and involved in everything they are doing. He showed signs of separation anxiety in his previous home when left for more than a couple of hours, so his ideal home would be one where someone is around for most of the day and any time alone can be built up gradually.

Crispin has a cataract in his right eye and is developing one in his left. Despite this, he gets around brilliantly and you would hardly know he has eyesight problems. He has also had all of his teeth removed and will need to remain on a soft diet for life. He has Grade 2 patella luxation in both hind legs, which may continue to improve with gentle exercise as

Crispin has a travel document, which says he is 7 years old, but we do feel he could potentially be a little older than this.

Crispin has been given the Gift of Life by Katrina Pirner

Crispin would love a one person, male or female, calm household where he can soak up all the attention from his special human. Although he gets on with all dogs outside of the home, he prefers to be cuddled up with his human wherever it may be.. sofa, bed he s not fussed as long as he knows they are close by him.

Crispin walks perfectly on a harness and lead and is good off lead too. He will walk ahead of you but keep coming back to 'check in' with you.

Crispin continues to thrive in his foster home and is loving this home life. He loves his food, loves his walks, loves his cuddles and just loves everything to be honest.

Although Crispin lives alongside his foster sisters, I do feel he would love a home with no other dogs and just a single active  adult home, male or female, where he can have all the attention and love. Cats are fine, as he dosen't take any notice of them.

Although his initial write states that he may be older than 7 I feel he is aged about right apart from his lack of teeth as he is full of energy and  fun.

Crispin is smashing this home life. He is an absolute gentleman and will make a perfect best friend for an active person who is at home most of the time.

This week he has visited various secure fields, visited coffee shops and even popped into a pub for a cool drink while out on a street walk. He loves to be out and about with his human and then return home for snuggles on the sofa.

Although Crispin has a cataract in his right eye this does not seem to affect him at all. His luxating patellas also don't seem to bother him and his movement is 100%.

Crispin recently moved foster homes through no fault of his own. He is a gorgeous, well mannered, cuddly boy who loves his walks, his humans and his food.

He gets along with the cats and dogs in my home, though initially Crispin demanded all the attention and would push the other dogs out of the way to get his cuddles first but with careful handling this has improved over the week.

He loves to cuddle up on my bed with my own dogs and sleeps all night there. He lives for his walks and gets very excited when his lead/harness appear. He can walk on his own or with another dog for company.

He happily shares his food bowl with his foster friend Lemon Pie. Even the cats dig in with him sometimes. He is getting used to being left when I go shopping and I am extending these trips so he gets used to being without humans for a while. Crispin does bark initially when visitors come into my home but this soon subsides when he realises they will do him no harm. Keep up the good work Crispin, you've got this my boy

Crispin has been back in foster care for a week and has settled in beautifully. He is an incredibly loving, cuddly little boy who simply wants to be loved. Sadly, he was returned because he became anxious and barked whenever the man in the household moved around.

He walks beautifully on a lead and harness, sleeps soundly through the night alongside the other foster dog, and travels well. Although he is perfectly happy living with other dogs, he could also be an only dog so he can enjoy all the cuddles and affection he deserves. He has had a few little accidents indoors first thing in the morning, but over the last few days he has settled into a much better routine.

Crispin has no teeth, so he will need to remain on a soft diet for the rest of his life. He also has a cataract in one eye and the beginnings of a cataract in the other, but you would hardly know he has any sight issues as he gets around so well.

He really is a very special little boy who simply needs a loving home where he can feel safe, secure, and cherished.

Crispin originally came to us from a breeder last October. He was adopted for a few months but has come back into our care after his adopters sadly realised they were not the right match for him. Although they gave him every opportunity to settle, Crispin remained very worried whenever the male in the household was home and simply couldn't relax in his company.Crispin is a dear little boy who can still be worried and unsure at times. It is clear that he had very little socialisation in the past, and although he has made lovely progress since living in a home, he still needs patient adopters who understand that building trust takes time. He can be touch-sensitive when he is feeling anxious, so gentle handling and allowing him to approach in his own time will help him continue to gain confidence.Crispin will be best suited to adopters who understand the needs of scared ex-breeding dogs and who will give him all the time he needs to settle at his own pace. He would be happy to share his home with another kind and confident resident dog in his new home. However, in the right home, with owners who are around enough to reassure him and who have experience with ex-breeding dogs, he could also be the only dog in the home.One thing Crispin has discovered is just how much he loves going for walks! He gets wonderfully excited when it's time to head out, twirling around and eagerly waiting by the front door. Once out, he walks beautifully on a lead, is very sociable with other dogs he meets, enjoys exploring new places, and travels well in the car. Walking has become one of his favourite activities and is a lovely way to watch his confidence shine through.As Crispin has now experienced life in a home, he has become familiar with many of the sights and sounds of everyday living. However, he hasn't quite mastered house training yet, so his adopters will need to continue helping him learn with patience, consistency, and plenty of encouragement.Crispin has also shown that he forms incredibly strong bonds with his favourite person. He loves to be close by and wants to be involved in everything they are doing. Because of this, he showed signs of separation anxiety in his previous home when left for more than a couple of hours. 25-09-26 Helga is a wonderful lady who originally came to us a while ago and was adopted into a loving home, where she spent several happy years. She is an outgoing lady that would love to go on plenty of quiet adventures where she can enjoy the outdoors in peace. However, she can also be a lazy lady, and would love a home where she can enjoy being a couch potato.

Helga can live with sensible, dog-savvy older teenagers aged 13+ who understand her needs and will treat her with kindness and respect. Having already lived in a home for several years, Helga understands the basics of home life and is house trained. However, her adopters should be prepared to give her a little patience and some gentle reminders while she settles back into a new routine. Moving home can be a big change, and we want Helga to have the time she needs to feel comfortable and secure again.

Helga is an amazing lady who has so much love to give. She does have some specific needs, but for the right person who understands her and is experienced with reactive dogs, she could be a wonderful companion. She just needs someone willing to look past her quirks, understand what makes her tick and give her the chance to find the right forever home.

name: Whispy
description:
I need a calm & quiet home, with adopters with experienced of scared ex-breeding dogs

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have not met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I haven't tried walks just yet and will find this a bit overwhelming at the moment.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have had 2 mammary lumps removed and 2 teeth extracted.

Whispy has come to us from a breeder and is a truly heartbreaking girl. When she first arrived, she was incredibly shut down and would bury her face into the wall in the hope that nobody would notice her. She would tremble when approached and could sometimes grumble or bark, but this has always come from a place of pure fear rather than aggression.

After spending a couple of weeks settling into her kennel routine, it is clear that Whispy has experienced very little kindness in her life. Her fears are deeply ingrained, and she has no understanding of what people's intentions are. When someone enters her kennel, she will often bark and grumble in panic because she is so frightened of what might happen next. Despite this, she allows gentle handling, strokes, and being picked up without any fuss, almost as though she has simply resigned herself to it. It is incredibly sad to see, and all she really needs is someone who will show her that people can be kind.

Whispy takes enormous comfort from other dogs and has formed lovely bonds with her two current kennel companions, who she happily shares everything with.She can be selective about the dogs she befriends and seems to prefer smaller, calm, gentle dogs rather than larger or more boisterous companions.Once she trusts another dog, they become an enormous source of reassurance, soshe will need at least one kind, quiet, confident resident dog in her forever home who can help her navigate the world and show her that life doesn't have to be so frightening.

Whispy is looking for a calm, adult-only home with adopters who have experience with very scared ex-breeding dogs and who understand that trust cannot be rushed.As she has never lived in a home before, she will need help learning everything from house training to settling into a routine. Walks are not something she is ready for at the moment, and her adopters must be prepared to let her progress entirely at her own pace. Gentle garden exploration will be much more appropriate until she feels safe enough to take the next steps.

Because Whispy is an older girl and her fears are so deeply rooted, she may never completely lose all of her worries or become the confident dog people often imagine. Her adopters will need to love and accept her exactly as she is, celebrating every tiny step forward without expecting her to become a different dog. For the right family, watching Whispy slowly learn to feel safe will be incredibly rewarding.

Whispy is a very special little lady who has spent far too much of her life living in fear. She deserves a safe place to call home, where she knows nobody will ever hurt or give up on her again. With endless patience, understanding, and unconditional love, we hope she can finally experience the peaceful and happy life she has always deserved.

She has had two mammary lumps removed at the time of her spay and has also had two teeth extracted.

Whispy has been given the Gift of Life by Alison Smith

I really wish I could say that since my last update, Whispy has made a lot of progress and is finally starting to realise that humans can be kind... but unfortunately, that’s not the reality.

Whispy is finding kennel life very difficult and is struggling massively with letting her guard down, even just a little bit. She still barks at me when I go in her kennel, she still runs away from me, she still won’t take treats from my hand... she basically still just wants to be left alone.

It’s so sad to see every day, but then I think of it from her perspective. Realistically, why would she trust me? When she’s spent 8 whole years not knowing kindness? It’s such a long amount of time to endure, so of course she’s not going to become a normal dog in just a few months.

I think this is something her future adopters will need to think about often. It’s probably not going to be a straightforward, easy road with Whispy, and there won’t be any cheat codes or miracles... as much as we’d want there to be. She simply just needs time, patience, and an abundance of understanding.

She needs somewhere she can finally feel safe, and I really hope it happens soon.

Whispy has been on my section for a couple of weeks now and oh my goodness is she a heartbreaker. I have no idea what she’s been through in her life, but her fears are deeply ingrained. She has no trust in anything or anyone, apart from a select few dogs at the rescue that she has dropped her guard with. She has absolutely no idea about human kindness, nor what our intentions are. She grumbles and barks when we enter her kennel in pure panic, as she’s so scared of what we’re going to do to her. Even though she may sound a little scary, she lets me stroke her and pick her up absolutely fine .. kind of like she’s just given up. It’s quite sad actually.Whispy currently has 2 kennel friends who she gets on well with and shares everything with. One is a Shih Tzu Cross and one is a Poodle Cross. I have tried quite a few dogs with her and it does seem as though she favours smaller dogs to larger ones. And definitely calmer, quieter ones that don’t get in her face.Whispy will need a very patient and understanding home with adopters who have experience with very scared dogs. Because she’s on the older side, she may never truly lose all of her worries and fears, and may never become a ‘normal’ dog, and this is something her adopters will need to be okay with, and love her and accept her anyway. Things such as going out for walks are not currently in the near future for Whipsy, and it’s going to take a lot of time and gentle guidance to ease her into such things.This poor, sweet girl does not deserve to live her life in fear and panic mode. She deserves to have a safe place to call her own, where she knows nobody is going to hurt her. She deserves to be loved unconditionally, and to not be given up on no matter what.

Whispy has come to us from a breeder and is a truly heartbreaking girl. When she first arrived, she was incredibly shut down, and would bury her face into the wall in the hope that nobody would notice her. She would tremble when approached and could sometimes be a little grumbly, but this was simply because she is so frightened and overwhelmed by her surroundings.

Since then, she has started to settle in and is trying so hard to be brave. She can be vocal with people and is still nervous to approach you but with patience and kind handling she has been joining in on yard times and taking treats, but she still has a ways to go. Whispy has never known the kindness of people so will retreat to a corner when she feels stressed.

Whispy will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and who are willing to give her all the time, patience and understanding she needs to settle and learn to trust.

She relies on other dogs for reassurance and so she will need at least one other confident, laid back resident dog in her new home who can take her under their wing and provide reassurance as she begins to build confidence. She can be selective over the dogs she enjoys spending time with however once she takes to a friend, she does so well with them and it boosts her confidence. She will need a very placid dog in the home who won’t worry when she is scared. She has had a few grumbles when meeting new dogs but she is just scared and needs time to develop a bond with them.

As she has never lived in a home before, Whispy will need kind and understanding adopters as she learns all about home life and new skills like house training. She doesn't yet walk on a lead and harness and this will be too overwhelming for her at the moment and once she is more comfortable she can begin learning in a secure garden until she feels brave enough to venture further.

Whispy is a very special lady looking for an equally special home. She has missed out on so much in her life and will need a home who will take things day by day with her and give her the support and love she’s so desperate for.

Nicole has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for her forever home. She was very scared when she first arrived and had clearly had little handling or socialisation, making human contact very worrying for her.

Nicole briefly moved into a foster home to learn about home life but returned to us following one incident where she became tangled in her lead and harness, panicked and nipped her fosterer. This was a single incident during a frightening experience, but adopters must understand that she can panic if she feels trapped or overwhelmed.

Nicole has now been back at the rescue for just over a month and is making lovely progress. She still doesn't like being picked up or handled, but is much better than she was and is increasingly comfortable spending time around people she trusts. She enjoys sitting in the play yard with her trusted people and responds brilliantly to treats, which are helping to build her confidence. She is a curious, cheeky little character who loves food, toys and snoozing in her bed, and she is even trying hard to be kennel clean.

Nicole loves other dogs and takes comfort from their presence, so she will need a kind and confident resident dog to help her feel secure and act as a role model.

She needs a calm, quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience of nervous ex-breeding dogs. As she has never successfully experienced home life, she will need patience with house training and learning the basics of being a pet. Lead and harness training will also need to be introduced very carefully because of her previous experience.

Nicole still has a long way to go, but her curiosity and wonderful personality are beginning to shine through. With the right home, canine companion and plenty of time and understanding, we hope she will continue to blossom.

Our vets noted a slightly unusual heart rhythm, and a heart scan showed mild valve changes. She currently requires no treatment and is expected to live a normal, happy life, although routine heart checks and monitoring for future symptoms are recommended. She has been treated for a ear infection.

Nicole has been given the Gift of Life by Shirley Bourne

Nicole has been back at the rescue with me for just over a month now, and even though she is still a scared lady, I can definitely see she has made progress. She still doesn’t like to be picked up and handled, but she’s a lot better with it now than she was when she first arrived. She’s also more content just being in my presence now and will happily hang out with me in the play yard with confidence. I spend a lot of time sitting on the floor with her and dishing out treats every so often to stay in her good books. She does love her food, so this helps massively with building some trust with her!

Nicole does still have a long way to go until she’s anywhere near being a ‘normal’ dog, but she has a lot of curiosity in her and definitely some Shih Tzu attitude as well, so I’m hoping she will blossom in the right home. If you have lots of time and patience, and a space in your heart and home to welcome a special lady, please consider Nicole. I promise you won’t regret it!

Nicole is the type of dog that can instantly put a smile on your face, even when she’s not doing anything. She has such a comical and infectious energy, and I really just love spending time with her. She loves snoozing in bed in her kennel through the day and playing with toys too. She even tries her hardest to be kennel clean!! She’s very easy to look after day to day. So please… give her a chance.

Nicole has been in foster for a week and is a sweetie. She has a wonderfully inquisitive nature and loves investigating everything around her, which makes us chuckle! She is still very nervous about being handled and will bark when she's feeling unsure, but she is already making progress. She now takes treats from us and absolutely loves her food. She is also mostly clean overnight.

Nicole has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for her forever home. She is a lovely little girl who is understandably feeling very scared and overwhelmed to find herself here. It’s clear she hasn’t had much handling or socialisation before, so human hands are quite worrying for her at the moment, but we will continue gently helping her learn that hands can be kind.

Nicole will be looking for a calm and quiet adult only home where she can settle in at her own pace. She would really benefit from adopters who have experience with nervous ex-breeding dogs and who understand the patience, time and reassurance she will need as she learns to trust.

She loves other dogs and takes great comfort from their presence, so Nicole will need another kind and confident resident dog in her new home to take her under their wing and help her feel safe and secure.

As Nicole has never lived in a home before, she will need patient adopters who are ready to help her learn everything about home life from the very beginning. She will need to learn new skills like house training and will also need to learn all about walking on a lead and harness.

With time, kindness and plenty of TLC, Nicole will begin to grow in confidence and let her personality shine.

Our vets have noted that Nicole has a slightly unusual heart rhythm, so she underwent a heart scan at our vets which showed some mild valve changes. At this stage she does not require any treatment and is expected to live a normal, happy life, although we would recommend routine heart checks and monitoring for any future symptoms.

name: Alice
description:
I need a home that can understand me and provide me with plenty of TLC.

I'd like to live with a resident dog my size and I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I have been spayed, please read below for more information!

12-10-26 Alice originally came to us from a breeder a few months ago, she was adopted but sadly she struggled to settle into the home and would chose to stay in her crate and wouldn't move freely around the home and so her adopters made the decision to return her to our care after a short adoption. She went straight into a foster home and has now spent two months there settling in.

Alice's foster family have worked patiently to help her build confidence at her own pace. A comfortable dog bed was gradually moved into the busier areas of the house, allowing Alice to become accustomed to everyday family life while still having a safe space of her own.

Initially, Alice found it difficult to remain in a room if her fosterer moved or walked past her. This has improved enormously, and she will now often stay in the room, even when people move around her. In the evenings, she is relaxed enough to settle with the family while they watch television.

Within the home she continues to be “hand shy” unless initiated by herself which is usually a quick lick of your hand.

Out on walks, Alice is an absolute superstar! The moment she sees her lead, she transforms into an excited, happy girl, wagging her tail in anticipation. She is a pleasure to walk alongside her three canine companions, and this is where her confidence and loving nature really shine. When outside on her lead she allows gentle cuddles, takes treats from your hand and is increasingly able to relax and enjoy the world around her. She needs two walks a day to allow for this interaction time.

Alice would love a calm, patient home with one friendly dog of a similar size to help her feel secure and with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs. She has shown a particular preference for the Labrador in her foster home, whose companionship she clearly enjoys.

Alice sometimes chooses to sleep away from her fosterers upstairs, but she has a charming way of persuading another dog to settle nearby in the hallway on their beds. Her need for canine companionship is clear, and having a trusted dog friend appears to bring her comfort.

Alice is not looking for a home where everything has to happen at once. She needs a family willing to give her time, reassurance and the freedom to grow in confidence without pressure. She also needs the companionship of another suitable dog and a home where her family are available for regular, gentle interaction throughout the day.

Alice has a continuing journey of discovering trust and the joy that comes with it .

Alice arrived with a cyst on her last mammary gland, which was drained during her spay surgery.

Alice has been given the Gift of Life by Carol Unsworth

name: Chewwie
description:
I’d like a quiet home filled with love and kindness!

I would like a home with a female dog medium size or larger. I am fine with cats.

I will need a secure garden with minimum 6ft fencing.

I'm new to lead walking and need some practice!

I have lived in a home so I know the basics.

I have been neutered and have had 2 teeth removed!

Chewwie originally came to us from a breeder to find his forever home. He was lucky enough to be adopted, but sadly, despite being very loved, it became clear that the home wasn't quite the right match for him and he has now returned to our care to begin his search once again. Chewwie was very worried of the adult sons in the home and also wasn't a great match with the smaller resident dog.

Chewwie is a sensitive boy who had experienced very little before coming into rescue and can find unfamiliar situations overwhelming. In his previous home, he formed a very close bond with his female adopter and absolutely adored her, but remained worried around the adult sons in the household. For this reason, he is looking for a calm and quiet home with patient adopters who have experience of nervous ex-breeding dogs and who will allow him all the time he needs to settle and build trust.

Since returning to our care, however, Chewwie has been an absolute pleasure. From the day he came back, he has been nothing but gentle, loving and affectionate with everyone here. Despite being returned because he was said to be nervous, we have seen a completely different side to him in kennels. He happily bounces over to greet us, is always looking for a fuss, and simply loves being around people. His affectionate nature shines through every day, and he has reminded us just what a special boy he is.

Although he had never lived in a home before his adoption, Chewwie adapted beautifully to family life. He was house trained and thoroughly enjoyed all the comforts of home, especially curling up in his cosy beds. He did find being left alone quite worrying, so his new adopters will need to be around for most of the time initially and gradually build up any time spent alone as his confidence grows.

Chewwie will need another kind and confident resident dog in his new home to help reassure him and show him the ropes, but this dog will need to be female and cocker spaniel sized or larger. He previously shared his home with a cat and happily ignored them, so he could potentially live with a dog-savvy cat.

Since being adopted, Chewwie has learnt to walk nicely on a lead and now really enjoys his walks, although he can still be worried in unfamiliar places and will benefit from ongoing encouragement as his confidence continues to grow.

Once Chewwie knows you, he is an incredibly loving and affectionate companion with a wonderfully cheeky personality. He loves playing with other dogs and is especially fond of his kennel friend. He's also a total water baby and absolutely loves splashing around in the paddling pool, making the most of every opportunity for fun. Like many mischievous youngsters, he has also been known to pinch things he shouldn't! His adopters will need to keep a close eye on shoes and other tempting items, as he developed quite a fondness for chewing shoes in his previous home. He especially enjoys hard toys, while softer toys and enrichment items should be supervised as he can quickly chew through them.

Chewwie is a truly special boy who has so much love to give. His return to rescue has shown us just how affectionate, gentle and resilient he is, and we know that in the right home he will continue to flourish. In return, his lucky adopters will gain a devoted, fun-loving and wonderfully cheeky companion who will fill their days with smiles.

When Chewwie first arrived, he had a lick granuloma on his front leg, which healed well. Following his return to the rescue, he began limping on the same leg and holding it up. X-rays at a local veterinary practice showed no abnormalities or injuries, so it is thought to be a soft tissue injury which should continue to improve. His adopters and their own vet should continue to monitor this as a precaution. He has had 8 teeth removed.

Chewwie has been given the Gift of Life by Paula Elliot

Chewwie is probably the cheekiest boy on my section, and oh, how I love working with him every day. If he’s not booping his nose on my bum, he’s stealing my work folder, the treats, or anything else he can find!

He’s a big, loveable cloud, and once he trusts you, that bond is built forever. He can still be nervous of new people, but if you have treats, then he’s more than happy to take them from you, which is a huge step forward!

Anyone who takes Chewwie home is going to have a life full of laughter because this boy will definitely keep you occupied!

Chewwie is an absolute angel. From the day he arrived on my section, he's been nothing but gentle, loving, affectionate, and just a truly special soul.

Despite being returned because he was said to be nervous, I honestly haven't seen that side of him. With me, he's all about cuddles and attention. He'll happily bounce over to say hello and is always looking for affection. He's also got a cheeky side that keeps me smiling. If you leave your folder, phone, or radio lying around for even a second, don't be surprised if Chewwie decides it's his now!

He's a total water baby and absolutely loves splashing around in the pool with his kennel friend. Watching him let loose, have fun, and just be a dog is one of my favourite things. He also loves heading down to the big yard where he can have a good sniff, stretch his legs, and enjoy himself.

Chewwie really is such an amazing dog, and I feel so lucky to know him. Looking after him has been an absolute privilege.

Chewwie is a sensitive and nervous boy who had experienced very little before coming into rescue and still finds new situations quite overwhelming. In his previous home, he formed a very close bond with his female adopter and absolutely adored her, but he remained worried around men and struggled to relax around the adult sons in the household. He will therefore be looking for a calm and quiet home with patient adopters who have experience of scared ex-breeding dogs and who will allow him all the time he needs to settle and build trust.

Although he had never lived in a home before his adoption, Chewwie adapted beautifully to home life. He was house trained and thoroughly enjoyed all the comforts that a home has to offer, especially his cosy beds! He did find being left alone quite worrying, so his new adopters will need to be around for most of the time initially and slowly build up the amount of time he is left as his confidence grows.

Chewwie will need another kind and confident resident dog in his new home to help reassure him and show him the ropes, but this dog will need to be medium size or larger. He previously shared his home with a cat and happily ignored them, so he could potentially live with a dog savvy cat.

Since being adopted, Chewwie has also learnt how to walk on a lead and now enjoys his walks, although he can still be worried in unfamiliar places and will need ongoing support and encouragement as he continues to gain confidence.

Once Chewwie gets to know you, he is an incredibly loving and affectionate boy who adores a fuss and cuddle. He has a wonderfully cheeky personality and loves to play with other dogs. He is also a bit of a mischievous boy and has been known to pinch things he shouldn't! His adopters will need to keep a close eye on shoes and other tempting items, as we are told he developed quite a fondness for chewing shoes in his previous home. He especially loves hard toys, but softer toys and enrichment items will need to be supervised as he can quickly chew through them.

Chewwie is a truly special boy who has so much love to give. In the right home he will start to come out of his shell and truly flourish. In return, his lucky adopters will gain a devoted, affectionate and wonderfully cheeky friend who will make them smile every day.

When Chewwie first arrived he had a lick granuloma on his front leg, which healed well. When he returned to the rescue he was limping on his front leg and holding it up, we took him to a local vets for an x-ray and no abnormalities or injuries were found, so it's possible that it is a soft tissue injury which should start to feel better soon, but this is something his adopters and their vet will need to monitor.

name: Tinkerbell
description:
I need an adult-only home with ex-breeder experience that can show me love.

I need a resident dog to help me feel safe but I haven’t met cats yet so I'm not sure

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I am learning to walk on a harness but may need more time as I heal.

Please be patient with me, I'm nervous and learning everything from scratch.

I have been spayed and am ready for my forever home.

Tinkerbell has come to us from a breeder and has now settling nicely into foster. She is an extremely hand-shy little girl who is still finding the world a very scary place and will run away and hide in the smallest of spaces when she feels worried. Her new family will need to be prepared to make adjustments around the home to ensure she stays safe while she learns to feel more comfortable. Although she still has a long way to go, Tinkerbell is beginning to show more interest in where her foster family are and what they are doing, which is a lovely little step forward for this precious girl.

Tinkerbell loves her food and treats, although she isn't quite ready to take them from your hand just yet. She gets on wonderfully with the other dogs in her foster home and is also happy to share her space with cats. Having a kind and confident resident dog will be very important for Tinkerbell, as she will need a canine friend to help guide her and give her reassurance as she learns about home life.

Tinkerbell has never lived in a home before, so everything is completely new to her. House training is still ongoing, and her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she gradually learns all the usual household routines. She will need a very experienced, adult-only home with people who understand extremely worried ex-breeding dogs and appreciate that building trust will be a long journey. She is not yet a little dog who is ready to enjoy lots of handling and cuddles, so her family will need to let her settle at her own pace without putting pressure on her.

Tinkerbell will also need regular grooming to keep her coat comfortable, and her adopters must be prepared to continue this patiently with an experienced and understanding groomer. She has already made progress during her time with us, and we hope that, with the right support, she will continue to discover that life can be a safe and happy place.

Tinkerbell is a truly special little girl who deserves someone willing to see her potential and give her the time she needs to blossom. She will need a very special forever home, but with patience, understanding and a kind canine companion by her side, we hope she will gradually grow in confidence and become the wonderful companion we know she can be.

We've had this little girl with us for nearly a month now and it's clear to see that she's going to need a special forever home with someone who understands that it's going to be a long journey to get this little darling to become the dog we now she can become.

At the moment she's still extremely handsome shy and will run away and hide in the smallest of places which will mean adjusting your house around for her safety. So far in foster Tinkerbell is starting to show interest in where you are and what your up to. She love her food and treats although she won't take them from your hand just yet she gets on great with all our other dogs and doesn't mind the cats either. Bearing in mind she's never been in a home before so everything is new to her so toilet training is ongoing.

Potential adopters will also need to be aware of grooming needs

In the past month I’ve seen more progress in Tinkerbell than ever, and it makes me sooooo happy and proud!!! A little while ago, out of nowhere, she jumped up onto the bench next to me and then quickly jumped back down. It was as if she was thinking “oh gosh, what did I just do!?” … but then she kept doing it again, and again. And now it’s like a little ritual that we have! I eat my lunch with her kennel in the yard nearly every day and because she’s so foodie, she jumps up next to me and waits to see what I have to share. It may or may not be the favourite part of my days!

Another big step for Tinkerbell is that we’ve moved forward with her harness training. I’ve started attaching a lead to it when she’s in the play yard so it trails behind her. A lot of scared dogs get freaked out by this, but it doesn’t seem to bother Tinks at all. I have attempted to pick the lead up twice to essentially ‘walk’ her, and she did panic at the tension, so I’m going to have to ease into it slowly. With dogs as frightened as Tinks, harness training is a huge step, so in my opinion it doesn’t matter how long it takes to get there. What matters is how we get there … slowly, gently, kindly.The last “win” in the past month came a couple of weeks ago. I picked her up in the back of the kennel to put her harness on (which she is not a fan of), and I put her down on my lap to make it easier for me to clip it up. For the first time ever, she just stayed put. She stayed sitting on my lap for about 2 or 3 minutes while I gently stroked her, not holding her in any way - she chose to stay. This made me SO happy and it was such a lovely moment to share with her.Tinks may still be against human touch, but the progress she’s made since her arrival is quite incredible. She really needs someone to take a chance on her now. She deserves it so much.

This week at the rescue we’ve had a big heatwave which resulted in a lot of our dogs needing to be shaved, including my beautiful Tinkerbell as she started to struggle having quite a thick coat. She has the most beautiful fur and she keeps herself so clean and dry, but it had to come off for her comfort. She was taken into the vets to be sedated again, but only because the weather has been so warm.. it would have been too hot to put her through the stress of shaving her all off with no sedation. I have been taking her into the grooming room regularly to brush her and trim the hair around her eyes, and she does definitely get better and better each time, so this is a good sign!! The next time she’s due a shave, I will try again without taking her into the vets to see how she does.

Even though Tinks is still a nervous girl, especially around people she doesn’t know, she is still progressing slowly and steadily. She’s still very reliant on other dogs and tends to copy them a lot of the time, so this has been good for her learning to trust me. She’s watched so many other dogs come up to me for a fuss, take treats from me, and just be comfortable in general being around me, and she is following suit.. just at her own pace. And that’s okay!

She is SUCH a sweet girl who has clearly been through a lot, and it’s not her fault she has such a strong guard up. I absolutely adore working with her and I understand and accept her for who she is. Seeing her get excited over toys and treats, and greeting me with a waggy tail in the mornings really makes me smile, and it gives me hope for her future. She deserves adopters who will love and cherish her the way she always should have been, regardless of if the feelings are mutual.. but I do think she is capable of loving and trusting.. she just needs to find herself with the right people.

Over the last few weeks, our lovely Tinks has reached a huge milestone. After seeing how well she has been progressing with her handling, we felt it was time to take the next step — harness training.

For a dog who finds handling so worrying, we knew there was a strong chance she might not accept wearing a harness. But unless we try, we’ll never know.

Tinks’ other kennel mummy and I took her into the grooming room, where we carefully introduced and fitted her harness. As expected, she was a little unsure and understandably a bit overwhelmed, but she made us both incredibly proud with how she coped. The next step was returning her to her kennel to see how she would manage wearing it throughout the day. Many of our more worried dogs will freeze or refuse to move in this situation, but not our Tinks. She carried on with her day as normal, moving around comfortably with the harness on.

To some, this might not seem like a huge achievement, but for Tinkerbell, it is a massive step in the right direction. Over the coming weeks, we will continue to build on this by practicing daily, with the hope that we can eventually begin introducing a lead in the yard.

With a dog like Tinkerbell, progress takes time, patience, and understanding. Thankfully, she has all of that in abundance, and we will never give up on her.

Tinkerbell has settled into my routine at the rescue beautifully now, so I’m finally starting to see glimpses of the real her. Her guard is definitely still up, but it has dropped slightly and I can tell she’s a lot more comfortable being around me than she used to be. She still won’t allow me to touch her and will bolt away if I go towards her, but she’s approaching me to sniff my fingers, sometimes give me kisses, and taking treats from me every single day now. She also feels content enough to lay near me when I’m sat in the yard eating my lunch, often with her back towards me which I guess is a sign that she does trust me!

One thing she has improved massively with is being picked up. I mentioned in my last update I still had to use a thick blanket and she would still sometimes try to bite (just not as often), but that’s even better again now. This week I was able to pick her up with no blanket, which is HUGE for Tinks!!

Because of how much better she had gotten, I thought I would attempt a full groom - going into it with absolutely no expectations. She allowed me to shave her back, but that’s as far as we could get. She started to get more and more stressed and I really didn’t want to push her and ruin the work we’ve done, so I took her into the vets so she could be sedated to complete the groom. So, she’s now shaved (minus her INCREDIBLE eyelashes), and I think she looks absolutely beautiful. Now that we’ve started fresh with her coat, I’m going to start taking her into the grooming room just once a week or so, and gently brush her etc to get her more used to it all.

Tinkerbell has made slow and steady progress since she’s been on my section and I’m so proud of how brave she’s trying to be. I can tell she wants to come out of her shell a bit more and join in with the rest of the dogs, but she’s not there just quite yet. Something big did happen last week though!! During dinner time I was hand feeding one of her friends, and Tinks came over and started licking the food off my hand for the first time!!!! I was absolutely over the moon and so happy that she felt comfortable enough to do that. Since then she’s done it nearly every day and has also started to take treats from me too if they’re yummy enough. I know this probably won’t sound like a lot to most people, but for a dog like Tinberbell it’s huge. For me, taking food from my hand is usually the first step in earning trust with my scared dogs, so I think we’re heading in the right direction.

We have also made a small amount of progress with Tinkerbell’s fear of being picked up. She still doesn’t like it - at all - but she’s not panicking as much any more and definitely doesn’t try to bite me as much as she did before. I still have to use a thick blanket and be very slow and calm with her, but I think she is starting to slowly realise that I’m not going to hurt her. I trimmed her fringe again a few days ago as her hair seems to grow quite quickly, so I took this opportunity to stroke her head gently for a little while once I was done. She actually started to close her eyes after a minute or so and I think she may have been enjoying it, or at least I hope she was.I adore this little lady and I’m going to do everything I can to show her what love and kindness is. I just hope a special someone will come along and feel the same way about her soon.

Tinkerbell has recently been moved to my section, as she struggles a great deal with being touched and handled by us humans. At present, she goes into complete panic mode whenever I go to pick her up, and she will try to bite to protect herself. This doesn’t mean she’s a nasty dog at all; she’s literally just so scared she will do anything she can to stop it happening. Once I have her comfortably in my arms, she will actually settle really well and will allow me to do things such as give her a gentle fuss and trim the hair on her face. I think the initial picking up is what scares her the most so this is what we’ll work on slowly together.

Tinkerbell is going to need a very experienced home with people who have had terrified dogs before. She’s going to need a lot of work and TLC put into her, and also a lot of understanding. Her adopters will need to accept the fact that she may never be a normal dog, and she may never be a dog who wants fusses or cuddles, but love her anyway. She’s a very special girl, and she needs a home equally as special to help her and give her what she needs.

I’m going to work as closely as I can with her over the next couple of weeks, and hopefully I can earn her trust and prove to her that she doesn’t need to be afraid of me. I’ll keep you all updated!

Tinkerbell has come to us from a breeder and can be a little unsure at first. She is touch-sensitive and may need time to feel comfortable, but once she calms down, she begins to show her gentle, sweet side. Tinkerbell will need an adult-only home that can handle her sassy personality and provide the patience she needs to settle in at her own pace.

She will also need a kind and confident resident dog to guide her and take her under their wing as she adjusts. Tinkerbell is looking for someone to teach her about trust, companionship, and the joys of home life.

As she has never lived in a home before, her adopters will need to be gentle and understanding while she learns about house training and walking on a lead. Starting with a few gentle garden sniffs will be perfect for her confidence as she begins to explore her new world.

Tinkerbell is a little gem who, with time and love, will grow into a devoted and affectionate companion.
