name: Royal
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I would like to live with a female dog. No cats please!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I can walk on a lead and harness and love to explore quiet areas.

I am learning about house training in my foster home, and am doing so good!

Royal is a very special Chow Chow who has come to us from a breeder in search of his forever home. When he first arrived, he was extremely frightened of the world around him and was very wary of being touched or handled. Thanks to gentle care and patience, Royal has made incredible progress and is continuing to blossom in foster, where he is experiencing home life for the very first time.

Royal has exceeded all expectations with how well he has settled into foster. He has been an absolute superstar, sleeping soundly through the night, travelling well in the car, walking beautifully on lead and has even been completely clean in the house. Every day brings a new milestone, and it has been a joy to watch his confidence grow as he discovers all the comforts and pleasures of family life.

Although Royal is still nervous of people initially, he so desperately wants to trust and tries his hardest to be brave. He has begun asking his foster carers for gentle neck and bum scratches, happily takes treats from their hands, enjoys rummaging through the toy box, has found his little voice and now greets them with his wonderful wagging tail. He is such a sweet, gentle soul who simply needs time to work things out at his own pace.

Royal absolutely relies on the resident female dogs in foster for confidence and reassurance. He watches their every move, learning how to be part of a family, and loves playing alongside them. He will need to share his forever home with at least one kind, confident female dog who enjoys a good play and can continue to show him the way. He cannot live with cats.

As this is Royal's first experience of living in a home, he thrives on routine and will need patient, understanding adopters who will allow him to settle without pressure. He has made remarkable progress already, but he is still very nervous of the unknown and benefits from people who understand that he needs time to process new experiences. A calm, rural or quiet home would suit him best, as he is currently worried by traffic. He is looking for an adult-only home with breed experience and experience with very nervous rescue dogs would be highly beneficial.

Royal has recently had a bath and full groom at the rescue and was an absolute gentleman throughout. As a Chow Chow, his beautiful coat will require regular daily grooming. He is very tolerant of being brushed when it is introduced slowly, little and often, and this has become an important part of his routine.

Royal is an incredibly special boy who has embraced this new chapter in his life with quiet bravery. With patience, kindness and the continued support of confident canine companions, he will become a wonderfully loyal and loving companion. Watching him continue to discover the world and grow in confidence will be an incredibly rewarding journey, and he is sure to make his forever family smile every single day.

Royal is currently being treated for an ear infection.

Wow! This darling boy has just exceeded all expectations with how well he’s settled into his very first home, in his first week. Not a single accident (unheard of for a boy), sleeps soundly over night out of a crate, happy to be left alone with the company of the resident dogs, walks well on a lead, travels well. A literal angel boy.

Royal is the sweetest soul, he doesn’t trust humans easily but he really wants to and tries so hard to be brave.

He relies heavily on our resident girl gang for confidence & reassurance, watching & copying them intently to learn what being a member of a family is all about.

After an initial overwhelming few days for him, every day now brings a new ‘first’ & burst of joy on our part! Asking for a neck / bum scratch, taking a treat from our hand, rummaging in the toy box, playing with the girls, finding his little voice & wagging his amazing tail when we talk to him. He is just loving this next step in life and is so ready to be someone’s special boy.

Royal currently needs an adult only home as has not yet been tested with children. He needs confident kind resident female dogs who like a good play. A rural / quiet location would be preferable as he’s currently quite scared of traffic.

He is still very nervous of the unknown, thrives on routine and needs to be guided and given time to work things out without any pressure so experience with very scared dogs would be helpful.

As a Chow, his beautiful coat will need grooming daily. He is very tolerant of this if done slowly, little & often.

Please get in touch if you feel you might be the right match for this special big guy, he will make you smile every day.

Royal is not a dog I’ve had the chance to work with until recently. I’ve heard a lot about him, as he’s one of our longer stayers. I had heard many great things from other members of staff, including the incredible progress he’s made since joining us!When I did get the chance to work with him, my first impression was “oh my days, you are beautiful!” On first sight, he is one of the most beautiful dogs I’ve ever seen and certainly the most stunning chow I’ve ever seen! How can you look at this handsome boy and not fall in love?!When I actually began working with him, I realised how shy and timid he actually was. Initially, he wouldn’t come to the front of the kennel to see me, he’d hide away in the back. It was evident to me that this boy did not trust me. As I continued to work with him, I was very aware of my actions, to ensure I wasn’t causing any anxiety. I began with treats (who doesn’t love a cheeky bribe?). It slowly worked. Initially, he wanted nothing to do with me. I didn’t want to invade his safe spaces (safe spaces are so important for a more scared or anxious dog. Could you imagine a big scary stranger coming into your home and not leaving? I wouldn’t feel too easy if that occurred to me). So, I’d place the treat and leave the kennel. He’d come out, have a little nosey and take the treat. With time, he began slowly coming out of the back as I entered his kennel. He then began taking treats from my hands and now, whenever I walk onto the section, he comes straight to the gate and waits for me. Honestly, such an incredible feeling making a bond like this with such an incredible boy! There is honestly no feeling like it. They say a dog is a humans best friend but, what no one tells you it works both ways. To build that bond, teach him that I’m not scary, I’m here to help him feel safe, comfortable, happy and to get such a response… it’s honestly the best feeling in the world. Royal needs a home, he needs people to show him this on a day to day basis. We do what we can but, we can’t teach him the safety and comfort of a home, of a family that’s there for him 24/7.Once I got to know this guy a little more, I was taken away. We go out on walks. I feel like this was another bonding experience for us. He loves a walk but, loud noises and interactions with loud people/dogs do freak him out, thus we try to go for quieter walks. He also loves frolicking in the yard. From my experience, he seems to just love being outside!When I worked with him, he didn’t have a friend in his kennel, however, since working with him I have seen him enjoying in the yard with other dogs and is now kennelled with a boxer. He seems very happy. As previously mentioned on his profile, he is to be homed with females around his size or alone. I have not worked with him enough to comment further on his compatibility and amiability with other dogs so, please read the rest of his profile and updates to get a fuller understanding of this incredible boy!At this point, I’ve worked with him enough for him to trust me. He’s happy to see me, he’s fine for me to touch him and fuss him. The Royal I see is a happy dude. He is a scared dog, I’m very aware of that but, the Royal I know now is far different to the Royal I first met. You just have to gain his trust and he’ll let you see him. When you first meet him, he will be shy. He’ll hide and he will not trust you. DO NOT let this deter you. He is one of the sweetest dogs I’ve ever met. From when I first met him to now, I feel like he’s a completely different dog. I was respectful of his boundaries, slow and calm, I did what I could to make him feel comfortable and safe, he then began to trust me and show me his true self (he hides it beneath all that fur). Honestly, I love him. I will take time out of my day to go see him, give him a little treat and some love, just because he is honestly that special. I cannot believe he’s been here over a year. He is one of our most special dogs. I don’t see how anyone can get to know this dog and not love him.Don’t overlook this fluffy dude. Yes, he’s shy and nervous but, the longer you spend with him, care for him and gain his trust, the more you’ll fall in love with him. I can say with confidence; if you put the effort in with Royal, you will fall in love with him.

I absolutely love this boy with my whole heart.

I've been working hard on helping him get used to being brushed because, as a Chow, it's something his future adopters will need to keep up with regularly to keep his coat healthy and prevent mats from developing, especially behind his ears.

Royal is now an absolute angel when it comes to grooming. I brush him every day, and with it being shedding season, no matter how long I brush for, there always seems to be more fur coming out! These days, he simply finds a comfy spot, settles down, and lets me get on with it. If he's had enough, or if I come across a mat that's uncomfortable for him, he communicates so well to let me know he's done for the day.

I also recently decided it was time to give him a bath. I wasn't sure how he'd cope, as it involved picking him up and putting him in the bath, but he was an absolute angel from start to finish. He allowed me to pick him up without any fuss and stood beautifully while I bathed and shampooed him.

I'm so incredibly proud of him. Afterwards, I introduced him to the grooming blower to help remove some of his loose coat. He wasn't a huge fan of it, but he tolerated it for a short while, and I'll continue using it regularly so he can build his confidence with it.

I honestly think all this grooming time has strengthened our bond even more, because lately he seems to be seeking out so much more affection and attention from me. He's such a special boy, and it has been wonderful watching his confidence grow.

Royal has now been with us for over a year, and we’re still waiting for the right person to see just how special he is. He’s had two meet and greets during this time, but sadly neither worked out as he was too nervous meeting new families.

Royal is a sensitive boy who simply needs time, patience, and understanding. He can be unsure at first, but once he begins to trust you, his cheeky, affectionate personality really shines through and it’s such a joy to see.

With a consistent routine, Royal truly thrives. He now enjoys running freely around our large yard without a harness or lead, and when it’s time to go back, he comes straight over. He’s also been out on two longer walks away from the rescue with one of our regular volunteers and has done amazingly well.

All Royal is looking for is someone willing to give him the time and patience he deserves. In return, he’ll become a loyal and loving companion.

I’ve come on leaps and bounds over the past month. I’m still a little shy and can get nervous when I meet new people, but I’m working on it!

I feel most comfortable when I spend quality time with people. It doesn’t take long for me to start feeling at ease (though I still sometimes like my own space). The more time you spend with me, the more comfortable I become—and treats help too! I’ll return your love in equal measure, as long as I’m given the right time, support, and respect.

I love going out for walks, though I can get nervous around loud noises or sudden movements. They might make me jump or feel uneasy, but a bit of love and reassurance always helps!

I feel more comfortable every day. I benefit not only from interaction with my humans, but also from the company of my kennel friends that I live with.

Another month has gone by, and my cheeky boy Royal is still waiting in kennels. I honestly don’t know why this handsome lad isn’t getting much interest. Not only is he completely unique-looking, but he also has the funniest, quirkiest personality. If you want a dog who’ll make you laugh every single day here he is!

Royal is 99% kennel clean and always keeps his bedding tidy… well, until I make his bed perfectly for him. Then he likes to “show me how it’s supposed to be done” by pulling it all across the floor. He walks beautifully on the lead now; he can still get a little spooked from time to time, but he’s made massive progress since the day he arrived.

He loves his toys he just doesn’t love sharing them! He’s also a bit selective with kennel mates, so his ideal home would include a calm, placid large female dog who won’t make too much fuss over him.

Royal truly is an amazing boy, inside and out, and I hope he doesn’t have to wait much longer for the forever home he deserves.

Royal never fails to make us smile with his crazy, funny, and quirky personality. He’s got such a cheeky side to him just waiting for the right people to help it shine.

On the lead, Royal is already walking beautifully, though he can still get a little nervous at times. His new family will need to be patient and willing to help him build confidence. Loud noises or sudden movements can overwhelm him, so he’ll do best with calm, quiet walks to start.

This week Royal had his very first trip down to the big yard! He loved it, though he found his confidence by sticking close to his doggy friend. With more practice, we’re sure he’ll begin to explore on his own.

Royal absolutely adores other dogs. Once he’s settled in, he loves to play, so he’ll need a kind and confident resident dog to show him the ropes, give him reassurance, and of course, enjoy plenty of playtime together.

He’s such a handsome boy with so much love to give we can’t believe he hasn’t found his forever home yet!

This past month has been a huge step forward for our boy Royal! Once a little unsure of the world, Royal is now walking beautifully on lead, it’s such a massive step for him considering how nervous he once was!

Royal currently shares his kennel with both a male and a female dog and he’s proving to be a respectful and easy companion. He enjoys their company, often watching what they do and following their lead. Royal will definitely need another resident dog around his size in his home, so he can continue to have the doggy companionship to help him continue to grow in confidence.

Despite his progress, Royal is still a sensitive soul, and it takes a little time for him to warm up to you. Royals forever family will need to give him time and patience to come out of his shell, so for this reason I believe Royal would be best suited to a home with no children.

Please don’t leave Royal waiting much longer for his forever home, he really deserves a cosy sofa to curl up on!

I’m so proud of Royal, this boy has come on tremendously since arriving at Many Tears. From arriving a terrified dog and very unsure of us humans, he has now slowly but surely begun to trust us and realise we are not so bad, especially when we arrive with cheesy treats.

Royal loves food, toys and being outside in our yards. He has just began harness training, ready to begin lead walking. At the moment he is not so keen on lead walking but he has taken a few tentative steps and with the help of some squeezy cheese and possibly a confident doggie friend to follow I think it won’t be long before he can begin to enjoy exploring the world.

Royals adopters will need to understand he is still very wary and unsure of his environment and he is going to need plenty of time, love and patience to trust his humans, but in the right home and given time I think this boy is going to be a big, playful and lovable boy. Royal will need a home where there is already a resident dog.

Royal is a very scared boy who has come to us from a breeder. He is especially scared when it comes to being touched by us humans but when you get him in the back of the kennel he will allow you to gently stroke him but he is uncomfortable with this. At the moment Royal could possibly make the wrong decision if handled incorrectly but this is purely through fear and he is already starting to make improvements. He will actually get excited to see his kennel mum in the mornings and will wag his tail but he’s not sure how to interact with her yet.

Royal has never lived in a home so this is going to be completely overwhelming at first and he will definitely need at least one other dog in the home to help his confidence. This will help him with house training and lead walking but these are things that are going to take him time to learn as the garden may be as scary as the home at first.

Royal will need a very calm and quiet, adult only home and adopters who have lots of experience with scared dogs. We think he’ll come out of his shell a lot more over time but Royal needs a lot of TLC, time and patience.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Hatty
description:
I need an experienced adult-only home where I can feel safe and loved.

I need a resident dog to help me feel safe. I've never met cats so I'm unsure!

I'm a bit of a Houdini and will need a secure garden to keep me safe.

I am too scared to go out for walks right now and will need careful introduction.

I'm still learning house training, lead walking, and other basics of home life.

I’m fully vaccinated and spayed, ready for my forever home!

30-09-26 Hatty originally came to us from a breeder, and was adopted for a period of time, and was sadly returned to our care due to her adopter becoming unwell. She managed a recent vet visit incredibly well considering how worried she can be, allowing the vet to examine her and administer her vaccinations while she was safely cuddled in her blanket. We know that the right home for Hatty is out there, and that with someone who truly understands her, she can form an incredibly special bond.Hatty is a very worried little lady who has come such a long way since arriving with us. She finds human interaction incredibly stressful and can still be very timid and defensive when she feels she is going to be handled. However, she has made some lovely progress in her foster home and is showing us that, with the right person and plenty of patience, she can learn to feel safe.

Hatty will still need a blanket to help her feel comfortable when she needs to be picked up, and she can become frightened enough to toilet herself when she is worried about being handled. Once she is safely settled, she will allow gentle strokes around her face, head and back, although she is not comfortable with her feet being touched. Her foster home has found that she is happiest when she is given plenty of space and allowed to approach things at her own pace.

Hatty absolutely loves other dogs and is particularly happy around other Dachshunds. She gets very excited to see her dog friends and enjoys being around them, so she will need a confident resident dog in her new home who can help her feel safe and show her the ropes. She enjoys having a cosy space of her own to retreat to, but also loves being able to relax on the sofa alongside the other dogs.

Hatty is very treat motivated and will happily come over for treats, which is a lovely way for her adopters to build a positive relationship with her. She is content plodding around, observing what is going on and enjoying the company of her canine friends. She can be destructive if left alone, so her adopters will need to be prepared for this and ensure she has plenty of safe things to occupy her.

Hatty will need a very special home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and understand just how frightening the world can feel for her. She will need a quiet, adult-only home with someone who is around most of the time and who can give her the time and space she needs without placing expectations on her. She will need gentle handling and continued support with things such as toilet training and lead training, although walks may not be something she becomes comfortable with.

Hatty is not going to be an easy dog to rehome, but she is a very special and frightened girl who deserves someone willing to see past her worries. With a confident canine companion, a quiet home and an adopter who can give her the time and patience she needs, we believe Hatty can continue to flourish and discover just how lovely life can be.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Pushkin
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I walk well on harness but I can be spooked. Let's take it slow!

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home. Read below for more information!

Pushkin has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for a loving forever home. She can be nervous when meeting new people and situations, but her confidence has grown so much during her time with us. She simply needs a little time to warm up and figure people out, and once she feels comfortable her wonderful personality starts to shine through.

Pushkin is a truly lovely girl with a fun, quirky nature and a very affectionate side. She has become a firm favourite with the staff who know her, and once she trusts you she is incredibly rewarding to spend time with. She loves being around people she knows and has a gentle, sweet temperament that is impossible not to fall in love with.

Pushkin takes a great deal of comfort from the company of other dogs and becomes worried and stressed when left on her own. Because of this, she will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home to take her under their wing and help guide her through life. She gets along beautifully with other dogs and has happily shared kennels and enjoyed play dates with a variety of canine companions. She is respectful around toys and eats well alongside other dogs, making her an easy companion to have around.

She is now walking on a harness and has made lovely progress, although some things can still make her nervous when out and about. Her adopters will need to be patient and reassuring, helping her to feel safe and encouraging her when she encounters new experiences. She gains confidence from having another dog alongside her and would benefit from a calm canine friend to help her navigate the world.

Pushkin has never experienced life in a home before, so her new family will need to be kind, patient and understanding as she learns all about home life. She will need help with house training and learning the everyday routines that most pet dogs take for granted. She enjoys treats, so positive reinforcement will be a wonderful way to help her learn and build confidence. She will need a home with adopters who have experience of ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace. We would consider homing her with dog savvy teenagers 13+. She will also need a secure garden with fencing of at least 6ft to ensure her safety while she adjusts to her new home.

Pushkin is a special little lady who has so much love to give. With plenty of patience, reassurance and the support of a canine friend, she will continue to blossom into a wonderful companion. She has brought so much joy to those caring for her, and we know that the lucky family who adopts her will absolutely adore her.

She has been treated for a ear infection.

Pushkin has been given the Gift of Life by Cherry Lewis

The last two weeks or so Pushkin, along with her kennel buddy Maggie, has been joining the big play group down the big play yard everyday (weather permitted) and she absolutely loves it. She enjoys saying hello to the other doggies there and play chases with some of them, it's so cute to watch, it makes my heart melt. It's amazing to see how much her confidence has grown, she really is blossoming.

She is quite attached to me, and does get excited to see me, she loves getting fusses from me, and is never too far from where I am if we're in a yard together, so if you like having a little extra shadow following you around she could be the girl for you.I took her out today on just a lead instead of a harness and she did amazingly, that being said for safety reasons and until she is comfortable and feels safe with you adopters would need to walk her on a harness for a while.Pushkin is just an amazing girl, I can't praise her enough and I'm always more than happy to talk about her with anyone who is interested in adopting her.

This beautiful lady brightens up my days, and as this has been a difficult week for me personally, she has been there to put a smile on my face through it.She can be nervous when you meet her initially but her confidence has grown so much she just needs time to warm up to you and figure you out, but once she's comfortable and her personality comes out she's just so much fun, and so loving. She has such a quirky personality and I absolutely adore her.Pushkin does walk on a harness, although some things do make her nervous still when out on a walk so adopters will need to be aware of this and let her know she is safe as well as some encouragement.Pushkin gets along with pretty much all dogs, any dog she has been kennelled with or introduced to for a play date she has always been so good, is fine with toys around and also eats well around the other dogs.She has never lived in a home before so her new family will have to show her the ropes and help her with her house training, be encouraging and use positive reinforcement, she does enjoy treats so they should be a big help.I'm not lying when I say I genuinely get excited to see her everyday I'm at work, she really is a little ray of sunshine.

Pushkin has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for a loving forever home. She is initially quite nervous and unsure, but once you spend some time with her she starts to come out of her shell and even begins to enjoy a fuss.

Pushkin is a sweet girl who simply needs understanding and the chance to build her confidence at her own pace. She will be looking for a calm and quiet home where she can settle in gradually and continue to blossom. She takes a great deal of comfort from the company of other dogs and becomes quite worried and stressed when left on her own. Because of this, she will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home to take her under their wing and show her that the world isn't such a frightening place.

Pushkin has never experienced life in a home before, so her new family will need to be kind, patient and understanding as she learns all about home life and new skills such as house training. She has made lovely progress with her harness training and is now walking on a harness, although she is still a little nervous when out and about. She is much more confident when she has another dog alongside her, so having a calm canine companion to help reassure her on walks will be a real benefit. She will need a home with adopters who have experience of ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace. She will also need a secure garden with fencing of at least 6ft to ensure her safety while she adjusts to her new home.

With plenty of love, reassurance and the support of a canine friend, Pushkin will continue to grow in confidence and become a wonderful companion. She is a lovely girl with so much potential, and we can't wait to see her enjoying the happy life she truly deserves.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Faith
description:
I will need an adult-only home that understands I need time to settle in.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I will need a large, extra-secure garden to keep me safe as I learn about the home.

I’m new to walking on a harness and doing well!

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before.

I've started my vaccinations and will be spayed before adoption.

Faith is a beautiful girl who came to us from a breeder and was initially incredibly shut down and terrified of people. She would run away from any human interaction and wouldn't even eat when people were around. However, over the last two months, Faith has made some wonderful progress and is slowly learning that people can be kind. She now walks on a harness, although she can still be easily spooked, and is happiest walking with people she knows and trusts. She will now take treats from us in her kennel, and sometimes on walks when things are quiet, with hot dogs being a particular favourite! Recently, she even allowed a little gentle fuss in the big play yard, choosing to stay for affection rather than run away. This may seem like a small step, but for Faith, it is a huge achievement.

Faith absolutely adores other dogs and truly comes alive when joining her friends for playtime in our big yard. She approaches them with a full-body wiggle and has even discovered how much fun toys can be, although she cannot be left unsupervised with soft toys! She will need a kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help her continue building her confidence and show her the ropes of home life. As a Collie, she will also need plenty of enrichment and exercise to keep her busy once she has settled in.

Faith is still a very nervous girl who will need an adult-only home with Collie experience, where her progress will be celebrated and she can continue learning at her own pace. She has never lived in a home before, so she will need patient adopters who can help her with house training, lead walking and all the other new experiences that come with family life. She will also need an extra-secure garden of at least 6ft to keep her safe as she settles in.

Faith really is such a sweet girl who tries her very hardest to be brave. Although she is making lovely progress with us, kennels is no place for a puppy to spend these important months of her life. Her three Collie friends who arrived with her have all found their forever homes, and now it is Faith's turn to find someone who can see just how far she has come and how much potential she has. With time, patience and lots of love, we know this special girl has so much more to discover, and we desperately hope her forever family won't keep her waiting much longer.

Faith has been given the Gift of Life by Raychel Mount

name: Julius
description:
I can live with older children, aged 16+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I would like another dog in my new home to be my friend. I have never met cats!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am neutered and am being treated for sore ears.

21-09-26 Julius has come to us from a breeder to start his new adventure. He is a very worried boy who is feeling overwhelmed by all the changes in his world. He is unsure of people and worried about being handled, so will initially run away and hide. Once safely in your arms, he does settle, and with time, patience and TLC, we hope he will gradually begin to come out of his shell. He has already discovered the joy of soft toys, which is lovely to see, although he can sometimes grumble at other dogs approaching his toys and may guard them, so his new adopters will need to be understanding and willing to work with him on this.

Julius will be looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and understand that he will need to settle in completely at his own pace. We would consider a home with gentle, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16+ who can give him the space and patience he needs.

Julius will need a kind and confident resident dog in his new home to take him under their wing and help him feel safe as he adjusts to home life. Having a canine friend to learn from will be important for Julius as he begins to build his confidence and discover that the world isn't such a scary place.

Julius has never lived in a home before, so he will need kind and patient adopters as he learns all about home life and new skills like house training. He will also need to learn about walking on a lead and harness, starting with gentle practice around the garden and gradually building his confidence.

Julius is a lovely boy who has so much potential, and with time, love and kindness, we hope he will gradually come out of his shell and begin to enjoy all the comforts of family life.

Julius is currently being treated for sore ears.

Julius has been given the Gift of Life by Sharon West

name: Sianon
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

27-08-26 Sianon has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for her forever home. She is a worried girl who is unsure around humans and isn't used to being handled yet. She is going to need plenty of love, patience and TLC as she settles in and slowly begins to grow in confidence.

Sianon will be looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and who understand that she will need time to adjust. Her new family will need to be kind and patient, allowing her to settle in at her own pace without putting pressure on her. She has never lived in a home before, so everything will be new to her, and she will need gentle guidance as she learns all about home life and new skills such as house training and how to walk on a lead and harness.

Sianon relies on other dogs for confidence, so she will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to be her friend and help her feel safe. We hope having a canine companion by her side will help her learn that the world isn't such a scary place. Any children in the home will need to be teenagers aged 16+.

Sianon is a gentle girl who has lots to learn, but with the right home, a patient family and a lovely canine friend to show her the ropes, we hope she will gradually discover her confidence and enjoy all the wonderful things life has to offer.

Sianon has been given the Gift of Life by Dee Wickson-Dix

name: Louise
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home with experienced adopters.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I am not ready to learn about lead walking yet. A garden is fine for now.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

Louise has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for a very special forever home. She is an extremely worried little girl who has had very little positive human socialisation and can still find people and handling very frightening. However, she has made lovely progress since arriving and is showing us more of her cheeky personality every day.

Over the past month, Louise has grown in confidence. While she is still very worried about being touched and picked up, she is no longer as shut down as she was when she first arrived. She is now more than happy to come over for treats and will sit close by while waiting for more. She likes to use her voice to let everyone know how she is feeling, is very partial to chasing flies, and has quite a big personality packed into such a tiny dog. It is wonderful to see her becoming more comfortable in her surroundings.

Louise will need a calm and quiet adult-only home with no visiting children, and adopters who have experience helping fearful ex-breeding dogs learn to trust. She relies heavily on the comfort and reassurance of other dogs and will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help guide her as she settles into family life.

Louise can be vocal around food and may give a warning growl, but she does not actually do anything and this appears to simply be her way of communicating that she would like some space. She can happily be fed alongside her canine friends as long as each dog has their own bowl and they stick to their own food. She is also absolutely fine taking treats, so this is something her adopters should continue to manage calmly and sensibly.

Louise is slowly becoming more comfortable with being handled, and gentle work has begun to help her get used to being picked up. This is still very worrying for her and she can become wriggly and panic when lifted, but she has never tried to bite during these sessions. With time and patience, we hope she will continue to learn that she is safe and that nobody is going to hurt her.

Having never lived in a home before, Louise has lots to learn. Her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she adjusts to home life and learns the basics, including house training. She is not yet ready for harness training, so her future family will need to carefully plan how and when to introduce this once she feels more secure. Everything must happen at Louise's pace so that she can continue building confidence without becoming overwhelmed.

Louise is a sensitive little soul who will need a dedicated home willing to invest time, patience and understanding into helping her flourish. Every small step she takes is a huge achievement, and she continues to surprise us with just how much she is growing in confidence. With experienced adopters, kind canine companions and lots of love, we truly believe Louise will continue to blossom into the wonderful little dog we know she can become.

Louise has been given the Gift of Life by Ann Winter

Louise has been with us for about 3 months now and even though she has progressed since she first arrived, things are happening very slowly and steadily. I would have liked for her to have gained more confidence by this point, but some dogs struggle with being in such a busy kennel environment to let their guard down … and Louise is one of them! That’s okay though. Making sure she’s happy and content within herself is the most important thing, and I’d say she is!

I haven’t really pushed Louise too far out of her comfort zone up until now, just because I didn’t want to send her backwards with her progress, but there does come a point where you have to, to prove to them that it’s okay. So today I took Louise into my grooming room for a very gentle and calm brushing session. She didn’t want to stand on the grooming table and kept clambering back onto me - which is the first time she’s ever done that - so I opted to keep her on my lap while I brushed her. She was settled for the most part, but she did have a little panic when we got to her ears as she had a couple of tangles which must have hurt her. I managed to cut them out with a scissors and then she was okay with me brushing around that area. I kept the session very short and sweet as I didn’t want to push too far, and I think it was the right decision. When I took her back to the kennel she didn’t sprint away from me or anything like that, so I’d say our relationship is still there!

Louise is such a special little character, and I really hope someone will see her in the same way I do soon. She deserves a life outside of kennels, one where she can finally start to thrive.

Louise has been on my section with me for about a month now, and I’ve definitely seen some positive changes in her. She’s still terrified of being touched and picked up, but her overall confidence is improving daily. She’s now more than happy to come and take treats from me and sit close to me while she’s waiting for more. She’s also nowhere near as shut down as she was when she first arrived and is now turning into quite a cheeky monkey. She does like to use her voice to express her feelings, and she’s also very partial to chasing flies! She’s actually got quite a big personality for such a little girl, and it’s a pleasure to see it emerging as the days go by.I’ve been working slowly on getting Louise used to being picked up, and while she’s definitely still very worried about it, she has calmed down slightly. She’s never tried to bite me, but she does sometimes have little panics and becomes very wriggly when she’s in my arms. I do think this is something that will improve over time. She just needs some more practice and to realise that we’re not hurting her. She obviously hasn’t been handled a lot in her life, so now it’s up to us to prove to her that it’s okay.I love working with Louise, and I can really see the potential in her. She just needs someone to give her a chance and work with her through all her worries and fears. She’s not ready for harness training or conquering the outside world yet, so that’s something her future adopters will need to take into consideration and make a plan for. I do believe she’ll progress faster in a kind home with adopters who have lots of time and patience to give her, so I really hope she won’t have to wait here for much longer.

Louise has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for a very special forever home. She is an extremely worried little girl who has had very little positive human socialisation and currently finds people and handling very frightening. At the moment, Louise feels safest keeping her distance and, if pushed beyond her comfort zone, may make the wrong decision and nip purely out of fear. She is a very scared girl who needs understanding, patience and time.Louise will need a calm and quiet adult-only home with no visiting children, and adopters who have experience of helping fearful ex-breeding dogs learn to trust. She relies heavily on the comfort and reassurance of other dogs and will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can take her under their wing.Although Louise takes great comfort from other dogs, she can show signs of resource guarding around food. For this reason, she will need to be fed separately from other dogs, and care will need to be taken when giving treats or other high-value food items. Her adopters will need experience of managing this behaviour and the confidence to do so appropriately.Having never lived in a home before, Louise has lots to learn. Her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she adjusts to home life and learns new skills such as house training. She is not yet ready to begin learning about lead walking or wearing a harness, as handling is still very worrying for her. These things will need to be introduced gradually and at her pace once she feels more comfortable and secure.Louise is a sensitive soul who will need a dedicated home willing to invest time, patience and understanding into helping her build confidence. We will continue to work with her every day, helping her take small steps forward at a pace she is comfortable with. In the right home, with the support of canine friends and experienced adopters, we hope Louise will slowly learn that people can be kind and that life has so much to offer.

name: Nora
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I’m new to walking on a harness and doing well!

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

Nora is a gentle girl who has come to us from a breeder and is now in foster, where she has been able to experience life in a home for the first time. She has been in foster for over a month now, and this has given us a much better understanding of her mobility, as well as allowing her confidence to grow and her lovely personality to shine through.

Nora is still very mistrustful of people, but she is beginning to show us that she really does want to make friends. She is now much more willing to approach her fosterer and has recently started coming over to take treats from her. She will even jump up onto the sofa to watch Netflix, as long as there is another dog already on the sofa with her! These may seem like small things, but for Nora they are huge steps forward and show just how much she is beginning to relax. She will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her home that will allow her to lean on them as she continues to settle.

She absolutely loves the comforts of home life and takes great reassurance from having other dogs around her. She has also been on a few short walks outside the home, allowing her to slowly experience the world beyond her garden. She is still a very sensitive girl and everything will need to be introduced gradually, but she is making lovely progress.

Nora's mobility has also improved in a home setting. Her ataxia appears to be closely linked to her stress levels and is much more noticeable when she is worried or overwhelmed. When she is relaxed, her movements are almost normal, which is incredibly encouraging. She is not currently on any medication, and her fosterer is helping her to build muscle strength through daily massage and gentle exercise.

Nora will need a quiet and understanding home with adopters who have experience with nervous dogs and, ideally, ex-breeders. She will need at least one calm, friendly resident dog to give her confidence and show her the way. Her new family will need to be incredibly patient and allow her to settle and build trust at her own pace, without expecting too much too soon.

Nora has had lots of hardships in her life and is still learning that she can feel safe around people. However, the progress she has made since moving into foster has been wonderful to see. Beneath her worries is a very sweet girl who is slowly discovering how lovely life can be, and we are hoping that the right home will give her the security, patience and love she needs to continue blossoming.

Nora has been given the Gift of Life by Judie Fisher

Nora has been in foster for over a month now which allowed us to have a good assessment of her mobility, and also helped increase her confidence and introduce her to living in a home. This gentle girl has a very sweet personality and loves the comforts of home life and the company of other dogs. She is still very mistrustful of humans, but I can see that she is now more willing to try and be friends. She has recently started coming up to take a treat from me, and will even jump up on the sofa to watch Netflix with me (as long as there is another dog on the sofa too). She has also been on a few short walks outside to see the world beyond my home and garden!

Nora's ataxia has improved in a home setting too, largely because it is connected to her mental state and seems to be worse when she is stressed. When Nora is relaxed, her movements are almost normal, which is lovely to see and gives me hope that once she feels safe and comfortable mentally, she will have a great quality of life. We just need to help her get there. Nora is not on any medication at the moment, but I massage her daily and we are working on building her muscle strength.

Nora's ideal home will be a quiet setting with one or more calm and friendly dogs. Her people will need to be kind and very patient, with experience of scared dogs and preferably beagles too. This gorgeous girl has had lots of hardships in her life, it is time for her to finally have a place where she feels safe and loved.

I have been working with Nora a few days a week since she first arrived with us and was on medication and crate rest for her legs. Around two weeks ago, Nora moved to a different section, so I haven't seen her in a little while. I popped over today to check in and chat to one of her new kennel dads to see how she's doing.

Since arriving on her new section, Nora has made huge leaps! She is now harness-trained and wears her harness comfortably during the day. She has grown more confident with handling and with walking on her harness to and from the yard, though she is not yet feeling up to walks outside the centre. She also now sits curiously at the front of her kennel, watching people and dogs come and go on her section, rather than hiding in the back.

Nora still has a long way to go in learning to trust humans and receive our love, but she's made huge steps already. It's a great reminder that all of us working here have different skills, and sometimes a dog who is struggling just needs a change of scene to take the next steps in their journey towards their forever home.

Nora is so gentle and if you ignore the deep defensive howl (she is a beagle after all!) eventually she quietens down and she shows her soft side.Nora is still trying to get used to enjoying human company. She is not there yet but is slowly beginning to show signs of trusting people and does settle near you with a little patience.

It appears to me that it's not that Nora dislikes people, it's more a matter of how she is unsure of who we are and how we do things.

Once she  settles and it does take a little time, although still afraid, is much more willing to be approached by people.

In this calmer state, I was able to smooth her coat all over and gently stroke her without her worrying too much which is a positive step for her.

Nora will need this gentle approach for some time but the reward will be endless love and loyalty which is priceless.

I believe all Nora needs right now is the stability and security that a loving home can offer.Nora does much prefer the company of dogs  at the moment so it is a must that there is a resident dog already in the home for her to be with.

Nora has kennelled with small dogs but we do feel she would be better placed with a dog of a similar size or larger.

Our next step whilst Nora is with us will be to train her to walk on a harness so she can start to discover and enjoy the outside world.

Nora has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for a very special forever home. She is a scared girl who is understandably feeling overwhelmed to find herself here and is desperately in need of kindness, patience and TLC as she begins to settle and learn that the world can be a safe place.

When Nora first arrived with us, she was showing some neurological symptoms and ataxia, and her back legs would occasionally slide from underneath her, causing her to stumble. Following investigations with our vets, it was found that her proprioception was delayed in all four limbs. She was trialed on a course of medication alongside crate rest and has made wonderful progress. Her proprioception is now normal, she is able to get around and play happily, and she enjoys life much more comfortably. She does still have a slight amount of ataxia and can occasionally limp still. Our vet feels that she may have suffered an acute injury at some point in the past which has largely resolved itself, though she will likely never present like a normal dog.

Nora will be looking for adopters who will love and cherish her just as she is. Due to her mobility history, she will need a home without slippery flooring, or one where plenty of rugs and runners are in place to help her move around confidently and safely.

She would be best suited to a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience of nervous ex-breeding dogs and understand her worries. Nora will need time to settle at her own pace and will thrive with patient adopters who are happy to let her progress in her own time. She takes great comfort from the company of other dogs and will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to show her the way and help her build confidence.

Nora has never experienced life in a home before so her new family will need to be understanding as she learns all about home life and new skills like house training. She doesn't yet walk on a lead and harness and initially she will need to practise wearing her harness and exploring safely within the home and garden before she is ready to venture further afield.

Although Nora is still very worried and unsure of the world around her, beneath her fears is a sweet and deserving little girl who simply needs someone to believe in her. Watching a scared dog slowly learn to trust is one of the most rewarding experiences, and with love, patience and understanding, Nora will blossom. The day she greets you with a wagging tail and a sparkle in her eyes will make every moment of that journey worthwhile.

name: Archie
description:
I'd like a quiet, adult-only home to help me relax and feel safe.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I walk well on a lead and would enjoy one or two walks a day!

I have lived in a home so I know the basics.

I have been neutered and have had 21 teeth removed.

Archie is such a sweet little man who came into our care from a breeder. He was adopted but has sadly been returned after his adopters felt they were not the right match for him. Archie formed a very strong bond with his female owner, but found it much harder to build a relationship with her husband, who was frequently away from home and therefore had very little opportunity to gain Archie's trust. When Archie becomes closely bonded to his favourite person, he can become protective of them. In his previous home, he nipped when he was sitting with his owner and her husband approached, so his new adopters will need to understand this behaviour and be prepared to continue building his confidence in a positive and patient way.

He is a cuddly and affectionate little dog once he feels comfortable, although he isn't quite brave enough to take treats from our hands just yet. Although Archie gets on well with other dogs, he can become protective of his favourite person around them, so we think he would be happiest as the only dog in the home, where he can relax and build a close bond with his new family.

As Archie has lived in a home before, he will already be familiar with the sights and sounds of home life. However, he may need a little reminding of his house training in a new environment. He walks well on a lead and enjoys his walks with volunteers.

Archie is looking for a quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience of the breed and of rescue dogs. He will need people who are happy to give him the time and space he needs to settle and understand that he is safe.

Archie is doing really well since returning to us and his confidence is growing all the time. He is such a loving little dog, and in the right home, we hope he will continue to thrive and become a devoted companion.

Archie is an absolute pleasure to work with! It’s been some time now, and our bond continues to grow stronger every day.He absolutely loves smothering you with kisses and will do anything to get himself onto your lap! Archie has been kennelled with a few dogs and socialised with plenty more, but he has become particularly taken with a Cocker called Trixie. They share some similar traits, including not wanting to share their humans, although neither has displayed any jealousy towardsthe other so far. They absolutely love running laps around the yard together before heading straight into your lap for some fuss. Archie will even stand on Trixie’s back just to make sure he gets in on the action and doesn’t miss out on any attention!As mentioned, Archie is yet to display any jealous traits towards either dogs or humans, but that doesn’t mean he won’t potentially show this once settled into a home. It’s something any potential adopter should be mindful of and prepared to manage appropriately.

What I can promise, though, is that Archie will become your best friend. He has so much love to give and, once he trusts you, he will love you unconditionally.This gorgeous boy deserves someone who will give him the love, patience and understanding he needs — and in return, you’ll have a loyal companion who will want nothing more than to be by your side.

Archie is the funniest and cheekiest of little Dachshunds. Archie needs a little time to warm to you (but not all that long), and once he does, he is the most lovely of boys. I have been caring for him for a few weeks now, and I am totally smitten.

Archie walks beautifully on lead and loves nothing more than when we venture out for a stroll along the lanes around the rescue. Archie is very fond of his toys and will happily run around the yard with a ball in his mouth. He will also spend much time organising his cuddly toys, making sure they are in just the right place.

Archie has been kennelled with other small female dogs. He seems to do best with robust smaller females, as he can be a little frisky with the more timid dogs. Archie could go as an only dog in the right home, one where there are humans who will have lots of time for him.

Archie is very enthusiastic with his kisses once he knows you and will desperately clamber over you for fusses. Archie is an all-round lovely little dog, best suited to a quiet adult home where there is plenty of love, time, and patience for him to truly settle in.

Archie is such a sweet little man who came into our care from a breeder. He was adopted but has sadly been returned after his adopters felt they were not the right match for him. Archie formed a very strong bond with his female owner, but found it much harder to build a relationship with her husband, who was frequently away from home and therefore had very little opportunity to gain Archie's trust. When Archie becomes closely bonded to his favourite person, he can become protective of them. In his previous home, he nipped when he was sitting with his owner and her husband approached, so his new adopters will need to understand this behaviour and be prepared to continue building his confidence in a positive, patient way.

He is a cuddly, affectionate little dog once he feels comfortable, although he isn't quite brave enough to take treats from our hands just yet. Although Archie gets on well with other dogs, he can become protective of his favourite person around them, so we think he would be happiest as the only dog in the home, where he can relax and build a close bond with his new family.

Archie is a gorgeous little boy who came to us from a breeder and was understandably unsure of the world around him. It was truly heartbreaking to see how frightened he was as he would shy away from human contact and retreat when approached. Archie needs gentle handling, patience, and calm, slow movements to help him feel safe. Already, we are seeing progress. He enjoys a gentle fuss and has grown some confidence wagging his tail enthusiastically.

He gains reassurance from other dogs and will need a kind, confident resident dog in his new home to help guide him, boost his confidence, and show him that people and home life can be safe and rewarding.

Archie has never lived in a home before, so his adopters will need to be patient and understanding as he learns the basics, including house training and walking on a lead. He could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over, who can appreciate and understand that he will need a gentle, quiet introduction to the home and his own space to settle in.

Since arriving with us, Archie has undergone extensive and much-needed dental treatment and has had 21 teeth removed. He is now recovering well and feeling much more comfortable.

name: Gail
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I would like a home with one kind resident dog. I cannot live with cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I can walk well on a lead and harness, and am doing well with those I trust.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

Gail has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. When she first arrived with us she was a very scared girl who found human interaction extremely overwhelming and would often hide away at the back of her kennel. It was clear that she hadn't had much socialisation before and was in desperate need of love and TLC. Since then Gail has started to come out of her shell and has made really encouraging progress. Although she is still a very nervous girl, once she gets to know you she does start to come out of her shell and will approach you for a gentle sniff and will allow you to gently stroke her, although still finds this very worrying.

She will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to come out of her shell and settle in at her own pace. Gail is a sensitive little girl and does really struggle with change, so she is likely to go backwards in her new home at first and will need time to adjust to her new surroundings.

Gail does rely on other dogs for comfort and reassurance and will be looking for a home where there is just one other kind, confident resident dog to be her friend. Gail doesn't really enjoy sharing her space with more than one dog and can be a little sassy and has shown that she much prefers just having one other dog to make her best friend. She does take a little while to warm up to other dogs, but once she bonds with them she absolutely adores them and finds confidence from them.

Gail has learned all about walking on a lead and harness since arriving with us and as long as she has a doggy friend by her side, now even goes for walks with some of our volunteers, which is very brave of her! She has never lived in a home before, so everything will be new to her and her adopters will need to be kind and understanding as she settles in and learns all about home life and new skills like house training.

Shortly after Gail's arrival to us, she started showing signs of back pain as well as some weakness and unsteadiness. As she's a dachshund and they can be quite prone to spinal issues, she went for x-rays to be on the safe side. The x-rays showed several mineralised discs in her spine, but did not show any obvious spinal cord compression. She was given pain relief and was put on crate rest, and initially returned to activity with the help of a supportive back brace. Gail has made a good recovery and is currently doing very well.

Gail's adopters will need to be aware that should she have any further issues in the future related to this, it would be classed as a pre-existing condition and would not be covered by insurance.

Gail is a truly special little girl who has come such a long way since arriving with us. She is still a very scared girl, and although her journey may not be a quick one, with lots of love, patience and TLC, we know it will be incredibly rewarding to watch her grow in confidence and discover just how wonderful life can be.

Gail has been given the Gift of Life by Candice Sullivan

What incredible progress this girl is making! I'm constantly impressed and surprised by her.I only work with Gail 1-2 times a month, and I'm always blown away by how far she's come when I see her again. Some things that may not seem like much can be huge milestones for our ex-breeding dogs - three months ago, Gail could only be touched by a few members of staff and was very anxious in human presence; six weeks ago, she would only tolerate having her harness put on and being walked by the two people she knew best; two weeks ago, she was walking with a few people but still spending most of her time in the back of her kennel hiding, and would try to hide in corners if she saw anyone unfamiliar; and today, she went on a 20 minute walk with me, then cuddled in my lap afterwards! She even goes for walks with volunteers she's never met before and is incredibly brave meeting new people. When visitors walk past, Gail runs to the front of her kennel with her tail wagging.Gail is a lovely little dog with so much personality. She's going to be the queen of wherever she ends up, and she deserves to be spoiled rotten! Hopefully, Gail's perfect home is right around the corner. Until then, we'll keep on showing her all the love and kindness we can.

We're super pleased with Gail's progress over the last few weeks.

Initially, we started yarding her with other dogs. She coped really well but would tell them off if they were too lively and in her face. We then started kenneling her with a female Cavalier, and she coped very well and seemed happier in herself. We then added a lively Poodle, but Gail told her off, so now she's just with the Cavalier. So, we've learnt that Gail can cope day and night with a calm dog, and on night duty, I saw them snuggled up in the same bed.Gail's walking is much better, but only with the staff who know her well. She follows her nose on a walk and likes walking in longer grass. Gail will roll over for a tummy rub but is still a little unsure about too much fuss.Gail is a happy little girl, full of character, who loves to carry her favourite toys around, and she's not possessive of them.

Gail has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for her forever home. She is a very scared little girl who found herself extremely overwhelmed when she first arrived, and it was clear she was not used to much handling or human interaction. At the beginning, Gail was very wary of people and would do her best to avoid being handled, often using warning signals to ask for space. If she felt pushed beyond her comfort zone, she could panic and make poor decisions through fear. With time, patience and consistency from the staff she knows and trusts, Gail is making lovely progress and is beginning to show her softer side.

Although still a nervous girl, Gail is progressing well with the staff she has built relationships with and now enjoys attention from the people she knows well. She absolutely loves a tummy rub and has started to seek out familiar staff members for reassurance, showing that, given time, she is capable of forming strong bonds with the people she trusts.

Gail spent some time recovering from a back injury, but she is now showing no signs of pain and is back to her normal self. She happily trots around as though nothing was ever wrong and has recovered brilliantly. During her recovery she spent time on her own and, although she was later reintroduced to a previous canine friend, it became clear that Gail no longer enjoys the company of other dogs and does not like for them to invade her space. For this reason, she will need to be the only dog in her forever home.

Gail will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience of scared ex-breeding dogs and understand the importance of patience, time and reading her body language. She will need kind, understanding adopters who will allow her to take everything at a pace she feels comfortable with and continue building her confidence without putting her under pressure.

She has never lived in a home before, so everything will be new to her. She will need to learn all about home life, including house training and settling into a daily routine. Gail has also recently started her lead training and has surprised everyone with how quickly she has progressed. After taking just a few tentative steps on her first outing, she was happily trotting around, sniffing her surroundings and even confidently walking over to one of her favourite people the very next day. She is proving that, with gentle encouragement, she is capable of making wonderful progress.

As Gail has had previous back issues, we have used a supportive back brace harness to help protect her while she builds her confidence on walks. This is something her adopters may wish to continue using in the future for extra support.

Gail is a very special little girl who still has plenty to learn, but she has already shown just how far she can come with the right people by her side. She is looking for experienced adopters who are willing to invest the time and patience she needs, and in return they will gain a wonderfully rewarding companion as they watch her confidence continue to grow.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Cuba
description:
I will need a loving and understanding adult-only home!

I'd prefer to be the only dog. I can't live with cats.

I am still unsure about the world, so a secure garden would be ideal.

I walk well on harness but I can be spooked, especially by traffic!

Please be patient with me, I'm nervous and learning everything from scratch.

I have been neutered and am ready for my forever home. Read below for more!

Cuba is a very sensitive and shy boy who is still finding the world quite overwhelming, but who is making lovely progress as his confidence slowly grows. Cuba arrived with very little life experience and can be easily worried by new situations, so he needs a calm, gentle approach and plenty of time to build trust.

As he gets to know people, Cuba is becoming increasingly sociable. He may need a couple of meetings to feel comfortable, but once he trusts you, he will happily approach with his tail wagging and enjoy quiet, gentle fuss. He particularly loves relaxing in his bed with trusted company nearby and finds calm strokes very reassuring, often drifting off to sleep while being gently fussed. Recently, he has started to open up his trust circle and has accepted a few new recruits. This is a big step for a worried boy like, Cuba and we are so proud of him! As his confidence grows, his playful side is beginning to shine. He adores playing with toys, cuddling, giving kisses, and will happily bounce around like a lunatic when he’s feeling safe and excited.

Cuba has never lived in a home before, so everything will be new to him. He will need experienced, adult-only adopters who understand nervous dogs and are happy to let him settle at his own pace. Patient guidance will be needed as he learns all about home life, including house training and walking on a harness and lead. He has recently started harness training and is beginning to enjoy it, but this will still need to be continued slowly and positively, starting with gentle practice in the garden. Once out and about, Cuba enjoys taking in the world at his own pace and loves sniffing everything in sight on his walks but he can be spooked by traffic.

Cuba would prefer to be the only dog in the home, so his adopters will need to be around enough to keep him company and provide reassurance as he settles. However, his kennel mummy has been working with him lately regarding his socialization skills and he is being an amazing boy. He has greeted friends fine, but this will continue to take time and lots of trust. He will need to be the only dog in the home, but these steps show how much is confidence is growing.

He will need a home without cats or small furries as he does have a prey drive.

He is quite fond of using his voice and enjoys a good grumble rather than barking, which is very much part of his character. Beneath his worried exterior, Cuba is a sweet, gentle boy who has already formed strong bonds with familiar staff and is learning that not all people are bad.

Cuba will need a calm and understanding home where his boundaries are respected and he can have his own safe space. With kindness, patience, and the right support, he has the potential to continue blossoming into a truly rewarding companion.

Cuba has had a bilateral entropion repair and has been treated for an ear infection. He is currently experiencing lameness in his back left leg, which is more noticeable after he has been sitting or lying down for a while. He initially struggles to put weight on it when he first gets up, but this improves after a few minutes of moving around. He is receiving pain relief to help keep him comfortable and will need very limited exercise while he recovers.

Cubawill need more than one meet and greet with his prospective adopters to allow him time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

The past couple of weeks I’ve focused on socialising Cuba with other dogs. So far we’ve done a couple of walks with a Poodle Cross and also a Samoyed Cross, and I was honestly so proud of how well he behaved. He had sniffs of them both, let them sniff him, and walked with them close by. He was a lot more comfortable with the Poodle as she was more laid back and not as interested in him, whereas the Samoyed was a bit more curious about him so wanted to sniff him a lot more. He wasn’t overly keen on this, but he didn’t show any aggression whatsoever! I’m going to keep doing walks like this over the next few weeks, and play it by ear.Cuba has also opened up his circle of trusted people at the rescue, and we’re now up to 4!! By this I mean he’s comfortable around them and lets them give him lots of fusses, which is pretty huge for a boy like Cuba with such big trust issues! He’s also been very good at taking treats off lots of other staff members, and will now stop in his tracks when he sees the particular people who usually have a tasty snack for him. Very cute (and funny)!!

Cuba has had quite a busy few weeks at the rescue and has had to put his big boy pants on!! I’ve started taking him into our on site cabin which is similar to being in a home environment. It’s got a sofa, bed, TV etc … so I thought it would be a good idea to start taking him in there to help desensitise him to new things.

Obviously he’s never been in a home before, so everything was completely brand new for him. The first time he was very nervous and really didn’t know what to do at all. He was holding himself low to the floor and hunched, but he was walking around doing little sniffs of things. I was sat on the sofa and he did come over to me a couple of times for reassurance which did help a little, but after about only 5 minutes I took him back to his kennel as I didn’t want to overdo it.

The second time he was still nervous again, but after a little while he did start to drop his guard and became quite curious. He kept coming over to me for a fuss and a treat, so that was a really good sign being brave enough to eat in there. He was fascinated by the TV and didn’t quite know what to think of it. He was a bit scared of it I think, but equally as intrigued. I’m going to keep taking him into the cabin once a week or so just to ease him into it slowly, and then hopefully that will help his transition to home life when he does get adopted.

Cuba has been with me for over 3 months now and I literally love him more and more every day. I’m lucky to have a very close relationship with him and he loves me and trusts me completely, so I see a side to him that not many other people get to see.

He absolutely oozes charisma and character, and he makes me laugh and smile every time we’re together. He’s fiercely loyal, super affectionate, and SO comical. He gives the best of everything. He loves running around the yard with me and playing with toys, but loves a big sit down snuggle equally as much. So much so, he now likes to sprawl across my whole lap and fall into a deep sleep on me (snores and all)! His kennel is filled with plush toys that he loves to carry around in his mouth and sleep with, and he’s SO gentle with them. Isn’t he just the sweetest boy!?

He does still find a lot of things quite challenging, but I do feel as though we’re still making steady progress, and you can’t rush certain things. He’s still very easily spooked by loud noises, cars passing, people trying to approach him etc, so on walks especially I do have to make sure I’m paying complete attention to him. Most of the time he does recover quickly with a bit of reassurance from me, but then sometimes it will ruin his whole walk and he’ll immediately want to turn around and go back to the safety of his kennel. That’s okay though - I always allow it and take him back to make sure he knows he always has a safe place as and when he needs it.

We’ve briefly mentioned in a previous update that Cuba doesn’t like other dogs that much, but I hope this won’t put you off him as he’s not reactive to other dogs out on walks or anything like that - he simply just doesn’t like to share his space with them. I don’t think he was socialised with others apart from his old kennel friend before he came to us, so I think it’s understandable.

If you have the time and the patience to put the work in with Cuba, I can promise you 10 times over that adopting him will be the best decision of your life. Once he settles, he will truly be your best friend and the love of your life. That’s how I feel about him and I’m just his kennel mum!! He is utterly special and he deserves someone equally as special, who will love him as much as he will love them. He has such a big heart and he really does deserve the world and more.

Cuba has come on leaps and bounds over the past few weeks, and I feel so lucky to have been appointed as his “Kennel Auntie,” spending two days a week with this incredibly handsome boy.

Although Cuba can still be wary of strangers, the bond he forms once he trusts you is truly something special. Knowing him from when he first arrived, you honestly wouldn’t recognise him now. He used to hide away at the back of his kennel, wishing we would go away, now he demands to be the centre of attention and absolutely smothers you in kisses. While he may take a little time to warm up to new people, once he feels safe, his affectionate nature shines through.

Cuba has taken some big steps (quite literally!) and is absolutely smashing his harness training. His progress has been incredible, and his confidence grows more each day. He happily trots along on walks, tail wagging, taking in all the exciting new smells he’s never experienced before. Watching him discover so many “firsts” is truly magical.

We’ve found that Cuba isn’t too fussed about other dogs (aside from his kennel friend Chippy), so he would be best suited to a home where he can be the only dog. This will allow him to soak up all the love and attention he thrives on.

I cherish every moment I get to spend with Cuba. He is the sweetest, soppiest boy. He is so full of love, yet not enough people get to see this side of him.
