He adores playing with toys, cuddling, bouncing around like a lunatic, giving kisses, and sniffing everything in sight on his walks. But most of all, he loves his people.

There isn’t a moment with Cuba where you won’t feel loved. He makes every second count and whoever is lucky enough to adopt him should do the same. He truly is a special boy, and you wouldn’t want to miss out on him.

Cuba has been on my section for a few weeks now and I am just head over heels in love with him. I knew he was a nervous and sensitive boy so I have taken things slow with him and left him be to suss me out and get used to my routine, but it really didn’t take long for him to become quite attached to me. Within a few days he started to trust me, and now I would say he actually trusts me completely. So much so, I’ve been able to start harness training with him, put medication in his eyes after his surgery, and he’s given me his belly a couple of times for fusses!!!

I still haven’t taken him outside of the secure yard on his harness yet, but I do think he’s ready so I’m going to try it really soon. His biggest fear was having any tension on the lead - he would get really spooked by it and panic - but I think we’re just about over that now and he’s gotten used to it.With Cuba, once he gets to know you and forms a bond with you he is an extremely affectionate, happy, and playful boy, but he is still standoffish with people he doesn’t know and he doesn’t trust them to touch him or handle him. This is something his future adopters will need to take into consideration and prepare for. He’ll just need to be given some time, patience and gentleness to begin with. I am certain he’ll come around, but it will need to be in his own time as he can’t be pushed.

Cuba is hilarious and so goofy, and he will make such a great addition to someone’s home in time, but it does need to be the right home to ensure he’s set up for only success. I adore him very much and I just know his future parents will too, so please keep him in mind if you think you could be a good match for him!

Cuba is making lovely progress and is becoming increasingly sociable as his confidence grows. He is still finding walking on a harness quite scary and will need a patient home willing to help him continue this training at his own pace.

Cuba may need a couple of meetings to feel comfortable, but once he knows you, he will happily approach with his tail wagging and enjoy a gentle fuss. He particularly loves relaxing in his bed with trusted company nearby, quietly enjoying being stroked as he drifts off to sleep.

At heart, he is a very sweet and gentle boy who is learning to trust and has already formed strong bonds with familiar staff. He is simply a scared boy who needs a fresh start in a calm, understanding and respectful home where he can continue to blossom.

Cuba is a very nervous and shy boy who is finding the world quite overwhelming at the moment. He needs a slow, gentle approach and plenty of time to build trust, but once he feels safe with someone, he will allow calm, gentle fuss while settled in his bed, which he finds very reassuring. Underneath his worried exterior, Cuba is simply a big, scared baby who needs kindness, patience, and understanding to help him feel secure.

Cuba will need an adult-only home with experienced adopters who understand nervous dogs and are happy to let him settle at his own pace. He has never lived in a home before, so everything will be completely new to him. His adopters will need to be patient and supportive as he learns about home life, including house training and how to walk on a harness and lead. Gentle practice in the garden will be an important starting point before he is ready to venture further afield.

Cuba will also need at least one kind, confident resident dog in the home. He gains comfort and confidence from other dogs and will benefit greatly from having a calm canine role model to help guide him and show him that the world is a safe place. He is not suitable to be an only dog.

Cuba is currently learning to walk on a harness, but this is something he finds very challenging and will require a great deal of time, patience, and dedication. He is also quite fond of using his voice and enjoys a good grumble rather than barking, which is very much part of his character.

Cuba will need a calm, quiet home where he can have his own safe space and plenty of downtime alongside gentle interaction. With love, reassurance, and understanding adopters, he will slowly begin to realise that not all people are bad and that he is finally safe. In the right home, with the right support, Cuba has the potential to blossom into a deeply rewarding companion.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

name: Koala
description:
I can live with older children, aged 16+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I will be spayed before going to my forever home!

01-10-26 Koala is a frightened little lady who has come to us from a breeder and is still very unsure of us humans. She can be quite a flighty girl and, at the moment, would much rather hide away than have people approach her. Once she is safely in your arms, she is easier to handle, but she will need plenty of time and patience to learn that people can be trusted.

Koala relies heavily on her kennel friends for confidence and comfort, so she will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can take her under their wing and help her feel more secure. Having a canine friend by her side will be very important as she begins to experience life outside of kennels.

Koala has never lived in a home before, so she will need understanding adopters who can give her the time she needs to settle in and learn about house training. Lead walking may be far too scary for her initially, so she will need a secure garden where she can safely explore, sniff and build her confidence at her own pace.

Koala can live with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16+ who are sensible and understand that she will need plenty of space and patience. Her adopters will need previous ex-breeding experience so they can better understand her needs and help her adjust to life in a home.

Koala is a very frightened girl, but underneath her worries is a little lady who deserves the chance to learn how wonderful life can be. She is looking for someone special who is willing to take a chance on her and give her the time she needs to blossom.

Koala has been given the Gift of Life by Margaret Hunter

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Sunny
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog my size or larger to help me settle in & I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I am learning to walk on a lead and harness, but it's still very new for me.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have an undershot jaw & I have had 4 of my teeth removed during spay!

27-08-26 Sunny is a sweet girl who has come to us from a breeder and is trying her hardest to be brave. She was very briefly adopted, but after a few days in her new home it was clear that her and the resident dog weren't a good match and so she has returned to our care.

Sunny loves other dogs and still looks to her kennel friends for comfort and reassurance, so she will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can look to and lean on as she continues to grow in confidence. She will be best suited to a home where any resident dogs were her size or larger and were fairly confident and well socialised. We think she will settle quickly in the right home, and with patience and encouragement, we’re sure her lovely personality will really begin to shine.

She will be looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace.She can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who are kind and sensible and will give her the time she needs to settle in.She will now happily approach you for a fuss and is easy to handle, which is lovely to see as she begins to settle in and discover the world around her. Sunny arrived with us very matted, but she was such a good girl during her grooming session and took everything in her stride.

Sunny has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be kind and patient as she learns all about home life and new skills like house training. She has started to learn all about walking on a lead and harness and though this is still new to her, she is doing well. Sunny is an amazing lady who has so much to look forward to and will make a wonderful addition to a loving and accepting home.

Sunny has arrived with an undershot jaw that does not seem to bother her, but will need to be monitored in her new home. She has had 4 teeth removed at the time of her spay.

Sunny has been given the Gift of Life by Victoria Charlton

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Maggie
description:
I'd like a quiet, adult-only home to help me relax and feel safe.

I can be an only dog or live with one dog my size or larger.

I'd like a secure garden to play in that has 6ft fencing.

I walk well on a lead and would enjoy one or two walks a day!

I have lived in a home so I know the basics.

I have been spayed and I’m ready for my new home! Read below for more!

Maggie is a very sweet girl who originally came to us from a breeder. She was adopted for around 16 months, but has sadly returned to us from a home following an incident with one of the smaller resident dogs in the home. During the evening, while out in the garden, Maggie was frightened by the other dog barking. Although we don't know exactly what happened, the interaction unfortunately ended in a fight and they struggled to make up or co-exist after this.

Maggie will be looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and where she can settle in at her own pace. Unfortunately on one occasion in her previous home, Maggie became tangled in her harness and in a panic, bit the hand of the male owner who was trying to help free her. This was purely through fear and was an isolated, one off incident, but due to this, Maggie will be looking for an adult only home.

When Maggie first returned to our care, she was a very shy girl who was unsure about new people, but since then she has settled in wonderfully and is an absolute dream. She is a very gentle girl who is so loving and confident, especially with her main carer, who has built such an incredible bond with her in a short period of time.

Maggie is now confident enough that we would consider homing her as an only dog in the right circumstances, with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and who have plenty of time to spend with her and to help her settle in. She could also live with another calm and confident resident dog, but they would need to be her size or larger. She has shared her kennel with quite a few different dogs since being back with us and she has been amazing with all of them and is happy to share food and toys. She even visits the big play yard with a larger group of dogs for a play date, which she really enjoys!

She is a playful girl and likes to keep herself entertained by playing with a tennis ball by herself, which is very sweet to watch! She does also like to run around and play with some of her dog friends too. She is also very food motivated and loves her treats.

As Maggie has previously lived in a home, she will be familiar with home life, but may need some reminders of house training. She can already walk on a lead and harness and will often check back to you for reassurance. She walks well without pulling and is lovely to take out on walks.

Maggie can be worried by men and did initially bark at the male resident in her previous home, but with time, patience, and gentle handling, she slowly began to come around. We are ensuring she socialises with males here and she does have a male staff member as part of her care team and has bonded well with him, which is lovely. She is very people oriented and once she knows you and is comfortable with you, she will become your best friend. She absolutely adores her main carer and will follow her around like a shadow and loves a fuss and cuddle!

Since Maggie has been with us, she has shown that when she feels stressed or overwhelmed, she may try to find a way to escape by climbing. Because of this, she will need a very secure garden with boundaries of at least 6ft to help keep her safe and prevent any potential escape attempts.

Once Maggie knows and trusts someone, she is a very sweet and happy girl. In the right calm and understanding home, with patient and dog-savvy owners who are willing to let her settle at her own pace, we are confident she will continue to make wonderful progress and become the most lovely companion.

Maggie has yet again made some new canine friends here at the rescue, Jinx - Hound and Hayley - Poodle and yet again she has been amazing with them, showing them that us staff here at the rescue are nothing to be feared and helping them understand that a human touch can be loving and kind, she has been incredible with a lot of our scardies and the change you then see in those dogs, a lot of it thanks to Maggie, is amazing, she really is a special girl.I also had to bath her (again) this past week as due to her fur type and the weather she gets dirty rather easily, but, she is so good in the bath, she's very tolerant of the water and being shampooed. When it comes to brushing and drying, she is also easy, for the most part she either just stands or lays there which makes her quicker to dry.She really is a dream dog and she's still waiting for her forever home after almost 5 months. Winter is coming, that means cold days and nights, and although we do everything we can here at the rescue to ensure that they're all comfy and warm, it's nothing compared to the home comforts of being wrapped up in her own blanket, snuggled up with her own family knowing, who wouldn't want that for her?Please consider Maggie, she's one of our most overlooked angels and it genuinely makes me sad that no one seems to take an interest in her. I promise you she'll make an amazing companion and a true best friend just like she is for me while I'm her kennel mum.

Maggie aka Magaluf, Magarita, Mags or Miss Maggie is a special girl. She's the kind of dog that once she's comfortable with you, you instantly feel the love she has for you from her and it's such a lovely feeling, she is very affectionate and loves her people more than anything, well, maybe not more than her food or treats but we're her second favourite.

Maggie's confidence has grown so much these past months that she's even helped some of our more shyer residents come out of their shells, and by them seeing how she is with us makes them realise that they too can be like that with us and have fusses and cuddles etc.

She is an incredible girl and it truly baffles me as to why she keeps getting overlooked. She is beautiful both inside and out and has such a fun personality. She is good with other dogs but won't necessarily need to be rehomed with another dog as we believe that she is confident enough to be an only.

Maggie will become a best friend and a true companion, and I know I'm probably a lot biased being one of her kennel mums but she truly is so so special and anyone would be lucky to have her in their life.

Maggie has settled into rescue life beautifully, but having spent over a year in a home, we are really desperate to get her back into one ASAP!

Since her arrival, Maggie has been kenneled with our lovely Bocker Eddie whom she gets along with wonderfully. She does enjoy her time with him, and would happily live alongside one resident dog - male or female, her size or larger!!

During Maggie’s time here she has formed a wonderful bond with her kennel mums who she absolutely dotes on. She’s even bonded with a kennel dad who has said she’s an absolute sweetheart, and he’s had no trouble with her too, which is so good to hear.

Maggie's kennel mummies describe her as loyal, affectionate, and loving. She really looks to them for reassurance, and when they’re around nothing else matters. Seeing as she’s grown so much in confidence, we’re happy to say she can now also be homed as an only dog too in the circumstance her adopters have lots of time to spend with her!!

Maggie isn’t really too fussed on playing with toys, but what she does love is her food & treats so gaining her trust will be a breeze!

A dog like Maggie is absolutely wasted in kennels, she’s already lived a life at home & we are so desperate to get her back into one!!

Maggie is a sweet Cockapoo who originally came to us from a breeder. She was adopted for around 16 months, but has sadly returned to us from a home following an incident with one of the smaller resident dogs in the home. During the evening, while out in the garden, Maggie was frightened by the other dog barking. Although we don't know exactly what happened, the interaction unfortunately ended in a fight and they struggled to make up or co-exist after this.

Maggie is a very shy and sensitive girl who is wary of strangers, although she does allow handling. She is trying very hard to be brave and is beginning to show small signs of progress, even getting close to taking treats from our hands, though she is not quite confident enough just yet.

Maggie is not yet confident enough to be an only dog, so we feel she would settle best in a home with one calm and confident resident dog of a similar size or larger, who can help her feel safe and reassured as she adjusts.

As Maggie has previously lived in a home, she will be familiar with the sights and sounds of a home environment. However, she may still need some support with house training as she settles into a new routine. Maggie can already walk on a lead, so she would enjoy one or two walks around the local area with the resident dog when she is settled in.

Maggie is particularly worried by men and did initially bark at the male resident in her previous home. With time, patience, and gentle handling, she slowly began to come around. Unfortunately, there was also an incident where Maggie became tangled in her harness and, in a panic, bit the hand of the male owner who was trying to help free her. Because of this, Maggie will need a calm adult-only home with patient and understanding adopters who have experience or understanding of the challenges that can come with rehoming ex-breeding dogs.

Once Maggie knows and trusts someone, she is a very sweet and happy girl. In the right calm and understanding home, with patient and dog-savvy owners who are willing to let her settle at her own pace, we are confident she will continue to make wonderful progress and slowly come out of her shell.

Maggie is currently being treated for an ear infection in the left ear.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Crush
description:
I can live with older children, aged 16+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I can be an only dog or live with other dogs. I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I walk well on a harness and would enjoy one or two walks a day!

I have lived in a home before so know the basics.

I have bilateral nuclear sclerosis. Please read below for more information!

Crush is a sweet gentleman who has come to us from a breeder and is still waiting for his forever home. After spending all his life breeding, he is now finally getting to experience the love and kindness he deserves, and his confidence has truly blossomed during his time with us. He has learned to walk on a lead and is doing so well, showing us just how much he has to offer!

Crush is a lovely, chilled and laid-back boy who gets on wonderfully with other dogs. He gets super excited when meeting new friends out on walks and can turn into a playful pup, which is so lovely to see! He also enjoys a good run around in the yards with his kennel friends before settling down again. Crush can happily live with other resident dogs, and in the right home, we feel he could possibly be an only dog too.

Crush has also been a little star for his bath and groom, happily allowing himself to be scrubbed, blow-dried and even having a little face trim. He really is a fluffy white ball of perfection! He will make a lovely companion for someone looking for a gentle, easygoing boy to share their home with.

Crush has never lived in a home before, so his adopters will need to be patient as he learns about house training and adjusts to a new routine. He could live with dog-savvy teenagers aged 16+ who understand that he may need some time to settle into his new surroundings. With his lovely progress so far, we hope he will continue to grow in confidence and enjoy all the little things that make home life so special.

Crush has bilateral nuclear sclerosis, which will need to be monitored in his new home, although it does not appear to bother him at present. He also has the potential for chronic skin issues and dental disease that will need to be monitored, and he has already had two teeth extracted while with us.

Crush has spent so many years waiting for his chance to be loved, and now we desperately hope someone will see what a wonderful boy he is. He has so much love to give and deserves to spend his golden years enjoying the comforts of a forever home, with a cosy bed, kind people and all the love he has missed out on for so long.

Crush has been given the Gift of Life by Carolina Olsen

How is this sweet gentleman still waiting for his home? At 9 years old, Crush wants nothing more than a place to call home. He’s spent all his years breeding until finally arriving with us where he has been showered with love, met new friends and even to walk lead! His confidence truly has bloomed in the last few months.

He is perfect around other dogs and gets super excited when meeting others out on walks and turns into a playful pup. He’s a very chilled and laid back boy but he does enjoy a good run around in the yards with his friends.

Crush had a bath and groom with me a few days ago and he was perfect. He allowed me to scrub him down and also blow dry him before giving him a little face trim.

The boy truly is a fluffy white ball of perfection!

Crush can live with other resident dogs and in the right home could possibly be an only.

Crush is a fairly nervous boy who has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for a loving forever home. He can be very shy and tends to rely heavily on his kennel friends for comfort and reassurance, so he will need time and patience as he settles into his new surroundings.

Crush will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in the home that he can look to and lean on as he learns about home life and begins to build his confidence. He has never lived in a home before, so his adopters will need to be understanding as he learns all about house training and adjusts to a new routine.

Crush is walking well on a harness, so he would enjoy one or two walks around the local area with the resident dog when he is settled in.

He could live with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16+ who understand that he will need plenty of time and space to settle in and begin to trust. Crush is a lovely boy who simply needs plenty of TLC, patience, and kindness as he finds his paws in the world.

He has come to us with bilateral nuclear sclerosis that will need to be monitored in his new home, and does not seem to bother him at this time. The vet has noted that he has a potential for chronic skin issues and dental disease that will need to be monitored in his new home. He has had two teeth extracted with us.

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Jules
description:
I can live with older children, aged 16+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I will need a kind resident dog in my new home. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I haven't tried walks just yet and will find this a bit overwhelming at the moment.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have had 32 teeth removed and will need a soft food diet.

21-09-26 Jules has come to us from a breeder to start her new adventure. She is a very nervous girl who is feeling overwhelmed by all the changes in her world. She is unsure of people and worried about being handled, so will initially run away and hide. She is a sweet girl underneath her worries, and we hope that with kindness, reassurance and time, she will slowly learn that people can be trusted.

Jules will be looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and understand that she will need to settle in completely at her own pace. We would consider a home with gentle, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16+ who can give her the space and patience she needs.

Jules will need a kind and confident resident dog in her new home to take her under their wing and help her feel safe as she adjusts to home life. Having a canine friend to learn from will be important for Jules as she begins to build her confidence and discover that the world isn't such a scary place.

Jules has never lived in a home before, so she will need kind and patient adopters as she learns all about home life and new skills like house training. She will also need to learn about walking on a lead and harness, starting with gentle practice around the garden and gradually building her confidence.

Jules is a sweet girl who has so much potential, and in the right home, we hope she will truly thrive. With patience, understanding and the support of a confident canine companion, she can begin to feel safe and discover just how wonderful life can be.

Our vets have noted that Jules has ectropion affecting her lower eyelids, which has been assessed but required no treatment. She has had 32 teeth removed at the time of her spay and will need a soft food diet moving forwards.

Jules has been given the Gift of Life by Susan Stacey

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Pop
description:
I can live with older, dog-savvy kids aged 13+ who love cuddles, and are active!

I will need to be the only pet in my new home, so all of the attention is on me!

I would like a secure garden where I can have plenty of play time!

I am very active and will need a home that will take me on plenty of adventures!

I may have previously lived in a home, so I may already know the basics.

I have been spayed and am ready to find my forever home!

Pop is a fantastic little lady who has come to us from a breeder, although we have been told she has lived in a home previously. She knows her name and responds to “Pop”, so her new family will need to keep this name.

Pop is full of love, character and energy. She can be a little timid when first meeting new people, but it doesn't take her long to warm up. Once she knows you, she absolutely loves cuddles, enjoys giving kisses and thrives on human company. She has a very affectionate nature and loves being involved in whatever her people are doing.

As an active Jack Russell Terrier x Collie, Pop is looking for a home that can provide plenty of physical exercise and mental enrichment to keep her clever little brain busy. She is a quick learner who has mastered “sit” and is currently learning “touch”. She picks things up quickly, which is helping with her ongoing muzzle training.

Pop walks beautifully on her harness and would happily walk for miles, so she will need an active home that enjoys getting out and about and helping her learn new things. She is doing well with her training and is now walking alongside calm dogs, which is lovely progress. However, she is not yet comfortable wearing a muzzle for long periods, and we are continuing to build her confidence with this gradually. The aim is to help her become comfortable wearing one when needed, so she can be kept safe around other dogs in busier areas in the future. At the rescue, under supervision with her surroundings managed, she is enjoying muzzle free play time with Lassie so it is possible she will not always need a muzzle for mixing with her canine friends.

Pop will need to be the only dog in her new home. Although she is making progress with carefully managed walks alongside calm dogs, she can still become reactive when she feels overwhelmed. Her adopters will need to be experienced, understanding and committed to continuing her positive, reward-based training to help her feel more comfortable around dogs when out and about.

As Pop has previously lived in a home, we think she is likely to know many of the basics, although she may need a few reminders as she settles into a new routine. She could live with sensible, dog-savvy children aged 13 years and over but will need a home without cats.

Pop is a wonderful little dog with so much love to give. With patient, experienced adopters who can provide the active lifestyle, ongoing training and consistency she needs, she will make a fantastic, loyal and loving companion.

Pops is such a beautiful, smart girl who is super friendly with people. She has just mastered "sit" and is currently learning "touch". She picks things up pretty quickly, which is also helping her with her muzzle training.

Pops isn't sociable with other dogs currently, but this is something we're working on by taking her on walks with calm dogs at a distance. Once she is happily muzzle trained, we will work up to safe mixes with dogs who are a good match.

She does need to be an only dog in the home, and her people will need to keep up the training we've put in place to help her feel more comfortable around other dogs when out and about in public.

She walks absolutely beautifully on her harness and would happily walk for miles and miles, so she will need an active home who enjoys helping their dog feel happier and learn new things.

Pop is a fantastic little lady who has come to us from a breeder, although we have been told she has lived in a home previously. She knows her name and responds to "Pop", so her new family will need to keep this name.

Pop is a wonderful little girl who is full of love, character and energy. She can be a little timid when first meeting new people, but it doesn't take her long to warm up. Once she knows you, she absolutely loves cuddles, enjoys giving kisses and thrives on human company. She has a very affectionate, sweet nature and loves being involved in whatever her people are doing.

As an active Jack Russell Terrier x Collie, Pop is looking for a home that can provide plenty of physical exercise as well as mental enrichment to keep her clever little brain busy. She is doing well with her lead walking and enjoys getting out and about, but she will need owners who are committed to continuing her training and helping her build confidence.

Pop will need to be the only dog in her new home. Whilst she can walk past some dogs, she is worried by them and can become reactive on lead, making the wrong choices when she feels overwhelmed. Her adopters will need to be experienced, understanding and willing to continue working on her doggy social skills using positive, reward-based training. We have already started muzzle training with Pop to help build her confidence, with the hope that, in time, she may be able to enjoy controlled walks alongside calm canine companions.

As Pop has previously lived in a home, we think she is likely to know many of the basics, although she may need a few reminders as she settles into a new routine.

She could live with sensible, dog-savvy children aged 13 years and over but will need a home without cats.

Pop is a truly wonderful little dog with so much love to give. With patient, experienced adopters who can provide the active lifestyle and ongoing training she needs, she will make a fantastic, loyal and loving companion.

Pop has been making really good progress and has even made a friend here that she mixes with unmuzzled, she seems to enjoy a little bit of a play but then needs to have a little pause during some play dates when her friend gets a little bit too playful and overwhelms her. After a couple of minute of calm she will happily play again but it's important that her new people don't rush her with her socialisation, and instead, just take it at a pace that Pop is happy and comfortable with. She is very good at communicating when she's feeling a bit overwhelmed so you just have to listen to her and take her out of the stressful situation.

We are still muzzle training her to help her with her doggy social skills, this is very much a work-in-progress as we want her to be 100% happy with one step before moving on to the next, but I am very proud of her for reaching the stage of putting her nose in on queue and holding it there for a few seconds before getting more tasty paste.

In general she is such a happy ball of energy who just wants someone who will take her on adventures and truly be her best friend.

Pop can be homed with dog-savvy teens but they must be understanding of her getting a little mouthy when over-excited and although this is something that she is improving on, we don't want her new adopters to be worried by this behaviour if it were to happen in the home. We ignore it and reward her for being calm, which is all it usually takes for her to stop and then we continue with something fun, she also will usually grab a toy when excited in her kennel, so we are in the process of teaching her to do this on command to help her know where to place all that excited energy safely.

I can see her making a family incredibly happy, she really does have so much to offer the right home.

name: Buck
description:
I would like an adult-only home that can understand my needs!

I would like to be the only dog in my new home.

I would like a secure garden with 6ft+ fences.

I can walk well on a harness and would love an active home.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have no tail and have been treated for a ear infection.

Please meet the very handsome Buck, who has travelled all the way from Romania in the hope of finding his forever home. Since arriving here a few months ago, Buck has truly blossomed! Initially a little shy with new people, he now settles quickly and happily shows off his affectionate, gentle nature. He loves attention, enjoys fuss, and is more than happy to make new friends once he feels comfortable.

Buck is such a comical boy, always finding little ways to make you smile, but he is also incredibly affectionate. He has that spark of energy that brightens even the hardest of days.

Buck absolutely loves his food. You’ll hear his excited bark echo around the rescue at mealtimes without fail. He also really enjoys his walks and having a good run around the big yard, where he can let out all that happy energy. Buck also has the most cuddly side to him; he loves nothing more than resting his head on your lap while he slowly dozes off to sleep.

Buck was briefly adopted but was sadly returned as he didn't get along with the resident dog and we believe that we would do best as the only dog in the home. He can get a little jealous of sharing attention with another dog in the home, but he mixes well out and about as long as he is supervised.

Buck will be looking for an adult only home and would be best suited to adopters who have experience of owning dogs from a similar background before and who are around most of the time, so they can spend lots of time with him. He would love to find an active home where he can be kept both physically and mentally stimulated and enjoy plenty of walks and adventures with his new family.

Although Buck had never lived in a home before being adopted, he settled in wonderfully and was clean in the house. He wasn’t phased by the TV or radio and quickly found the sofas and beds! He can still be a little shy when first meeting men, but it doesn’t take him long to warm up. Buck also isn’t keen on sudden loud noises or sticks and brooms, so this is something his adopters will need to work on desensitising him to. He doesn’t like having his front paws touched, but he will politely let you know by gently pulling them away.

Buck is a truly special boy with so much love to give. He is absolutely wasted in kennels and will make a loyal, devoted companion for a very lucky family. He arrived with no tail, but this doesn’t bother him in the slightest and only adds to his charm. Please don’t overlook this wonderful lad, as Buck is more than ready to find his forever home.

Buck has received negative test results for Brucellosis, Leishmania, Giardia, Heartworm, Ehrlichia canis, Borrelia burgdorferi and Anaplasma.

Buck will need more than one meet and greet with his prospective adopters to allow him time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

In just 73 days time, my darling Buck will reach his one year anniversary with us at Many tears and no matter how much I love Buck with my entire heart, I would love nothing more than for him to be in a home to call his own before he reaches the one year mark!

Buck is quite honestly one of the most loveable, loyal boys to the people he knows and trusts. Once you’ve built that special bond with him, you get to see just how much love this boy has to give.

Recently, I’ve been spending some extra time with Buck by bringing him into the cabin with me during my night shifts, and it really does show how much love he has to give.

There is something so special about getting to know a dog like Buck, watching him feel comfortable in your company and seeing more of his beautiful personality shine through.

Buck may need a little time and patience to let you into his world, but I promise you that the bond you build with him will be worth every second, he truly is the most special boy!

253 days of Buck waking up in a kennel, waiting for the day his person finds him!

Buck isn’t the sort of dog who instantly shows you everything he has to give. He needs time. He needs patience. He needs someone who is willing to sit beside him and let him learn that they’re safe.

But when he trusts you, you get to see the funniest, silliest, most loving boy hiding underneath all those initial nerves. You get to see his personality come alive, and there is honestly no better feeling than knowing he finally feels safe enough to be himself, I just wish everyone else could see the Buck that I see.

Because I know, without a doubt, that someone out there is going to absolutely adore this boy. Someone is going to give him the time he needs, and in return, they’ll get a friend who will love them with his whole heart, but until that person finds him, I’ll keep loving him and reminding him every day that he matters!

Buck is truly the most special dog in the world, I love spending my days caring for him and preparing him for home life, but I would love it even more, to be seeing updates of him in a home.

Buck has now been with us for 7 months and is still patiently waiting for his forever home.

Buck absolutely loves the people he knows and trusts. If Buck is unsure of someone, it will take him awhile to come out of his shell and get to know them, but once they've built a bond with him, he is the most loving gentle boy, who loves attention!

Buck has plenty of doggy friends and enjoys socialising outside of his kennel environment, although he definitely has a preference for the ladies and gets on best with female dogs.

Buck can potentially live with another calm female dog who will respect his space when he needs it.

Buck is looking for an adopters who will give him the time he needs to settle and understand that he can be a very worried boy at first.

I do genuinely love Buck with my entire heart. I would love nothing more than seeing him finally settling into home life, with people who will cherish him just as much as I do!

For the past few weeks, Buck has been front and centre in our big yard play group! This is a great chance for our people-shy new dogs to meet and play with more confident long-stayers like Buck, and he's met a lot of new dogs this way, which suggests that once he's settled into his new home, he might benefit from a dog park or opportunities to meet up with friends.

Buck's best friend is another Romanian dog called Olive. You rarely see one without the other, in their yard, the big yard, or on walks! Sometimes in big yard play group, Bucky and Olive will separate from the other dogs and chase and wrestle each other for a while, and it's lovely to see. Unfortunately, Buck and Olive don't like to be kenneled together as they prefer their own space to unwind after all that time spent playing.

However, Buck has really come out of his shell with people around the rescue. He has a few people he's very close to, and is always up for cwtches with them. How can you say no that handsome face? He's also happier now to meet new people than he used to be, and now goes on walks with volunteers (accompanied, of course, by Olive) most days.

Buck can still get possessive over his favourite people, which is something we have to be aware of in big yard play group and that his adopters will need to bear in mind. He may grumble at other dogs in warning if they get too close when he's having his cuddles, though this does not usually escalate beyond a warning snap. It's likely that our sweet Bucky may not have had stable affection in his past, so he feels the need to guard that love from other dogs.

Luckily for Buck, we have plenty of love to go around at Many Tears! Hopefully, as he settles, he'll realise he is safe and loved and doesn't have to guard anyone anymore.

I’ve had the absolute pleasure of working with Buck, or “Buckaroo” as I like to call him, since the very day he arrived with us. I know you’re not supposed to have favourites, but if I’m honest, Buck has completely stolen a place in my heart.

Buck is such a comical boy, always finding little ways to make you smile, but he is also incredibly affectionate. He has that spark of energy that can turn even the hardest days into better ones.

Buck’s kennel friend, who he came over from Romania with, has recently been adopted. He adored her so much, and since she left, there’s been a little piece of him missing. Now he is the one still waiting, and it is heartbreaking knowing he doesn’t understand why it is not his turn yet.

Although Buck has shared his kennel and enjoys playdates with other dogs, always greeting them nicely out on walks, he would also thrive as the only dog in a home. He loves human attention so deeply and would really benefit from having people around most of the time to give him the love, comfort, and reassurance he deserves.

I recently took Buck out for a day to a local beach. From the moment we arrived, he was in his absolute element and enjoyed every second of it. Buck spent the majority of the time on a long line; although he ran around and explored, he also came back to me when called and always turned to make sure I was still close. This just shows how much of a loyal companion he can be.

I honestly love Buck with my whole heart, and it breaks me a little every single day knowing he is still waiting for his people to come for him. He has so much love, loyalty, and joy to give; he just needs someone to give him that chance.

It’s been a few weeks since Bucks arrival, and oh my has he made his presence known. Every single staff member who has had the pleasure of meeting this boy is utterly obsessed, and it’s very clear as to why!

Buck’s energy is infectious, he is the happiest, bounciest, most adoring little man and whoever adopts him will be truly lucky!!! When you meet him you’d never assume he is 6 years old - he exudes puppy energy.

Buck loves to play with his fellow Romanian buddy Jenny and they get along great. He also goes for play dates with the lovely Orietta, and he thoroughly enjoys it. He would like adopters who have experience with owning dogs before and who are around most of the time.

This sweet sweet boy is absolutely wasted in kennels, he is bursting with love to give and he’ll make a very lucky someone the happiest person in the world. Our foreign dogs are often overlooked and tend to hang around in kennels much longer than needed - please don’t let this be the case for our lovely Buck.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Tummy
description:
I could live with dog-savvy teenagers, aged 13+ who respect my space.

I will need to be the only dog in the home so all of the attention is on me!

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I walk well on a lead and would enjoy one or two walks a day!

I have previously lived in a home, so I may already know the basics!

I am on a special diet for bladder stones, please read below for more information!

11-10-26 Tummy is a lovely lady who originally came to us from a breeder and was later adopted into a home. Sadly, she has returned to our care after around 5 months as she wasn't getting along with the resident dog, so she is now looking for a home where she can be the only dog and have all of her family's attention to herself. She also cannot live with cats or small furries.

Tummy is a sweet and outgoing girl with a big personality! She loves toys and having a good play, but she also enjoys a quiet fuss and relaxing alongside her people. She has lived in a home before, so she may already know some of the basics such as house training, although she may need a few gentle reminders as she settles back into home life.

Tummy would do best with a family who has experience with Dachshunds and understands their wonderful but sometimes strong personalities, although she could also live with a sensible family who are willing to learn and understand her needs. She can live with dog-savvy teenagers aged 13+ who are sensible and will give her the time and space she needs to settle into her new home.

Tummy has never been left home alone before and so this is something her adopters will need to build up gradually with her to ensure she doesn't develop separation anxiety.

Tummy is an amazing little lady who has already had a change of home and is now ready to find her forever family. We hope that the right home will give her the love, attention and stability she deserves.

Tummy has previously been treated for ear infections and also has some hair loss that seemed to begin to grow back when she was in her previous home. She has a history of bladder stones and is currently on a specific diet to help with this, and this will need to be continued in the home. This will need to be monitored by her new vets and her adopters will need to be aware that should she require any treatment or potential surgery in the future it would not be covered by insurance.

Hungry has been given the Gift of Life by Jacqueline Wanstall

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

name: Milo
description:
I will need an adult-only home that understands me.

I will need to be the only dog in my new home, so all of the attention is on me!

I will need an extra secure garden, at least 6ft+ where I will be safe!

I walk well on a lead but will need my adopters to be understanding of my needs!

I have lived in a home before so may I may already know the basics.

I will be neutered before finding my forever home!

06-10-26 Milo is a super sweet boy who has come to us from a home through no fault of his own. Sadly, he has already been through more changes than a young dog should have to, and he is understandably a little worried in new environments. He takes a lot of comfort from people he knows, but once he feels comfortable, his fun and affectionate personality really starts to shine.

Milo is an incredibly sweet boy who absolutely loves being close to his people and thinks he is the perfect lap dog! He is happiest when he can have a cuddle and will happily climb up for a lap sit. He is a sensitive little soul and will need a kind and patient home where he can continue to build his confidence and learn that he is safe and secure.

Milo will be looking for a home where he can be the only dog and get all the fuss and attention for himself. We are told that he has had a previous incident with a cat and so he cannot be homed with cats or small furries and must be kept on lead unless in a secure area.

Milo has missed out on some socialisation, but he is currently working on his social skills and is making lovely progress. He can happily walk alongside calm dogs and has had some nice greetings. He doesn't always know what to make of other dogs yet and can sometimes get a little carried away when mixing, but with continued positive socialisation we are sure his confidence will grow. He can also react if another dog barks at him first while on lead, so his new family will need to understand this and help him learn how to navigate these situations.

Milo will need an adult-only home with people who have experience of bull breeds and understand what sensitive souls they can be.Although he is a wonderful boy, he would not be suitable for a first time dog owner.He will need a kind and patient family who can give him time to settle and continue building his confidence. He will also need the time he is left home alone built up gradually as he settles into his new home.

Milo will need an extra secure garden of at least 6ft to keep him safe, as he is a young and active boy who could be an escape artist if given the opportunity.

Milo is such a lovely young boy who has already been through so much change. With the right family, patience and continued socialisation, we know he will make a wonderful companion and be the loving, fun little lap dog he is so desperate to be.

name: Tucker
description:
I can live with older children, aged 13+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before

02-10-26 Tucker is a calm and quiet boy who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. He is an easy boy to pick up and handle and enjoys a gentle fuss. Tucker is currently kennelled with another male as he is quite an amorous boy, but we think he would also be fine to be homed with a suitable female, who could provide him with some companionship and reassurance as he settles into his new home.

As Tucker has never lived in a home before, he will need to learn all about house training, lead training and the other basics of home life. His new family will need to give him time and patience while he gets used to his new surroundings. He can live with dog-savvy teens, aged 13+ who are sensible and will allow him time to settle in.

Tucker has a Grade 3 heart murmur and is currently underweight. He also has bilateral cataracts and will need a dental, which is to be expected given his older age. His adopters will need to be prepared for any ongoing care and monitoring that may be recommended.

Tucker would love a calm and quiet home where he can enjoy a slower pace of life, with a warm and comfy bed to curl up in and all the creature comforts he deserves. We hope he can find a loving family who will give this gentle old boy the chance to retire in comfort and enjoy his well-earned home comforts.

Tucker has been given the Gift of Life by Shirley Bourne

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Dutch
description:
I could live with dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who respect my space.

I need to be the only dog in my new home. No cats please!

I walk well on a lead and muzzle trained. I would enjoy an active lifestyle!

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before.

I am already vaccinated and neutered and ready for my new home!

Dutch is an incredible boy who has come into our care from a pound in Ireland in search of a fresh start. Unfortunately, we don't know much about his history, but what we do know is that he is one of the most loving and affectionate dogs you could ever hope to meet, with a heart as big as his personality. Dutch simply wants to be close to his people, whether that's following you around, leaning into you for fuss, or curling up beside you for cuddles. Being with the people he loves is all he really wants.

Dutch would love to find a home with adopters who are around for most of the day and can include him in everyday life. He thrives on human companionship and will make a wonderfully devoted shadow to his new family. He will need adopters who have experience with similar breeds and understand typical breed traits, including prey drive and the need for appropriate mental and physical enrichment.

Dutch would be best suited to life as an only dog. Although he can socialise well with other dogs of a similar size, he can become overexcited and mouthy, which may lead to frustration. Because of this, he is muzzle trained and wears a muzzle during social interactions to help him continue building positive experiences. He cannot live with cats or small furries.

As Dutch has never lived in a home before, he will need support with house training and learning the general routines of family life. He is such a clever boy and always tries his very best to do the right thing, so we are confident he will enjoy learning with patient, positive guidance.

Dutch already walks well on a lead, although he can occasionally be reactive when passing other kennels. This is understandable in a busy rescue environment and may be something his adopters will need to continue working on. He is an energetic, happy-go-lucky boy who is more than ready to start exploring the world with his new family. An active home where he can enjoy plenty of walks, enrichment, training and quality time with his people would suit him perfectly.

Dutch could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers who can appreciate that he will need a gentle introduction to his new surroundings and his own space to settle in.

Dutch is bright, affectionate and full of love. He has so much to offer and is simply looking for someone to love as much as he loves them. For the right family, he will be an incredibly loyal, fun-loving and devoted companion.

Dutch has a passport and travel document.

Dutch has been given the Gift of Life by Louise Southward

I still can’t quite understand how this incredibly smart and loving boy hasn’t found his forever home yet.If you’re looking for a dog to train, learn new tricks and go on lots of adventures with, then Dutch really is your boy.He’s the best of both worlds a crazy, energetic boy who also absolutely loves his people and loves nothing more than a good snuggle.

Dutch, or as I like to call him, Dutchy, is honestly one of the most loving and affectionate boys you could ever hope to meet.

He's the kind of dog who just wants to be close to you. Whether it's following you around, leaning into you for fuss, or curling up for cuddles, being with his people is all he really wants. Watching him have to go back into his kennel after spending time together is heartbreaking because kennel life is just no place for a boy like him.

What makes it even sadder is that he hasn't received a single application. If I'm honest, my biggest worry is that he'll become one of our long-stay dogs, and my heart breaks at the thought of that because he simply doesn't deserve it.

He's such a clever boy and always tries so hard to do the right thing. He recently went on his first long walk with one of our wonderful regular volunteers and was an absolute angel. He took everything in his stride and made everyone so proud.

He's also been having play dates with our lovely girl, Swanny, to help him burn off some of that doggy energy while learning good doggy manners.

At the end of the day, Dutchy is just a baby. He's got the biggest heart, so much love to give, and he deserves a home where he'll be someone's whole world instead of waiting behind kennel doors. I know his family is out there somewhere; I just hope they find him before he spends another day wondering why no one has chosen him.

Dutch is an incredible boy who has come into our care from a pound in Ireland in search of a fresh start. Unfortunately, we don't know much about his history, but what we do know is that he is one of the most loving and affectionate dogs you could ever hope to meet.

He would love to find a loving home with adopters who are around most of the time and would have plenty of time to spend with him. He would need adopters who have experience with similar breeds and experience with his typical breed traits like prey drive etc.

Dutch would be best suited to being homed as an only dog as although he does socialise well with other dogs of his size, he can become over excited and mouthy which can lead to frustration. For this reason he is being trained to wear a muzzle when socialising. He cannot be homed with cats or small furries.

As Dutch has never lived in a home before, he will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. With patience and guidance, we think he will adapt well and enjoy all the comforts a home has to offer.

Dutch can already walk well on a lead, though he can be a little reactive when passing other kennels, this is understandable in a busy rescue environment, but may be something his adopters will need to work with him on. He is an energetic and incredibly lovely bo who ie is happy-go-lucky in nature and is more than ready to start adventuring with his new adopters. He would love an active home where he can enjoy plenty of walks, enrichment, and quality time with his people.

Dutch could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers who can appreciate and understand that he will need a gentle and quiet introduction to the home, along with his own space to settle in.

He is a bright, affectionate, and fun-loving boy who is sure to make a wonderful and loyal companion for a lucky family.

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

name: Lollipop
description:
I could live with dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 +, who respect my space.

I need a doggy friend in my new home and would prefer a male dog. I don't mind cats!

I'm new to lead walking and need some practice!

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I have a grade 2 luxating patella and have had 7 teeth extracted. Read below for more

Lollipop is a lovely Bichon Frise who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. She is an inquisitive and funny little girl who is already showing glimpses of her playful personality. Lollipop will happily come over to lick our fingers before darting away again, as if she's still deciding whether people are quite as interesting as her kennel friends.

Lollipop is still a nervous little girl, but she has been making lovely progress and is gradually becoming more curious about the people around her. The more time you spend with her, the more interested she becomes in you, and it is lovely to see her slowly coming out of her shell.

Lollipop loves the company of other dogs and relies heavily on them for comfort and reassurance. She is happy to follow their lead and takes great confidence from having another dog around. For this reason, she will need to have a resident dog in her new home. She will be looking for a home with a male resident dog as she can sometimes be a little sassy with female dogs.

Lollipop has also been making lovely progress with her harness training. She is easy to put her harness on and recently went out for her very first walk. Considering how nervous she can be, she did incredibly well! She will need plenty more gentle practice to help her become confident and comfortable with walking, and her adopters will need to continue this at her own pace.

As Lollipop has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. Her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she adjusts to a whole new world and gains confidence in her surroundings.

Lollipop could share her home with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over who can appreciate and understand that she will need a gentle, quiet introduction to the home and her own space to settle in.

She has arrived with a Grade 2 luxating patella, but her mobility appears unaffected and this may improve as she builds muscle tone. Lollipop has also arrived with severe periodontal disease and has had seven teeth extracted.

Lollipop is an active and spritely little girl with a bright future ahead of her. With the support of a kind canine friend and a patient family, we hope her confidence will continue to grow and her charming personality will shine through even more.

Lollipop has been given the Gift of Life by Jodie Stanley

Lollipop is a lovely lady, she’s doing ever so well here and making great progress in confidence. She loves going out for a stroll or bouncing around with her friends in our yards. Lollipop also loves to sunbath as seen in her photos.

Lollipop still has a way to go in terms of confidence with humans and is looking for a gentle adult only home with where there will be a doggie (male as she can be a little sassy with female dogs)  companion. Lollipop really is a sweet, funny and  gentle lady, and so ready for a proper home.

Lollipop has been making lovely progress with her harness training. Today, she went out for her very first walk and, considering she is still quite a nervous girl, she did incredibly well. She is easy to put her harness on, but she will need plenty more practice to help her become confident and comfortable with walking.

Lollipop relies heavily on her kennel friends for reassurance, so she will need a kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help her settle into family life. The more time you spend with her, the more curious she becomes about you, and it is lovely to see her gradually coming out of her shell.

She definitely prefers the company of other dogs at the moment, but she is happy to follow their lead and takes great comfort from having them around. As Lollipop gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends, she will need a kind resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws.

As Lollipop has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training, and the other basics of home life. Her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she adjusts to a whole new world and gains confidence in her surroundings.

Lollipop could share her home with older dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over who can appreciate and understand that she will need a gentle, quiet introduction to the home and her own space to settle in.

She has arrived with a Grade 2 luxating patella but her mobility appears unaffected and this may improve as she builds muscle tone. Lollipop has also arrived with severe periodontal disease and has had 7 teeth extracted.

Lollipop is an active and spritely little girl with a bright future ahead of her. With the support of a canine friend and a patient family, we hope her confidence will continue to grow and her charming personality will shine through even more.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Flash
description:
I would like to be the only animal in my new home.

I would like a good sized, secure garden to explore.

I can walk on a lead but find this very overwhelming at the moment.

I have entropion in both eyes, which have been repaired by the vets.

Flash is a truly striking Standard Poodle with a big personality, a sensitive soul, and an oversized puppy spirit. He first came to us after his previous owners could no longer give him the time and exercise he needed. Since then, we’ve watched him grow from a worried boy into a much more confident and affectionate companion, and he continues to make us proud every single day.

Flash is still very much a character, goofy, playful, and full of energy but beneath his bouncy exterior lies a gentle heart that just wants to love and be loved. He can be sensitive in new situations and still finds the world a little overwhelming at times, but with people he trusts, his sweet and loyal nature shines through. Once Flash bonds with you, he is yours for life.

Recently, he’s been showing us more of his loving side. On rainy days when we huddle together out of the downpour, he rolls over for belly rubs, brings his toys for attention, and happily drifts off to sleep during a cuddle. It’s in these quiet moments that his true personality comes out, affectionate, trusting, and eager to please.

Flash’s training is going from strength to strength. He’s mastered “touch” (booping his nose to your hand) and is now learning “place.” He still gets a little mouthy when he’s overexcited, but he’s come a long way since his arrival and continues to improve with patience and consistency. He’ll need his future family to have ex-breeding experience and to continue this gentle guidance in the home so he can keep building on all the progress he’s made.

Being an active breed, Flash loves his walks and enjoys exploring the world at his own pace. He’s happiest in calm, quiet areas where he can relax and take everything in without feeling rushed. He will need to be the only pet in the home, as he prefers human companionship over other animals, and he’s not a fan of pigeons or seagulls either!

Flash has had successful surgery for entropion in both eyes, he received care for mild dermatitis around both eyes, but this has since cleared. He is currently being treated for sore and sensitive ears.

What Flash truly needs now is a calm, understanding, adult-only home with rescue experience and with someone who’s around most of the time, someone who can offer him patience, structure, and all the love he deserves. With time and trust, Flash will repay his person a hundred times over with loyalty, affection, and that special spark that makes him so unforgettable.

Please don’t overlook this beautiful boy. Flash has come so far and is ready to start the next chapter of his life he’s just waiting for that one person to believe in him and bring him home.

Flash will need more than one meet and greet with his prospective adopters to allow him time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

Flash recently spent 3 nights in a home environment & did INCREDIBLY well!He got along brilliantly with our 11-year-old female dog and was very respectful around our two cats. After  initial excitement, he simply wanted to have a sniff, say hello and then settled around them really nicely.Flash absolutely loved being out on his walks. He passed other dogs calmly and only showed a little excitable frustration around a puppy because he just wanted to play!His lead manners were also great, walking nicely to heel for most of the walk. The only time he got a little eager and pulled was when he realised we were heading towards the beach — which quickly became one of his favourite places!We also took him to a secure field where he had a brilliant time running around freely with our resident dog, where we practiced some recall which looked promising!Back at home, Flash was calm, affectionate and loved nothing more than a cuddle on the sofa, with the occasional cue to play with our dog.He was 100% clean in the house without a single accident too!Although Flash can appear reactive in the rescue environment, his time in a home showed a very different side to him. He was calm, well-behaved, super affectionate and a pleasure to have around.These three nights gave us a lovely glimpse of the dog he could be, once settled into the right home

Flash has officially been waiting for a home for a whole year. After a first few months of (a lot of) patience and training, it's then blossomed into the most incredible remaining months where we’ve really seen Flash’s true heart and soul. This dog is phenomenal in more ways than one, and it’s so sad he’s now become part of the MT furniture, and that the rescue has now become his home.

So for Flash’s 1 year anniversary, I took him off site to the nearby country park for a lovely stroll, followed by a visit to McD’s for some chicken nuggets.

Flash was suuuuuuch a good boy on his walk. He took in all the new smells, and took the new environment in his stride. He was even approached by 3 off lead small dogs, and didn’t react at all. He trotted along the park, with the world at his feet and it was the most amazing thing to see.

He is an absolute darling in the car, so we made a swift visit to McD’s for a box of 20 nuggets to eat together in our on site flat.

It was so nice to see Flash in a home like environment, he jumped straight on the sofa, and wandered around inspecting every room. We sat on the floor together eating our nuggets, and he eventually rested on the raised bed and had a little snooze.

It was heartbreaking putting him back in his kennel, when he seemed so at peace and settled in the flat. I just wish there was someone out there who could see him for everything he is and more!!!

Our beautiful, bonkers Flash has learnt a new trick and we thought we would share.

Flash has also been enjoying the sunshine with lots of walks and plays in the yards this week.

Flash continues to work hard on growing his calmness around new people and he is doing ok. He has now been 10 months here at the rescue and has an increasing fan base amongst the staff but he of course longs for a home and people of his own.

When I first started working with him, I was apprehensive. He was a much larger dog than I was used to working with, and he would mouth you til his hearts content. Not because he is a nasty dog, or means any harm whatsoever, but simply because he has come from a home (just out of puppyhood) and he has become extremely anxious and unsettled being in a kennel environment. On top of that, he has been taught 0 manners which definitely didn’t help with the matter!!! I struggled to bond with him, I struggled to understand why he wouldn’t listen when being told, and why all he wanted to do was treat my arm like a toy…

However I found myself thinking, what has Flash been through in his life that was ever HIS fault? He didn’t ask to spend so much of his life in kennels. He never asked to be put in situations where his anxiety gets the better of him, it was never his decision to not be trained to behave normally. So I decided to buck up my ideas and realise he’s not as scary as he seems, and he’s probably just as anxious being around me as I was him. And from that moment on, our relationship has blossomed…

This boy is truly a superstar in every sense of the word. He is SUCH a goofball, and can have you in fits of laughter within seconds of being with him. His personality is infectious, and as soon as he is comfortable with you and realises you are no threat to him, he shines like the star he is. It’s gutting that Flash doesn’t allow every staff member to see all sides of him. The side that shows his softness, his sweetness, his kindness. But that just makes me so much more grateful that he feels comfortable enough around me to do so.

You can see from his pictures, Flash is muzzle trained. Not because he is an aggressive dog, not because he is a violent dog, it’s simply due to his anxiousness. On one hand, Flash is a super intelligent Poodle but on the other hand, he doesn’t really show it. His anxiety gets the better of him, and he puts himself in uncomfortable positions with new people & then panics whilst he’s in it. It is SUPER important that whoever adopts Flash’s main priority is keeping him safe, and keeping him from making decisions that he feels uncertain about. He wants to make friends with everyone, but also decides halfway through some interactions that he’s not to keen on the thought too!

Among (of course) all of the other precious angels I look after the rescue, Flash is one of the reasons I get excited to go to work. You shouldn’t really have favourites, but Flash does take the cake. I cherish every single moment I get with him. Our lovely strolls up the country lanes, our snuggles in the back of his kennel after a long day, our zoomies down our big play yard. Every single moment & memory I look forward to recreating every single day. Nothing tops being around this dog, nothing else matters when you’re with Flash.

If I was in a position to take him home & work with him through his quirks, I absolutely would, in heartbeat in fact. There is just something so special about him, and I truly envy whoever is fortunate to adopt this incredible young man. And for as long as Flash remains in kennels, I will advocate for him, make him feel safe, comfortable and most of all loved.

Flash has completely changed my mind about Poodles. I am absolutely in love with him. He might not be the sharpest boy in the bunch, but he more than makes up for it with his goofy charm and endless silliness.We are still working on his mouthing when he becomes overexcited. Progress is steady, and every small step forward feels like a real achievement. Flash loves his freedom. We take daily trips to the big yard where he runs around like the happiest whirlwind you have ever seen. He would really benefit from visits to private dog fields where he can safely zoom and explore to his heart’s content.Meeting new people can still be a little tricky for him, but we have a careful plan in place to help him do so safely and comfortably. For those of us who know Flash well, he shows a side many would not expect. Beneath his anxiousness and the need for a muzzle at times is the sweetest, softest boy who adores snuggles and head tickles.He loves to stay close, gently resting his head in your lap until he drifts off to sleep. At the end of each day, we share a quiet moment together, curled up side by side until his eyes close and he is peacefully dreaming.Flash truly is a special boy who deserves a very special home. He needs someone who can offer love, patience, and understanding. In return, he will give unwavering loyalty and companionship for life.

Flash is an absolute character, this boy is full of life and once he knows you he adores you but his introductions to new people always need to be slow as this sensitive boy can be easily overwhelmed.

Flash works well within a routine, he has an abundance of energy and a super inquisitive nature which can sometimes lead to him becoming quite lively, he will often revert to ‘mouthing’ and jumping up when he is uncomfortable or unsure.

Flash has a super inquisitive nature and loves to observe what’s going on at a distance. This boy can also be an absolute cuddle monster and adores a snuggle with his favourite people, and will fall asleep next to us when we have the opportunity to sit quietly with him. One of flash’s unique traits is his love of a pamper session! I have never known a dog who enjoys a bath and hairdryer the way he does and he becomes quite docile under the hair dryer whilst having a gentle brush.

Flash’s ideal home would be a quiet an experienced dog owning home (adults only) with humans that have the patience and time to help grow his confidence and who also understand the need to grow calmness in him. Flash has had a few dog friends at the rescue but his high spirted nature can be a bit much for some dogs and he does not seem to like male dogs, for this reason a home where he is the only pooch would suit him best.

Flash walks well on lead but can become very excited when he sees other dogs, walks in quiet areas would be perfect for him, he loves to be outdoors and often just enjoys sitting in the yard with me watching birds, but he will equally enjoy time spent just hanging out with his humans at home. Flash really is a wonderfully, lovable, giant puppy, looking for kind and understanding humans to provide him with the security and love he deserves.

Flash has had a brilliant few weeks. He celebrated his second Birthday and was treated with his first snow day, which he loved frolicking about in. Unfortunately, he did have to spend his birthday in kennels, but I made sure it was still a very special day for him.
