name: Cooper
description:
I would like a calm and quiet, adult only home in a semi-rural area.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I don't mind cats!

I would love a good sized garden to explore and will need 6ft fences.

I am a beginner to walking on a lead, but would like an active home.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am neutered and ready to find my forever home! Read below for more!

Meet Cooper, a lovely boy who has travelled all the way from Romania to begin his new life and search for his forever home. He is a sweet boy who was extremely overwhelmed when he first arrived. Although he is still feeling quite overwhelmed to find himself here and can be very worried, especially in new situations, he is making good progress, especially with those people he knows. He was initially very worried when he first met new people, but his circle of friends has grown and he is making more human friends daily. With his favourite people, he is a friendly, affectionate boy.

Cooper will be looking for a home with adopters with experience of scared rescue dogs and though not essential, experience with Romanian rescue dogs would be a bonus. He would be happiest in a calm, quiet, adult only home where he can settle in at his own pace and continue building his confidence. Cooper would be best suited to a home in a rural or semi-rural location and would prefer to go for walks in quiet areas. He will need a secure garden with 6ft fences.

Cooper is especially worried when he finds himself in new or unfamiliar areas, and busy environments with lots of noise, people and hustle and bustle can feel particularly overwhelming for him. He finds visiting the front of the rescue and reception area quite daunting, where there is more activity and unfamiliar sights and sounds. However, when he is given the chance to spend time in a quieter, open yard, he is much more relaxed and happy, showing us that he does best when he has space and a calm environment around him.

Cooper absolutely adores other dogs and takes great comfort from having canine friends around him, so he will need another kind, confident and playful resident dog in his new home to be his companion and show him the ropes. He is also beginning to discover the joy of toys and is enjoying learning how to play, which is so sweet. He has met cats at the rescue fine, and we may consider homing him with a dog-savvy cat.

As Cooper has never lived in a home before, his adopters will need to be patient, kind and understanding while he settles in and learns all about home life, including new skills like house training. He is very much a beginner when it comes to walking on a lead and harness, but he is already starting to enjoy his walks and would love an active home where he can continue exploring the world at his own pace.

With patience, understanding and plenty of love, Cooper will start to discover just how wonderful his life can now be. In return, this gentle boy will reward his family with the privilege of watching him blossom into the happy and loved companion he was always meant to be.

He is currently being monitored for left back leg lameness, and has a potential soft tissue injury. He will continue to be monitored by our vets for any further treatment he may need.

He has tested negative prior to arrival for heartworm, lyme disease, ehrlichia, anaplasma, giardia, leishmania and brucellosis.

It’s been just over a month since I last did an update on our handsome boy Cooper and since then his confidence has grown even more!

Cooper is now the centre of attention in our big play group, he will engage in play with all the dogs who attend, and even greet any new ones with very good manners! Cooper is also now making lots of human friends with numerous members of staff that he used to be scared of!!

It’s absolutely crazy to see how confident Cooper is being, compared to the day he first arrived! It just goes to show all it take is time, patience and love!

I literally love Cooper with all my heart, watching him turn into the happiest, friendliest boy makes my heart so full!

I really hope his time to be in a home comes soon, he really does have so much love to give when he knows you!

When Cooper first arrived, his world was filled with fear. He would quietly tuck himself away at the back of his kennel, very unsure of all his surroundings and who we all were. It was so heartbreaking to see how scared cooper really was.

But every day, with kindness, patience and love, Cooper has taken another tiny step forward. Those tiny steps have turned into giant leaps. Today, the Cooper who once hid away greets his kennel mum with a wagging tail every morning and spends his days happily playing or relaxing with his kennel friends. His personality is really staring to come through and he is slowly learning that the world isn't such a scary place.

When Cooper first arrived, he'd had very little experience walking on a lead. Now he is improving so much more, he even happily takes trips down to our big play yard!

Cooper still finds unfamiliar places and new people a little scary, but it doesn't take long for him to realise he's safe. Once he trusts you, you see the sweetest, gentlest soul who simply wants to love and be loved.

Cooper has done everything we've asked of him. He's been brave. He's learned to trust. He's opened his heart. Now, we're asking for someone to do the same for him.

This beautiful young boy shouldn't be growing up behind kennel doors. He should be learning about the world from the comfort of a sofa, chasing toys around a garden, falling asleep after long walks, and knowing what it feels like to be in a home.

I am so incredibly proud of the progress Cooper has made and I have no doubts in a home with all the patience and kindness he will blossom into the most amazing loving family member anyone could wish for.

Meet Cooper, a lovely boy who has travelled all the way from Romania to begin his new life and search for his forever home. He is a sweet boy who is quite overwhelmed to find himself here, but is starting to settle in and adjust to his new surroundings. Understandably, he is feeling quite scared at the moment, especially when he first meets new people. With those he knows, he is starting to come out of his shell and its lovely to see his confidence growing. Despite his worries, he is easy to handle and in the right home we think he will truly thrive.

Cooper absolutely adores other dogs and takes great comfort from having canine friends around him, so he will need another kind, confident and playful resident dog in his new home to be his companion and show him the ropes. He is also beginning to discover the joy of toys and is enjoying learning how to play, which is so sweet.

Cooper would love to find adopters who are experienced with dogs and, whilst not essential, experience with Romanian rescue dogs would be a bonus. He would be happiest in a calm, quiet, adult only home where he can settle in at his own pace and continue building his confidence. With patience, understanding and plenty of love, Cooper will start to discover just how wonderful his life can now be. In return, this gentle boy will reward his family with the privilege of watching him blossom into the happy and loved companion he was always meant to be.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Iggy
description:
I can live with older, dog savvy teenagers, aged 13+ who respect my space.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I am new to lead walking, and would like to continue this once I have settled in.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have Grade 3 bilateral luxating patellas.

Iggy is a scared little lady who has come to us from a breeder. She has now been with us for almost two months and, although she has made some lovely progress, she has had very little interest so far.

Iggy's biggest fear is being touched. When someone reaches for her, she can crouch down and tremble with fear, but she is slowly learning that people can be kind and that she is safe. She is beginning to show more interest in people and, by watching the other dogs around her, has started running towards her carers' hands and giving them a little boop! She has also started taking treats, which is a huge step forward for this very special girl.

Iggy takes great comfort from her kennel friends and will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help her build confidence, learn to trust and discover the joys of home life. She absolutely loves being out in the yard with her friends and enjoys nothing more than rolling around in the sunshine.

As Iggy has never lived in a home before, her adopters will need to be patient while she learns about house training and settles into a new routine. She is still new to lead walking and will need continued, gentle encouragement as she learns. She will need adopters with experience of ex-breeding dogs who understand how frightened she can be and are prepared to give her plenty of time and patience.

Iggy can live with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 13+ who are sensible and able to allow her to settle at her own pace.

Iggy has been assessed by our vets and has Grade 3 bilateral luxating patellas. These are not causing her any issues at present and may improve with gentle exercise as she builds muscle. They will need to be monitored by her adopters and their vet, and they should be aware that any future treatment relating to her luxating patellas will not be covered by insurance.

Iggy is a wonderful girl who has already shown us that, with the right canine companion and plenty of patience, she can take those important little steps forward. We hope the right family will give her the chance to continue blossoming and discover how lovely life can be.

Iggy has been given the Gift of Life by Susan Stacey

This wonderful girl is Iggy! It’s been almost two months since she arrived, and although she is doing incredibly well, sadly she has had very little to no interest so far.

As a Frenchie / Bulldog lover myself, I took to this girl instantly, and she has now moved into my section. She has settled in so well and walks beautifully on her harness.

Iggy’s biggest fear is being touched. When someone reaches for her, she crouches down as though she wishes the ground would swallow her up, and she trembles with fear. Every day, I sit beside her in her kennel and gently stroke the side of her face, reassuring her that she doesn’t need to be afraid anymore. She is slowly learning that not everyone is there to hurt her, but I can only imagine what this poor girl may have experienced in her life.

What makes her progress even more special is seeing her learn from the other dogs around her. When they come over for fuss, Iggy has started running towards my hands and giving them a little boop! She has even started taking treats, which is a huge step for this very special girl.

Iggy absolutely loves being out in the yard with her friends. She enjoys nothing more than rolling around in the sunshine, and I could happily sit and watch her all day when she’s feeling relaxed and happy.

But as wonderful as her time here has been, I know that what Iggy truly needs now is a home of her own. A quiet, patient and understanding home where she can continue to learn that the world isn’t such a scary place, at her own pace, surrounded by people who will never give up on her.

Iggy is a scared little lady who has come to us from a breeder. She is beginning to show an interest in people and will cautiously approach if you crouch down to her level, but she quickly loses confidence if movements are too fast or overwhelming. She simply needs time to learn that people can be kind. Iggy takes great comfort from her kennel friends and will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home that she can lean on as she builds her confidence, learns to trust, and discovers the joys of home life. As Iggy has never lived in a home before, her adopters will need to be patient while she learns all about house training and settles into a new routine. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 13+ who are sensible and allow her time to settle in. She will need adopters who have experience with ex-breeders as she can be nervous and will need a home that understands her needs.

She is new to lead walking and will need continued, gentle encouragements in her new home as she continues to learn. Iggy is a wonderful girl who just needs time, patience and lots of TLC. With an understanding family and a confident canine companion by her side, we're sure she will continue to blossom and find her paws.

Iggy has been assessed by our vets who have noted that she has Grade 3 bilateral luxating patellas. These aren't causing her any issues at the moment and may improve with gentle exercise as she builds muscle. They will need to be monitored by her adopters and their vet and her adopters should be aware that any future treatment relating to her luxating patellas will not be covered by insurance.

name: Bee
description:
I could live with dog-savvy teens who respect my space.

I would like to be homed with another canine friend. I've not met cats so I'm unsure!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I haven't tried walks just yet and will find this a bit overwhelming at the moment.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I will be spayed before finding my forever home.

26-09-26 Bee is a gentle, shy little lady who has come into our care from a breeder alongside her sister, Gemma. She has been making great progress since coming to us, although she is still a very timid girl who is feeling overwhelmed by many aspects of the world around her.

Bee can be handled and picked up as long as you take things slowly and carefully. She still finds human interaction worrying, so her adopters will need to give her plenty of time and patience to build trust and understand that people can be kind and positive.

Bee has always lived with the company of other dogs and gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends. She relies on their company for comfort, so she will need a kind, confident resident dog in her new home who she can learn from, follow and look to for reassurance as she settles into home life.

Bee has never lived in a home before, so there is lots for her to learn. She will need patient adopters who understand that lead training, toilet training and all the other basics of home life will be completely new to her. She does not yet have these skills and will need them introduced gradually, with plenty of encouragement and positive reinforcement.

Bee will be looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with worried ex-breeding dogs and understand that she will need time to settle and gain confidence at her own pace. She can live with teenagers who are sensible and understand that she will need to be given space and allowed to settle without pressure.

Bee is a really lovely girl who is trying hard to find her confidence. She deserves a home who will absolutely adore her and give her all the time, patience and reassurance she needs. With an experienced ex-breeding dog home, a kind resident dog to guide her and plenty of love, we are sure Bee will continue to blossom into a very sweet addition to the family.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Ellie
description:
I can live with older, dog savvy teenagers who understand me.

Elite needs at least one kind and gentle dog in her new home to support her

Elite would like a secure garden to help her get used to going outside

Elite has never walked on a lead so will need to be gradually introduced to this

Elite will need to learn about house training

Elite has has a small pea sized mammary lump removed.

30-09-26 Ellie is a super sweet little lady who has returned to our care after a short adoption due to her adopter becoming unwell. She originally came to us from a breeder and has now come back into foster care and has made some lovely progress. When Ellie first returned to foster, she seemed very sad and withdrawn, sitting quietly in the corner of the sofa and not really interacting with anyone. After some time to settle, she is now starting to come out of her shell and is showing much more of her lovely personality. She loves sitting on the sofa having cuddles and fuss and will happily come over for treats.

Ellie loves being around other dogs and will need a kind, friendly and confident resident dog in her new home to help her settle and continue building her confidence. She enjoys running around the garden with her canine friends and is doing well with harness walking when she has another dog alongside her. She finds walking alone more difficult, so this will need to be continued gently in her new home. She will also need a secure garden as she can startle and has been known to slip out of her harness.

Ellie has never shown any aggression and is simply a very gentle and timid girl who can be unsure when approached too quickly. She can live with sensible, dog-savvy teens who understand that she may need some time and space to settle. She is mostly clean in the home but will need her toilet training continued.

Ellie is a truly lovely little lady who is trying so hard to be brave. With a kind family, a confident canine companion and plenty of patience, we know she will continue to blossom and show just how special she is.

Elita has been given the Gift of Life by Linda Evans

name: Pippa
description:
I'd like a quiet, adult-only home to help me relax and feel safe.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I will need an extra secure garden to keep me safe.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I'm fully vaccinated and will be spayed before adoption.

30-09-26 Pippa is a very scared and nervous lady who has come into our care from a breeder. She is very worried about being handled and becomes stressed if we attempt to pick her up. She will try to jump from our arms and, because of this, we would consider her a flight risk and she will need fencing of at least 6ft in her new garden to keep her safe. She will need very careful handling and adopters who understand just how frightened she is at the moment.

Pippa gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends and relies on their company for comfort, so she will need a kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws.

As Pippa has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to be very patient and give her time to adjust to all the new sights, sounds and experiences that come with living in a home.

Pippa will need a quiet, confident, adult-only home where she can relax and settle into her new surroundings without too much hustle and bustle. Her adopters will need to have ex-breeding experience and understand her nervous nature and allow her to progress at her own pace.

Pippa is a very worried girl right now, but with the security of a kind canine companion and a calm, patient family, we hope she will slowly begin to feel safe and gain the confidence she needs to enjoy her new life.

Pippa has been given the Gift of Life by Margaret Hunter

name: Paris
description:
I'd like a quiet, experienced, adult-only home to help me relax and feel safe.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I will be spayed before finding my forever home!

30-09-26 Paris is a scared girly who is not used to being handled. She has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start and is not a fan of human touch at the moment.

When we have needed to get close to Paris for health checks, we have had to carefully corner her so that we can pick her up. She panics and shakes, but she does allow us to handle her and, once she is safely in our arms, she eventually cuddles into us and allows us to carry out her checks. This shows us that although she is very frightened, she is beginning to understand that we are not going to hurt her.

Paris will need another kind and confident dog in her new home, and this dog will be a much-needed support system for her as she settles in and starts to find her confidence.

As Paris has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training and the other basics of home life. She will need an ex-breeding experienced, adult-only home with adopters who understand just how much patience and reassurance she will need.

Paris is a very worried little girl right now, but once she is given the security of being held, we can see that there is a much softer side to her. We hope that with time, patience and the support of a reassuring canine companion, she will slowly learn to trust and enjoy the happy new start she deserves.

Paris has been given the Gift of Life by Margaret Hunter

name: Hooper
description:
I can live with older children, aged 16+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am neutered and have had an entropion repaired on my left eye.

21-09-26 Hooper is a very handsome gentleman who has come to us from a breeder. He can be a little on the nervous side, especially when meeting new people, but he is growing in confidence every day and we are beginning to see more of his lovely personality. Hooper is starting to trust the familiar faces he sees regularly, although he can still be unsure when someone new approaches him and may retreat to the back of his kennel where he feels safest.

Hooper shares his kennel wonderfully with his doggy friends and really enjoys having them around him. He will need at least one calm and confident resident dog in his new home that he can lean on and look to for reassurance as he continues to build his confidence. Having a friendly dog by his side will be a big help to Hooper as he learns that the world isn't such a scary place.

Hooper can live with older, sensible, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16+ who understand that he is a nervous boy and will give him the time and space he needs to settle in. He isn't walking on a lead yet, so his adopters will need to be patient as he learns this new skill. For Hooper, some quiet garden sniffs may be the perfect place to start while he gets used to his new surroundings before gradually building up to adventures further afield.

Hooper has never lived in a home before, so there will be lots for him to learn. His adopters will need to be kind and patient as he learns about house training and all the new sights, sounds, routines and experiences that come with home life. He will need someone who understands that his progress may take time and who will allow him to move at his own pace without putting pressure on him.

Hooper will need adopters with previous ex-breeding experience who understand the patience and understanding these dogs can require. He isn't going to be the sort of dog who walks straight into a new home and feels completely at ease, but we know that with the right person, he has the potential to make some amazing progress.

Hooper really needs someone to take a chance on him and show him just how wonderful life can be. He is a gentle boy who is slowly learning to trust, and we hope that the right family will see the lovely dog underneath his nerves and give him the time, patience and love he deserves.

He has had an entropion repaired on his left eye.

Hooper has been given the Gift of Life by Jackie Coleman

name: Gabriel
description:
I need an adult-only experienced home that understands me.

I would need to be the only animal in the home.

I may be shy now, but once I have settled I would love a nice garden I can play in!

I love going for walks, and would love an active home!

I know some tricks & walk well on the lead but will need help with housetraining.

I have been neutered and am ready to find my forever home.

Gabriel originally came to us from a breeder, and for him the world felt like a very frightening place. He was worried of people, and new environments and unfamiliar experiences left him feeling overwhelmed. Even something as simple as having a lead put on was a huge challenge. He needed time, patience and gentle encouragement to begin to feel safe.

Gabriel was adopted for a short period, but unfortunately it was not the right fit for him. He was returned after displaying unwanted behaviours in the home and making the wrong choices when he felt uncomfortable in a situation, which did result in Gabriel biting. He will need a quiet, adult-only home without resident or visiting children. Gabriel can struggle with visitors coming to the house, so he will need a home without too many visitors and where he can be placed in a separate room when people do come over. His adopters will also need to be willing to meet him multiple times before adoption so that he has the opportunity to develop a bond and build trust with them.

Gabriel is a very sensitive boy who feels anxious about a lot of things. During his time here we are trying to help him feel more comfortable by giving him the tools to know how to be more relaxed in these scary situations. To Gabriel, new people are very scary and he feels that he needs to tell them to go away by barking and lunging, when put in poor situations this has led to him having a bite history. He is a very sweet dog but he has very little he trusts in this world and unfortunately humans are top of that list at the moment. With people who have earned his trust he is exceptionally sweet and loving, he loves to give you cuddles and he really thinks he should be a lap dog. When introductions are done slowly and in a manner that he can cope with he will allow that person into his circle reasonably quickly and then he gets very excited to see them.

As he has had very little in this world he does become exceptionally attached to his trusted humans and doesn't like to share them with other dogs or other people, so he is looking for a home with a maximum of two people and will need to be the only dog in the home. Adopters with experience of guarding behaviours are essential to help him succeed in his next home and make sure it really will be his forever home.

Gabriel walks nicely on his harness and gets very excited to see dogs when out and about but is wary of strangers walking past, for this reason he is muzzled when out as it keeps him safe in the event of someone getting too close or trying to touch him.

He has shown signs of resource guarding his food here and any high value long lasting treats. He has Kongs as he is happy for the empty Kong to be removed from his kennel once he feels he's finished with it, but these are things that will have to be managed in his new home. It would be a good idea to limit his access to the kitchen in the home to avoid the possibility of him getting things that he may be inclined to guard, especially until he settles and the bond has been built with him to ensure that he trusts that you won't take things away from him without him getting something higher value in its place.

Gabriel socialises well with other dogs here and does enjoy chasing dogs around our big play yard here, so having the opportunity to continue making friends with playful dogs in his new home is necessary to keep him happy and help him to continue to grow in confidence. Someone will be incredibly lucky to have Gabriel as their companion, they will just have to understand that he does require the time and effort to make sure he progresses and starts to see the world is less scary than he thinks it is.

Gabriel will need more than one meet and greet with his prospective adopters to allow him time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

Today I got to spend more time with Gabriel than I usually would so I took advantage of that and we went for a much longer walk.... As usual he was brilliant, he listens, if we need to move out of the way for a car he'll listen to me and move off the road to the side, if he's walking slightly ahead and I call him he stops and turns back.

We also sat around the other side of the rescue where it's usually busier as I want to get him used to being in busier areas and being around people he doesn't know, as he can be a bit reactive.... He did so well, it was fairly busy so he was a little unsure at first but the longer we stayed the better he was, he was good with others around him too, he has come such a long way, but this is something I'm going to keep on working on with him for the foreseeable as we don't know what life he'll have outside of here and he may need to used to busier areas.

We also played with a puzzle feeder today, which he decided would be fun to pick up with his mouth and drop it on the floor to get the treats out faster, he really is a funny boy, but he's super smart too and is quick to pick up tricks especially when there's treats involved.

He really is every Bocker lovers dream and he always gets so overlooked.

He is muzzle trained, and would need to wear his muzzle when meeting new people, dogs or at the vets, but he's also just a big softy who gives the loveliest cwtches and kisses, to be a part of his gang is such an amazing feeling and he shows his affection for you so clearly when he loves you.

This week we’ve had a heatwave which has meant alot of our rescue dogs have needed their ears checked incase they’ve had any mucky build up - Gabriel was one of the unlucky few that have needed some TLC in this area!!We’ve recently had a new meds person who has been visiting Gabriel to do his ear cleans & he has been an absolute angel. He’s even been given the nickname Angel GabrielIt’s just a testament to Gabriel that yes he can be unsure of new people, but once he knows you he truly is such a wonderful boy. He just needs someone to take that chance on him, show him the love he’s desperate to have & he’ll return it tenfold.Gabriel has been waiting such a long time now, and seeing a boy so full of love & hope is heartbreaking when we can’t reassure him that his time will come soon!!!

Today, I worked with Gabriel again for the first time in months. I was a little worried he’d have forgotten, however, it’s safe to say the bond previously made still remains.Gabriel is such an excited little boy. He lives for treats. He’s such a clever and obedient boy when the treats come out. Usually, he’s full of energy and excitement. Once the treats are out, he’s still and sits like the perfect little boy we know he can be.As he can be very busy, I’ve always thought it essential to take him out on walks, the longer the better. As mentioned in a previous update, he loves walks! Once you pull the lead out, you get a similar reaction to the treats.The longer the walk the better. Walks are so good for this gorgeous boy. They keep him stimulated and help shave off the pounds he gains from everyone giving him treats!On the whole, I was so happy to see my boy again. So happy, so loyal, keen to go on walks and he listened so well. I’m so proud of the progress he’s made since I last saw him!Gabriel still can be a challenge and, he does not like everyone. Once you’ve made that bond with him though, it stays. Don’t overlook this boy. He’s such a beautiful, intelligent and fun dog!

This boy has my heart, once you form that special bond with him I do believe it's for life. He is very loving and enjoys a cuddle and a fuss from people he feels comfortable around, as his adopter you'll hopefully get that bond through spending time with him and letting him go at his own pace.Gabriel, as most bockers do, lives for his food and treats, whenever I run him in from being in the yard I always leave a small treat in his bed or somewhere in the back for him to find, and he absolutely loves this he gets so excited knowing he'll get a treat and runs straight to the back of his kennel to find it.He loves his walks and his time in the big yard. He's the curious, adventurous type who just wants to investigate everything, a 10 minute stroll up the road can take us an extra 20-25 minutes to stroll back because he likes to explore, but I don't mind, seeing him happy makes me happy I'd never want to stop him from exploring the world.Gabriel would need an experienced, adult only home (view profile for explanation), he would need someone who is active and can provide him with mental and physical stimulation daily. He is a very smart boy and can pick things up quite quickly which is why, with the help from some treats I think he would pick up toilet training rather quickly.Please don't overlook this handsome guy just because he's not your small and fluffy type dog, Gabriel is a special boy with a lot of love to give, and for that right person/people he would become a true companion and best friend.

Gabriel, a stunning Bocker with a huge personality and an even bigger heart. This handsome boy is full of life and enthusiasm, always ready to embrace whatever the day brings. Gabriel thrives on affection and absolutely loves a good fuss and cuddle — he’s a real people-dog who enjoys being close to those he trusts.

Gabriel is a clever lad with so much potential. He’s already showing us just how intelligent he is as he responds to basic commands! With the right guidance and training , we know he’ll flourish and continue to grow in confidence, not that he lacks any confidence! He also walks beautifully on the lead, making him a joy to take out on adventures.

Sadly, Gabriel has been returned to us, and we are now searching for the right forever home where he can truly settle and feel secure. Gabriel would be best suited as an only dog, in a calm and quiet home environment. We are looking for a home with minimal visitors and no children, as busy households can feel overwhelming for him.

Gabriel can display guarding behaviours, so he will need experienced owners who understand this and can manage the home environment appropriately to support him. With the right knowledge, structure, and patience, Gabriel will thrive and continue to build trust.

Gabriel has so much love to give to the right person. With understanding, consistency, and kindness, he will make an incredibly loyal and devoted time

Gabriel is a stunning Bocker who is full of life, love, and character! This gorgeous boy is bursting with energy and adores nothing more than a good fuss and a cwtch.He’s incredibly smart, and we just know it wouldn’t take long for him to be trained to a very high standard – he’s already showing us how bright he is every day. Gabriel also walks beautifully on the lead, making him a joy to take out and about.Now all he needs is a forever family who can give him the love, attention, and adventures he deserves. With his brains, energy, and big heart, Gabriel is sure to make someone the most wonderful companion.

Gabriel has come to us from a breeder and has made incredible progress since arriving with us! When he first came, he was nervous around new people and worried about having a lead put on, which made walks and new kennel staff introductions a real challenge. Now, he gets excited for walk time and happily allows us to put on both his lead and harness with no issues.This handsome boy is a true foodie and loves learning new tricks. He already knows “sit” and “paw,” so with trust and patience, teaching him more tricks should be a fun and rewarding experience. Gabriel needs a confident, experienced, owner who will provide clear boundaries and structure, as he can be cheeky if he thinks he’s in charge as well as an adult-only home where he can continue to learn. Gabriel has the confidence to be an only dog in a home with can allow him the dedication and time he needs and will need a home with no cats or small furries.Once Gabriel knows and trusts you, he is affectionate, loyal, and loves nothing more than sharing his goofy charm. Underneath his shy moments, he is a beautiful boy with a heart full of love. He is looking for someone who will continue his training, set clear rules, and enjoy all the affection, loyalty, and joy he has to give.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

name: Juice
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I have learned how to walk on a lead and am enjoying going for walks.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I have had 7 teeth extracted at the time of my spay.

Juice came to us from a breeder and when she first arrived, she was understandably very shy and overwhelmed by everything around her. She wanted to trust people but was nervous about approaching, often hovering nearby and watching with interest before her worries got the better of her. She has since moved into foster and has made some lovely progress and is settling in well. Juice is still cautious, but she now follows her fosterers around the house and will approach for fuss when they offer their hand to her. She particularly loves belly rubs and will completely relax and close her eyes!

Juice will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace. She will need another kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can take her under their wing and help her settle into her new home. Although she does rely on other dogs for comfort, she can guard her bed from other dogs, particularly when she has just woken up, so she will need a calm, relaxed resident dog who will not disturb her while she is sleeping. She can also be startled by people when she is in her bed and on one occasion she did nip her fosterer when they stroked her in her bed. Her new family will therefore need to be confident managing this behaviour, recognising her body language and ensuring she is always left undisturbed when she is resting.

Juice had never lived in a home before moving to foster, but she is already settling in wonderfully. Her toilet training is going really well and she has only had 2 accidents in the home so far. She has also learned all about walking on a lead and harness and is now becoming more confident wearing her harness and she is starting to enjoy her walks. She is also beginning to understand that the home is a safe place, happily relaxing and sleeping near her fosterers and enjoying the company of their resident dog.

Juice will be looking for an adult-only home with experienced adopters who understand that she is still learning to trust and who will allow her to continue building her confidence at her own pace. She has already come such a long way in a short time, and we hope that with the right family, she will continue to blossom into a happy and loving companion.

She has had 7 teeth extracted at the time of her spay.

Juice has been given the Gift of Life by Holly Kantolinna

Juice has settled in really well. She is still cautious but follows us around the house although backs off if we approach her as she prefers it if you put your hand out to her. She will then approach us, sniff our hand and accept fuss and scratches. She loves having scratches but her favourite are belly rubs and she will close her eyes and completely relax!

She sleeps well over night in her bed on the floor in our bedroom and will wake us up by walking around the room when she needs to go to toilet. Her toilet training is going really well and apart from 2 accidents early on she goes in the garden either asking to go out or when the back door is open taking herself out to go.

She is getting more confident having her harness on for walk and as long as you put it on slowly, she is happy to have it on. She is starting to walk really well on her lead and enjoys her walks and plenty of sniffs! She has met a few dogs on her walks and as long as they are not too energetic and boisterous she seems happy to meet them and have a sniff! She is ok walking along roads but does startle if there are any loud or sudden noises.

She loves being with us in the house and although she doesn't sit right next to us she enjoys being close by and really relaxes and sleeps. She enjoys being with our resident dog but is also happy to follow us outside or sit with us when our dog isn't there. She's also happy travelling in the car with our dog.

She hasn't mastered going up and down stairs yet so at present we are carrying her up and down. She is starting to go up a few small steps on her walks.

She enjoys her food and will sometimes take treats or food from our hands.  She is a lovely girl who has really progressed in the short time that we have had her and is continuing to develop her confidence.

Juice will need an experienced, adult only home with adopters who can understand and manage her nervousness and recognise when she needs space. She can guard her bed from other dogs, particularly when she has just woken up, so any resident dog will need to be calm and relaxed and not likely to bother her while she is sleeping. She can also be startled by people when she is in her bed and, on one occasion, she did nip when she was stroked resting. Her adopters will therefore need to be confident in managing this behaviour, ensuring she is left undisturbed in her bed and giving her the space she needs to feel safe and comfortable.

Juice has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for a loving forever home where she can begin the next chapter of her life.

She is a wonderful little lady who is feeling a little shy and overwhelmed at the moment, but she is trying so hard to be brave. Juice is already showing lovely signs that she wants to trust people. She will quietly hover nearby, watching you with interest and looking as though she would really like to come over for a gentle fuss, but at the last moment her worries get the better of her. We think that with time, patience, love and plenty of reassurance, her confidence will continue to grow and her true personality will begin to shine through.

Juice will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home where she can settle in at her own pace. She will need patient adopters who understand that building trust takes time and who will let her make progress without putting any pressure on her. She will also need another kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can be her friend and help show her that life is full of good things.

As Juice has never lived in a home before, everything will be a brand new experience for her. She will need help with housetraining, learning about household routines and gradually becoming accustomed to all the sights and sounds of family life. She is also yet to learn how to walk on a lead and harness, so her adopters will need to introduce this gently and positively as her confidence grows.

Juice is a lovely girl with so much potential. With a patient family by her side and a canine friend to guide her, we are sure she will blossom into a happy and much-loved companion.

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Rupert
description:
Rupert – 14 month old male Cross-Breed is a friendly chap who’s ready to find a loving home of his own.

Rupert is one of three brothers rescued as young pups.

He is neutered, microchipped, and fully vaccinated.

Rupert is a friendly chap and is good with other dogs. He just needs the opportunity to come to a family of his own.

He is young and would suit a family with teenage children who are dog savvy or a couple or individual who has time to acclimatise him to his new surroundings.

Rupert would be transported directly by registered pet courier to your home and would arrive with his passport and health paperwork.

We give lifetime rescue backup to all of our dogs.

name: Bao
description:
Meet Bao – 5 year old male Cross-Breed. Bao is a charming pup from Romania whose heart is as big as his soulful brown eyes and whose journey has shaped him into the most gentle of souls.

Bao may have started life with uncertainty, but today he’s blossomed into a mellow, affectionate companion who’s simply searching for a cozy spot in a loving home. At five years old, Bao has the perfect balance of calm maturity and soft playfulness. He enjoys relaxed walks, and quiet companionship.

While he can be a little shy at first, Bao warms up with patience and kind words. Once he feels safe, he becomes a loyal shadow. He’s most comfortable in calm environments and would thrive with a family who can offer him structure, consistency, and lots of love.

Bao may need a little support adjusting to a new life, but he responds well to positive reinforcement and routine. His ideal home would be one that understands his past while focusing on the beautiful future ahead.

He’s already proven his resilience and his capacity to trust again, and now he’s patiently waiting to be welcomed into a home where he can truly relax and feel safe.

Could your family be the one to show Bao the warmth he needs?

VaccinatedBlood testedFlea and worm treatedNeutered

name: Kia
description:
Kia is a lovely approximately 2-3 year old, large sized crossbreed who travelled to the UK from Spain recently and is currently fostered in the west midlands area.

Kia was originally rescued from the streets of Spain and spent over a year waiting in the shelter for her chance of a home.

In her time in the shelter Kia was noted to be people and dog friendly but disliked cats.

She is currently under assessment in the UK and so far has shown to absolutely love people, she would probably be best living with a calmer male dog on correct introductions. She isn’t sure about big bouncy dogs and can grumble at them.

Kia is happy to be crated and is clean in the home. She has not been destructive and walks well on the lead too. She is currently learning basic commands such as sit, down etc

Kia is a calm girl who loves attention and is more than happy to climb into your lap to get it! (Although with her size this is quite a challenge at times).

Despite being calm for the majority of time she does have bursts of energy and due to her size would be best homed with children 8+ due to the potential for knocking little children over by accident.

name: Chance
description:
Chance is a 2 year old male Cross-Breed and is currently being fostered in Surrey, ready to find his forever home with a family who will adore him.

Chance is a small-to-medium-sized dog with a soft white coat, a cheeky personality, and the cutest little Mohawk. He’s full of character, very affectionate, and ready to find his forever home.

He walks beautifully on the lead and enjoys off-lead time at the park. Chance is muzzle trained, and when he is off lead, he does wear his muzzle. That said, he’s friendly with most dogs and people—especially if they have a dog with them!

Chance currently lives with a resident dog and gets along wonderfully with her.

At home, he’s loving, cuddly, and calm. He enjoys a good walk followed by a nap (sometimes even before breakfast is finished!) and will happily flop over in front of you for belly rubs. He’s food-motivated, learns quickly, and does an adorable little spin when asked to sit.

He does best with slow introductions to new people in the home and builds trust over time. Once he knows you, he’s loyal, doting, and will look at you like you’re his whole world.

We’ve grown very attached to Chance, and while it’ll be hard to say goodbye, we’re excited to see him find the love he deserves. If you ever need someone to care for him while you’re away, we’d happily take him back in a heartbeat.

If you think Chance could be the one for you, get in touch to arrange a meet-and-greet. He’s ready to steal your heart.

name: Odin
description:
Odin is an 18-month-old male Cross-Breed. Odin is one of three brothers currently searching for the forever home of his dreams. He’s already had quite the start to life and is more than ready to trade kennel walls for the comforts of a loving family.

Odin’s the size of a small Collie, so he’s a great medium-sized companion — not so big that he’ll knock over your nan, but not so small he’ll disappear between the couch cushions.

Odin has been neutered, fully vaccinated, and microchipped, which means he’s ready to go without any of the faff. He’s a friendly chap who gets along well with his brothers, which shows he’s got solid doggy social skills already.

That’s a major win if you’re hoping to bring him into a multi-dog home or want a pup who can make friends at the dog park.

Odin also seems to be friendly with cats, which is basically the Holy Grail of dog qualities — no fur-flying drama in sight.

His easy-going nature will make him a delightful addition to many kinds of households, whether it’s a busy family home, a couple who love outdoor adventures, or an individual looking for a loyal sidekick.

Because Odin is still a young dog, he needs a family, couple, or individual with time and patience to teach him about the world. He’s eager to learn and experience life outside kennel walls, so he’ll thrive in a home where he can get plenty of guidance, attention, and love.

He’s already spent a significant chunk of his life in kennels, which is just heartbreaking for a pup as sweet as him. Giving Odin a stable home now would mean giving him the chance he deserves to discover the joys of comfy beds, long walks, and the occasional cheeky treat.

To make things easier, Odin will be delivered straight to his new home by a registered pet transport company, so you won’t have to worry about a stressful handover or tricky logistics. All you have to do is open your door — and your heart — to this lovely boy.

Odin is truly a diamond in the rough, and whoever adopts him will not only be changing his life forever but will gain a loyal, happy companion who will return that kindness tenfold.

name: Hera
description:
Hera is nervous around visitors in the home which will cause her to be reactive and bark at them however once trusted she is very loving. She regularly visits her 92 year old owner’s dad who she is very good with.

Hera accepts a collar, harness and lead. She is very strong on the lead and can pull towards things so she will therefore need a strong owner to handle her size and strength.

Hera can be reactive towards vehicles, cars, scooters, bikes and buses which can cause her to chase them. She has also recently started to become reactive towards dogs on walks too however it is felt this may be due to the other smaller dog in the home having reactive which Hera picks up on.

She will need continued training on this.Hera is toilet trained and crate trained. She isn’t destructive but has chewed her own bed previously.

Hera does show guarding and dominance behaviours with the other dogs. She can be left alone for up to 4 hours with no issues and she sleeps well overnight, she will bark if she needs the toilet.

She is okay in the car but can sometimes need some encouragement. She has been sick on one occasion.

name: Vinnie
description:
Vinnie is reactive to people visiting the home which can cause him to bark and growl at them. Vinnie will need a home with minimal visitors and someone willing to continue building his confidence and provide training.

Vinnie is a very loyal, loving and affectionate dog. He isn’t a fan of baths or showers and hates being wet however he takes this in his stride.

He loves cuddles and getting lots of attention from his favourite people however he equally likes his own space in the home to be able to settle and have some alone time.

He loves being outside in the garden and is a super playful boy who loves his toys, especially anything that squeaks and he will spend hours chewing his bones.

Vinnie accepts a collar, harness and lead. He is very strong on the lead and does pull however he will calm down and responds well to heal.

He can however be reactive towards other dogs on walks which causes him to bark, growl and squeal, this is due to excitement and not aggression.

Once he has said hello to the dog or they have passed he will calm down. Vinnie loves his walks and loves to run around in secure fields and burn off his energy. Vinnie is a high energy boy who needs an active family to give him lots of attention and time.

He will need lots of long walks, training and mental stimulation to keep him out of trouble and keep him busy but more importantly he needs someone who can love him unconditionally.

He has a beautiful personality and character. Vinnie has been known to be noise reactive to noises he hears outside especially people and he will bark if people knock on the door.

He would therefore prefer a home in a quieter area.Vinnie is toilet trained but is not crate trained. He can be known to be destructive towards shoes, carpet and does love to dig holes in the garden.

Vinnie can be left alone for short periods of time within the home with no issues. He sleeps well overnight and travels well in the car.

name: Aris
description:
Aris is a 9-year-old male Cross-Breed. Aris is currently in Cyprus, where he has been waiting patiently for a new home for the past 16 months.

It’s heartbreaking to think about his journey: surrendered by the only family he had ever known after living with them since he was a puppy, Aris went straight from the warmth of a home to the cold reality of a shelter cage.

Despite the upheaval he has faced, Aris remains one of the friendliest dogs you could ever meet when it comes to humans. He adores people and is eager to please, always ready to show off his affectionate and loving side to anyone willing to give him a chance.

His time spent with his previous family wasn’t wasted either; he was well-trained and his obedience still shines through.

Aris obeys commands and walks beautifully on the lead, which makes outings with him easy and enjoyable. He is a big boy at 30 kilograms, but he carries himself with grace and calm, proving that he’s a mature dog who just wants to be someone’s loyal companion again.

While Aris has an incredible temperament with humans, he’s not fond of other dogs or animals, so he needs to be the only pet in his future home. Given what he’s been through, it’s understandable that he prefers having his humans all to himself, where he can soak up every bit of love and attention.

His shelter caretakers believe that somewhere out there is a perfect home for Aris — a place where he can experience the security, comfort, and affection he once knew. After everything he’s been through, he more than deserves a second chance at happiness.

Aris comes with full rescue back-up from Saving Souls, ensuring his new family will always have support. He will also be treated for parasites, vaccinated, and arrive with his own doggy passport, ready to start his new life.

For anyone willing to open their heart to a loyal, affectionate, and well-behaved older dog, Aris is ready and waiting. He just needs someone to finally see him and give him the home he has been dreaming of for so long.

name: Bruno
description:
Bruno is a 2-year 6-month-old male Cross-Breed. Bruno is currently in Cyprus, waiting patiently for his chance to find a loving forever home where he can finally stretch his legs somewhere other than the shelter yard.

Described as a goofy boy, Bruno is a handsome young dog bursting with personality and charm, who just wants someone to notice his big, hopeful eyes.

It’s heartbreaking to watch Bruno, a happy and playful boy, stuck in the shelter where his only joy comes from short bursts of playtime in the yard with his doggy friends. Seeing him beg with his eyes for just a little extra time outside shows just how much he craves freedom, adventure, and a loving family.

Bruno’s eyes reveal his true soul: a dog desperate to be loved and included as part of someone’s life. He adores humans and wants nothing more than to share his days with people who appreciate his playful, energetic nature.

He also loves water and having fun with other dogs, proving that he’s ready for all kinds of adventures.

As an active dog with a strong, muscular build, Bruno weighs in at a solid 24 kilograms. While he’s all muscle, he’s not a giant in stature, making him a medium-sized dog perfect for those who want a sturdy companion without the overwhelming size of a large breed.

Bruno needs a home with an active lifestyle, where his boundless energy and love for outdoor activities will be embraced. He thrives on play, exercise, and adventures with humans who share his enthusiasm for life and the outdoors.

Despite his current circumstances, Bruno has remained a loving boy who enjoys every moment of human interaction he can get. His loyalty and affection make him a wonderful companion for the right family who can give him the exercise, love, and attention he deserves.

Bruno comes with full rescue back-up from Saving Souls, so his future family can adopt with confidence knowing they’ll always have support. He will also be vaccinated, neutered, treated for parasites, and have his blood work done, ensuring he arrives healthy and ready for a new beginning.

Bruno has so much love and life left to give. All he needs is someone willing to see past the kennel bars and offer him the chance he’s been waiting for.

name: Nora
description:
Say hello to Nora – 1 year old female Saluki Cross who’s shy, sweet, and quietly adorable. She’ll warm up quickly in a loving home, especially if you’re around a lot to give her those cuddles she craves.

Nora was rescued when she was a newborn pup after her mum had been abandoned to the streets of Muscat. They went into foster until Nora was 3 months old and now she is in a boarding facility.

She has recently spent time in a foster home again which gave us a good insight into her behaviour in a home environment.

Her foster family describes her as shy, sweet, and quiet. She does like some people instantly but will need some time with others to get closer.

With the foster mum being at home a lot, she warmed up fast and started to cuddle and play. She followed her two foster sisters in everything and copied their behavior, but there was some conflict at times over toys and space.

The foster family thinks she’d be better in a home with other dogs as long as they were male or friendly females.

She is very playful, happy, and active, but also sleeps a lot during the day. She likes toys, running around the garden, and her treats.

Potty training went well when she had access to the garden. She listened well to her name, but sits are still a challenge to learn. She likes her walks and is easy on the leash, but new sounds and people still make her nervous. She seems food motivated and is a happy eater.

All in all a really lovely young dog with good potential to be the best family dog. She will benefit from another dog for confidence, but it’s not essential. She is protective of the house and will bark when she is alerted, but not much.

Nora is fully vaccinated, microchipped, and spayed. She will be ready to travel to the UK in September/October 2025.

name: Leia
description:
LEIA – A Devoted Soul Ready to Complete Her Journey Home

Leia is a Ukraine war dog in need of a safe haven. Available under a foster-to-adopt. UK Based Retford, DN22 Available For Meet-and-Greet

Leia is a 4-year-old German Shepherd cross, a truly stunning girl with an intelligent mind and an even bigger heart.

She’s already captured the hearts of her foster family – now she’s waiting for her forever one. She arrived in the UK on 20th June, travelling from Ukraine.

SIZE: Upper-medium (55 cm / 30 kg)SPAYED: YesCHARACTER HIGHLIGHTS: Loyal, playful, loving, intelligentDOGS: Selective, best as only dogCATS: Not testedCHILDREN: Great with kids 8+

Foster UpdateLeia settled beautifully into her foster home. She is friendly, affectionate, and adores human company. She’ll lean in for strokes and is happiest close to her people – she’s already proven to be a loyal shadow.

While she has a touch of bounce and energy, it’s been easy to manage with a little guidance.

Leia enjoys spending time outdoors and would love a home with a secure garden and a tall fence where she can safely explore and relax. She travels well in the car, showing calm and relaxed behaviour throughout her journey.

She’s been loving the daily brushing and absolutely thrives on attention – her foster says she’s a joy to have around.

Rescue StoryLeia’s story could have ended in tragedy. She and her companion Dior were found abandoned outside a rural shop, begging strangers for scraps.

The shop owner arranged for them to be poisoned – but one kind worker couldn’t stand by. A rescue team was called and arrived just in time. Now safe and thriving in the UK, Leia is ready to complete her journey home.

More About LeiaLeia is highly intelligent, eager to please, and picks things up quickly. She enjoys walks, enrichment. Selective to other dogs, tolerant or even playful on walks, prefers not to share space and home, perfect as the only dog.

She would suit an active, caring home – one that offers companionship, structure, and security. She’s good with older children (8+) who respect her space and energy.

Health InformationLeia is fully healthy, spayed, and up to date on all core vaccines. She’s microchipped, and all dogs are C.Brucella tested before travel (owners will receive a licensed laboratory test certificate).

RBU, post-adoption support, and 4 weeks free PetPlan insurance provided upon adoption.

name: Kriss
description:
Kriss is a 2 year old male Cross-Breed. His journey hasn’t been an easy one—just a few weeks ago, he was spotted wandering the streets of Dubrovnik, starving, malnourished, and desperately searching for safety and affection.

Thankfully, some concerned locals noticed him and reached out for help, and now Kriss is finally safe in a shelter in Croatia.

Since arriving, Kriss has completely turned things around. He’s shown himself to be an upbeat, curious, and playful pup, full of life and energy.

He’s not just surviving anymore—he’s thriving, and he’s ready to find that special someone who’ll give him the loving home he’s never had.

Kriss gets along well with female dogs and would do great in a home where he can share his joy without stress. He’s the kind of dog who brings a spark into a room—cheerful, eager to play, and easy to love.

If you’re looking for a no-drama, happy-go-lucky companion who’s all about fun and tail wags, Kriss is the guy.

He’s already microchipped, castrated, blood tested, vaccinated, and treated for fleas and worms—fully kitted out and ready to go. Kriss comes with rescue back-up from Meadow of Hope Dog Rescue, and standard adoption checks will apply.

name: Ringo
description:
Ringo is a 6-year-old male Cross-Breed. Weighing around 10kg, this small boy is currently living a bleak life in a cage, stuck in a pound with little to no comfort.

His story is brutal—found as a stray with a microchip, only for his owner to be contacted and respond by saying he didn’t want Ringo and would kill him if he was returned. So now he waits, day after day, with no family and no reason why.

Despite that trauma, Ringo is still holding on. He can be okay with other dogs but has a habit of bothering them, which causes tension in the pound.

Because of that, a home where he’s the only pet is ideal. He deserves to be someone’s one and only after everything he’s been through.

He’s also okay around respectful children, which opens the door to a loving family environment—just one that understands his past and gives him the space and patience to feel safe.

Ringo is neutered, vaccinated, wormed, flea-treated, and will have his blood work completed before travel. He comes with full rescue back-up from Saving Souls Animal Rescue.

He’s not broken—just let down by humans who should’ve protected him. Now, he needs someone to show him that not all people give up.

name: Dukey
description:
Meet Dukey, a 7-8 year old male dog of unknown breed who is currently in foster kennels in Romania.

Dukey is in foster kennels in Romania. He was saved from Lancram kill shelter in August 2021, coming up to five years ago. This is so sad.

He is not one of Just Kind Dog Rescue’s dogs, but I was involved in taking him out of Lancram and now, with your help, I am trying to find him a home.

Dukey is 7 to 8 years old and 50 cm tall. It has taken time, but this boy now allows contact; he just needs to be approached slowly, with no quick moves. He is friendly and not aggressive in any way, he just needs time to build up his trust. He is a timid, gentle boy.

He has been on a lead but definitely needs training with this. So far, when tried, he does not like it.

Are you looking for a handsome boy? Look no further, Dukey is here.

7-8 years old.50 cm tall.Approx 28 kg.Neutered.Vaccinated.Dewormed and deflead.Passport and health book.Delivered to your door.Rescue back-up for life through Just Kind Dog Rescue

name: Gypsy
description:
Meet Gypsy, an 11 year old female Poodle Cross Jack Russell Terrier.

Gypsy came to us in a poor state, and it appears she previously lived outdoors, possibly under a caravan. Her expectations of human care were minimal, and she would not come into the house unless encouraged. She has had a couple of litters in her past.

Despite this neglect, Gypsy is the sweetest little girl we have fostered. She has a gentle and affectionate nature and is an absolute joy to be around. Her only quirk is that she becomes excited by the scent of foxes and may bark.

Gypsy was not initially house-trained, but after three days of constant monitoring she is now clean in the house and no longer needs to be crated at night. She has settled beautifully and continues to be a very good girl.

Health-wise, Gypsy is on a raw diet as it is clear she is allergic to kibble. Her ears require daily cleaning, and she was previously chewing her paws, which has reduced significantly. Her paws are not in poor condition.

Gypsy is friendly with people and other dogs but is not suitable to live with cats. She is independent in nature and tends to do her own thing, calmly ignoring most distractions.

She is food-oriented and would be happy living with another friendly dog. Two 30-minute walks per day suit her well, as she enjoys getting out and about and is now comfortable walking off lead.

Gypsy would make a wonderful companion for an older person, provided she continues on a raw diet and receives her daily walks.

She will need ongoing help with ear care and is slightly deaf, although her hearing has improved as her ears have been cleaned. The ear canals remain somewhat swollen due to past neglect.

Gypsy now loves the warmth and comfort of indoor life and enjoys choosing between the sofa and her bed. This lovely little girl truly deserves a caring home with a garden where she can enjoy her retirement years in comfort.

name: Tito
description:
Tito is a 4 year old large male Beagle Cross.

Tito is Black, Brown and White in colour and his coat is long in length.

Tito’s nature is sweet, gentle and he loves to cuddle.

Tito came to the shelter with his siblings when he was around 3 months old. We don’t know his history because he just appeared. Someone broke in at night and left the puppies there absolutely terrified.

For a long time communication with Tito was very difficult. A couple were interested in adopting Tito so they invested a fair amount of time coming and walking him and he improved a great deal.

However, they were ultimately unable to offer him a home.

With time and patience Tito will be a lovely dog. He’s shy and scared of unknown situations but he is such a lovely boy and we believe worth the commitment.

He gets on well with other dogs in his kennel and his leisure time is spent playing with approximately 12 dogs. Because of his lack of confidence Tito should only be homed with another dog.

name: Forest
description:
Meet Forest, a 5 year 11 month old male Cross-Breed with a gentle soul and a big heart.

Friendly Forest is a gentle and loving boy who was found abandoned in the forest (hence his name) and has been safe at the shelter since 2021.

Forest is a sociable and well-mannered companion who adores human company and enjoys spending time with people he knows and trusts.

He is happy to live either with other dogs or as an only dog, and he is comfortable being left alone at home for reasonable periods. With appropriate introductions, he may be able to live with dog-savvy children aged 10 and above.

Forest has not yet been tested with cats, but this can be done if required.

He would thrive in a home that can offer access to a secure garden, as he loves having outdoor space to explore, relax, and enjoy a peaceful life.

Forest is neutered, fully vaccinated, and in good health. He weighs approximately 25 kg and measures around 50 cm in height and 70 cm in length.

This lovely boy has waited far too long for his chance at a forever home and would make a wonderful, loyal companion for the right family.

Full rescue backup and support throughout the adoption process and for the lifetime of the dog.

name: Walter
description:
Walter is a 4-year-old male Cross-Breed. He is a medium-sized dog weighing 26kg and is currently in North Lanarkshire, Scotland.

He is sadly searching for a new home after his owner experienced a serious health emergency and can no longer care for him.

Walter forms very strong bonds with his person and is described as incredibly cuddly and loving once he knows you. He and his previous owner were especially close, which makes this change particularly difficult for him.

Because of this, he can feel anxious around new people and unfamiliar dogs.

His anxiety can sometimes show itself as reactive behaviour. On one occasion, he redirected his fear and did use his teeth on his adopter, which highlights that he needs understanding and careful management.

He can also be startled by sudden movements, which can add to his worries in new situations.

Despite this, Walter is not without his softer and more social side. He can be super friendly with other dogs and is able to play very nicely with them. With the right introductions and calm guidance, he has the potential to enjoy canine company.

Walter’s ideal home would be an adult-only environment. He needs patient people who are willing to give him a second chance and help him feel safe again. A calm household with a steady routine would help him build confidence over time.

One of Walter’s absolute favourite activities is running around in a secure field. In these safe spaces, he recalls beautifully and clearly enjoys the freedom to move. This kind of outlet will be important for his wellbeing and happiness.

name: Mason
description:
Meet Mason, a 4 year old male Newfoundland cross Belgian Malinois Cross who is large in size and has a sensitive nature with lots of love to give once he builds trust.

Mason was born in approximately April 2021. He weighs around 30 kilograms and appears to have Newfoundland and Belgian Malinois heritage.

Mason is a handsome golden boy with a gentle soul. He is affectionate, a little goofy, intelligent, and sometimes charmingly stubborn.

With the people he knows and trusts, Mason is a gentle and loving presence. He likes to sit nearby, enjoys calm affection when fully awake, and finds comfort in being close to his people.

He is very food motivated, which makes training enjoyable and effective, and he gets excited when the lead comes out, as walks are one of his favourite activities.

Mason can be wary of strangers at first. He may bark and keep his distance until he has had a chance to assess the situation. Once he realises someone is safe, he relaxes and shows his friendly, tail-wagging side.

With other dogs: Mason is very friendly and enthusiastic. He enjoys meeting other dogs, approaches with excitement, and loves a good sniff. He may attempt to mount, so continued training and guidance will help him learn polite greetings.

With cats: Mason is not suitable to live with cats, as he will bark and attempt to chase.With visitors: Mason finds unfamiliar people overwhelming and will bark and retreat if approached.Around noise: Loud or sudden noises can worry him, and he will look to move somewhere quieter.

Mason can be reactive in certain situations, especially if startled when asleep or approached while tired. He needs patient guardians who can read his signals, give him space when needed, and continue building his confidence using positive methods.

He can be stubborn, particularly if he is comfortable or wants to go a different direction on a walk, but he responds well to calm and consistent guidance.

Health and groomingMason sheds lightly throughout the year, with heavier seasonal moults, so regular brushing is needed. He may experience mild skin irritation after running through long grass, which can be managed with seasonal allergy tablets.

Mason’s ideal homeMason will thrive in a home that can offer experienced adult owners who understand reactive or sensitive dogs, a calm and predictable environment, and a secure garden. Another friendly dog could be beneficial for companionship, but this is not essential.

Why Mason is worth itMason is a wonderful dog with great potential. With the right home, patience, and understanding, he will form a deep bond and show his affectionate and playful nature. He is loyal, intelligent, food motivated, and eager to be part of a stable and loving home where he feels safe.

If you have experience with reactive dogs and can provide the steady environment Mason needs, he will reward you with trust, companionship, and plenty of golden-furred affection.

name: Mara
description:
Welcome lovely Mara, a 1 year 6 month old female Cross-Breed.

Lovely Mara is a beautiful and friendly girl who was rescued as a young pup after being mistreated. She has been safe at the shelter since September 2024, where she has continued to grow in confidence and personality.

Despite her difficult start in life, Mara has blossomed into a cheeky, affectionate dog who enjoys human companionship. She can live happily with other dogs and can be cat tested if needed. With sensible introductions, she may be able to live with older, dog-savvy children.

As a young dog, Mara will need ongoing training and guidance to help her learn and settle into home life, and she would benefit from owners who are patient and committed to continuing positive training.

Mara is comfortable being on her own and can be left for a few hours, making her a good match for a home that is not always busy. She would really benefit from a home with access to a secure garden, as she enjoys spending time outdoors.

Mara is spayed, fully vaccinated, and in good health. She weighs approximately 20 kg and measures around 55 cm in height and 70 cm in length.

This lovely young girl would thrive in a home that can offer her love, stability, and the chance to enjoy life beyond the shelter. Mara truly deserves a family of her own where she can continue to grow and feel safe.

Full rescue backup and support throughout the adoption process and for the lifetime of the dog.

name: Maddox
description:
Maddox is now in foster in Hartlepool. Looking for adoption.

He is a gentle giant. Very calm, great with all dogs & people. Walks well on the lead.

Maddox is a large dog, weighing about 40 kg and standing approximately 60 cm tall.

He is a big, friendly, gentle giant who has waited a long time for his forever home.

Maddox is a great dog who simply loves other dogs and adores humans. With his lovable and fun nature, Maddox would make a wonderful addition to any home.

He is neutered, fully vaccinated, and microchipped, ensuring that he is ready for his new life in the UK.

Once all checks have been completed, Maddox will be delivered directly to your door.

The adoption comes with lifetime rescue backup, providing ongoing support.

Maddox’s gentle and affectionate personality makes him an ideal candidate for a loving home, where he can finally find the happiness he deserves.

He eagerly awaits the chance to become a cherished member of a family, ready to share his love and joy.

name: Sylvester
description:
Meet Sylvester, a 1 year old male Cross-Breed, a young boy who has had a bit of an unlucky start since coming over to the UK as a puppy.

Having already been surrendered twice, he is currently in a foster home that does not suit him as well as originally hoped.

Sylvester would adore a retired family or someone who works from home, as he suffers from quite severe separation anxiety.

His foster has been working on this, but he is likely to take a step backwards again when he moves, as he simply does not know where to call home anymore.

He is anxious around the male in the home, although he has previously lived with men without any reaction.

His foster is struggling to walk him, as he can be anxious outside, so he will need an experienced and confident owner who is comfortable walking a nervous dog.

Sylvester thrives around other dogs and takes both confidence and comfort from them. He would love to live with a confident canine companion who can help guide him, with plenty of playtime along the way too.

NeuteredVaccinatedMicrochippedBlood tests completedFlea treatedWormedPassport ready

Sylvester needs a patient, understanding home where he can finally feel safe and secure. With the right environment and support, he has the potential to truly blossom.

name: Hector
description:
Hector is an absolutely gorgeous little terrier mix that turns 8 in April 2027.

He was surrendered to us when his owner was suffering with mental health issues and was no longer able to give him the care he needs, we know he has multiple homes prior to the latest one.

He has a lovely character that will melt you and he would make a fantastic companion for someone who likes the slower pace of life and a little buddy to talk to.

Hector is a happy little guy that would love a family or person of his own, he absolutely loves food and snuggles – in no particular order! Hector is an inquisitive little guy.

He likes to follow you around and has to know what’s going on, he is also a very laid back little lad perfect for an older person looking for a companion.
