When Hector first arrived he was pretty shell shocked, but as he has settled in his personality is shining through. He loves to run around with the other dogs in a secure field and he loves to sniff everything.

He has fab recall and walks lovely on a lead; he travels well and is an all round little pleasure to have. He weights 7.7kg.

Hector lives with both dogs and cats and is absolutely fine with both – unless they go to steal his food, then he will shout at them!

He is a comical little lad that always makes me laugh, especially when such a tiny little guy manages to hog so much of the bed!

He absolutely adores other dogs so could happily live with other dogs, that said he is also a very independent little man so would be happy as the only dog in the home as well. He is also fantastic with cats so can happily live with cats.

Hector is fine to be left for short periods and is a quiet little lad, not a huge barker like most smaller breeds. He will happily cuddle up in his bed. He is house trained however will scent mark in a new environment.

Hector is a gorgeous happy little man that so desperately needs a forever home and family to grow up with. Hector is neutered and recently had a dental, he is microchipped de flead and wormed.

name: Goldie
description:
Our extra special girl Goldie is approximately two and a half years old and is an incredibly pretty small cross breed.

Goldie weighs a perfect ten kilos and measures thirteen inches from shoulder to paw. Having been found abandoned on the streets, Goldie has been in our Cyprus shelter for a number of months.

Goldie has an enviable reputation as being the absolute favourite amongst the shelter staff, volunteers and visitors. She is so attractive with a huge presence. Goldie has a gorgeous rich tan coat and truly lovely eyes.

Our shelter manager describes Goldie as calm and sweet albeit a little timid at first encounters. Goldie is longing to find her forever home as she so adores human contact.

She so cherishes a hug, a cuddle and lap. Goldie’s adopter will be blessed with a lovely lifelong companion who will be exceptionally low maintenance.

Goldie enjoys her time in the car and seems to mix perfectly well with other dogs and children. She does however show fear of cats.

name: Shelby
description:
Shelby is a 6-year-old male Rottweiler. He came into rescue due to his owner’s ill health, meaning he needs a new home through no fault of his own. His background explains a lot about his sensitive but gentle nature.

He was rescued as a puppy after being found tied to a tree with a head injury, which has understandably shaped how he feels about handling. Because of this, he can be worried about touch until he feels safe and trusts the person with him.

Once he gets to know you, his true personality shines through and he shows what a really sweet boy he is. Calm, confident handling and a pocket full of treats help him relax quickly, and he will soon start initiating contact himself.

He enjoys company and would struggle in a home where he is left alone for long periods. If he is to be an only dog, he would need adopters who are around most of the time.

He could live with Wilma, who came into rescue with him, or with other large breed dogs following successful introductions at the rescue. He is not suitable to live with cats or young children.

He does have an underlying health condition, but it is currently causing him no issues and can be fully discussed with anyone interested in offering him a home. With the right environment, he has the potential to be a loyal and loving companion.

name: Shadow
description:
Please meet Spirited Shadow! Shadow is a beautiful German Shepherd that is 4 years old. He joined us when he was abandoned in a garden chained to the fence, nobody came forward for him.

When Shadow was in kennels he was very scared and reactive. Since being with us he has flourished and is a beautiful lad inside and out.

He seems to prefer women to men so we assume a man wasn’t very nice to him, although he is confident with both, his preference is always me given the choice.

Since joining the pack this guy has absolutely blossomed mentally. He is still young and has a lot to learn but would make a fantastic dog for someone who knows the breed and has experience with them.

On arrival, he had no social skills and just barked in their faces, but now he has learnt how to play and is a good lad.

He hasn’t had the training or socialisation he needs, so he is basically a blank canvas for his adopters to make into the perfect little lad we know is in there!

Since joining us, Shadow has come on in leaps and bounds and has much better manners around other dogs. He is an absolute gift for someone that wants to train a dog to do a job, as he is so eager to learn.

He isn’t the smartest shepherd I have met, but he is willing!

Shadow is crate trained and walks well on a lead, he has fab recall and loves going for a run with the other dogs. Sometimes he likes a ball, sometimes food wins! He travels well in the car and loves a routine!

Shadow would do well with an older similar breed role model, but equally could be the only dog if someone is around a lot. He can live with children age 13 years plus that are used to large breed dogs.

Shadow will make a fantastic dog for someone prepared to put in the time and training. He loves to have something in his mouth, and this keeps him out of trouble.

When he doesn’t have something to carry he will nip other dogs to heard them which sometimes gets him in trouble with them. When he has a toy to carry he doesn’t do this, only dropping the toy for treats!

Shadow is non destructive, house trained and happy to be left for short periods. Like most shepherds, he is fond of a bark although he is much better now that he has a routine and only barks to tell us he needs something.

Shadow mixes with dogs of all sizes but he can be a bit boisterous with the small dogs, he doesn’t realise his size and is basically a big dopey puppy at heart!

Shadow is a gorgeous dog that so desperately needs a forever home and family to grow up with.

name: Marty
description:
Marty is a wonderful Bull mastiff; he is approaching 2 years old.

Well, what can I say?! This lad is both stunning inside and out and can’t do enough for you.

He is so focused on his human family and eager to please, sometimes he can be a bit boisterous in his eagerness to do as his told, but he means well!

He especially loves to give you his paw, which is more of a whack than a gentle nudge when he wants attention. He is a happy bouncy pup full of playfulness and love once he knows you.

Like most Mastiffs, he can be aloof with new people but a treat usually wins him over. He has no idea of his size and does think he is a lap dog!!

Marty is fine with other dogs, in fact he adores them, but he does like space to himself at home, so he would be happiest as the only dog or with a large female dog. H

e is far too clumsy with smaller dogs, he is an absolute clown of a dog and his gormless expression makes me laugh all day.

He is just so dopey! The only dangerous thing about Marty is his lack of brain cells, he isn’t the brightest crayon in the box, but what he lacks in brains he sure makes up for is enthusiasm and Dopiness!

Marty is castrated, vaccinated microchipped, de flead and wormed.

Marty walks perfectly on the lead and also has impeccable recall, He is a total star in every way and would be an amazing addition to any household!

Marty can live with children age 13 years plus; due to his size he may knock smaller children over. Marty will need an owner with a good knowledge of the breed and previous experience.

Marty is house trained, travels well and is fine to be left for short periods. Marty knows sit stay paw, please, he is a very clever boy in that he will perform for treats!

Marty is a big baby and loves his home comforts, he shares my bed with me every night as he just adores his humans! Marty is still a pup so will need ongoing training and socialisation.

name: Wally
description:
Wally is one of 33 Brittanys who were kept together on a piece of land and used for hunting and showing.

When the land was put up for sale and the dogs needed to be moved on, one of the shelters we work with stepped in to get as many of them out as possible before they ended up in the hands of other hunters.

Initially, TSPP with a couple of other rescues were able to help 17 of the dogs, but sadly, the hunter wouldn’t give us the other dogs at the time.

A little further down the line, we were asked to help another eight of the Brittanys. We quickly agreed knowing we didn’t want to risk losing the chance to help them again. Sadly, that number dropped to seven and then in the end was just four.

Thankfully, those four have now made it to the shelter and have the chance of a much better life, just like they have always deserved.

Wally is a really lovely energetic and lively boy who loves to run around in the enclosed area at the shelter.

He gets on well with the other dogs he has met at the shelter and is very affectionate with people and becomes more affectionate once he gets to know you. He can live with older children and can be cat tested for the right home.

name: Bat
description:
Bat is a medium English Setter, 10 years old.

Bat is an adorable setter given by a hunter because he wasn’t wanted when he became too old.

He is a lovely laid back lad, who is very affectionate with people and loves nothing more than having a cuddle. However, he’s still a working setter and age is just a number with these dogs!

He still loves having a run around in the enclosed area at the shelter and getting all the sniffs!

Dogs like Bat are the ones that really break our hearts, after a lifetime of loyal service to a hunter they are tossed aside.

Thankfully this means Bat now has the chance of having the retirement he’s always deserved and we hope we can find it for him! He can live with children and can be cat tested for the right home.

name: Yair
description:
Yair is one of 33 Brittanys who were kept together on a piece of land and used for hunting and showing.

When the land was put up for sale and the dogs needed to be moved on, one of the shelters we work with stepped in to get as many of them out as possible before they ended up in the hands of other hunters.

Initially, TSPP with a couple of other rescues were able to help 17 of the dogs, but sadly, the hunter wouldn’t give us the other dogs at the time.

A little further down the line, we were asked to help another eight of the Brittanys. We quickly agreed knowing we didn’t want to risk losing the chance to help them again.

Sadly, that number dropped to seven and then in the end was just four. Thankfully, those four have now made it to the shelter and have the chance of a much better life, just like they have always deserved.

Yair is a very charming little Brittany. Sadly it’s clear that Yair hasn’t had the easiest start in life and isn’t used to human contact.

He struggles to stay still and is constantly on the move and tends to avoid human contact.

We know what affectionate dogs Brittany’s are so we hope that in a home once he’s had a chance to get to know that people aren’t anything to worry about, he will become the affectionate boy we know he is under all those nerves!

Yair would do best in an adult only household which he can navigate the world at his own pace, and a friendly resident dog or two to help show him the ropes. He can be cat tested for the right home.

name: Jett
description:
Handsome Jett is an eight year old Labrador/Pointer cross who has been lucky enough to be a well loved member of his family since arriving in the UK from Cyprus back in 2020.

Regrettably, through no fault of his own, we’re seeking a new home for Jett.

The arrival of young children has meant they simply don’t have the time he needs or deserves, so we’re looking for a family where he can enjoy plenty of time, love and attention.

His family will be very sad to see him go, but with building work and a growing family, they feel he would be happier with someone who has more time to dedicate to him.

Jett has a sweet, mellow temperament at home and loves being part of family life. He enjoys a fuss and plenty of attention, although he is also happy to settle in his bed when he needs some time to himself.

He can be a little anxious when meeting new people, particularly when visitors come to the home, but once he has had time to get to know them, he settles and becomes comfortable.

He also tends to feel more at ease with people who have dogs of their own.

Don’t let Jett’s calm nature at home fool you, though! Outside, he is a very energetic boy who loves running, charging about and following his nose.

He enjoys long walks, exploring new places and sniffing out interesting scents, and would be delighted to have an active family who can give him plenty of opportunities to stretch his legs and use his nose.

He particularly enjoys scent games, and a large garden or easy access to fields and woodland would be a real bonus.

Jett is a typical scent loving hound and can be keen to investigate wherever an interesting smell takes him. He does pull towards things he wants to sniff, but he has had training and can walk to heel when asked.

His recall has also been worked on, and he knows a good range of commands, including sit, lie down, paw, spin, roll over and wait.

He can enjoy off lead time in secure areas, but his nose can sometimes get the better of him, so open spaces need to be approached with care as is common with hounds.

Jett is friendly with other dogs and would enjoy having a canine companion in his new home. He can be a little nervous around larger dogs, although he is often keen to play, and his family feel he would enjoy having another dog to play with in the garden.

One thing to note is that he can sometimes be a little bit territorial around treats and chews, so these will need to be managed thoughtfully in a home with other animals.

Jett has been very good with children, although he doesn’t always realise his own size! When he gets excited, he can charge about without being aware of little ones in his path, so a home with slightly older children would be a better fit.

Jett is housetrained and is used to family life. He doesn’t have much interest in playing ball, but enjoys a game of tug of war and a bit of wrestling. He is a lovely, affectionate dog who is loyal, loving and enjoys being close to his people.

Jett is looking for a family who can give him the time and attention he deserves, with plenty of opportunities for long walks, sniffing and exploring.

A home with a garden and countryside walks nearby, and potentially another friendly dog for company, would suit him well. He has lots of affection to give and a lovely balance of calm companionship at home and energetic hound adventures outdoors.

With the time and space to enjoy life to the fullest, Jett will make a very rewarding addition to his new family.

name: Amlet
description:
Hello, friends! My name is Amlet, and I’m a sweet?natured, friendly black Labrador cross, around 7 years young. For the past three years I’ve been living at CyDRA shelter, patiently waiting for a forever home. Could it finally be with you?

I might not love labels, but I do embrace one classic Labrador trait with pride: I absolutely love food!

After what I’ve been through, I think I’ve earned it. I also love water—paddling in the sea, splashing in puddles, even a good hose?down makes me wiggle with joy.

And my favourite game is chasing my ball; I’m a keen fetch partner and will happily play until it’s time for cuddles and a nap.

You see, I spent my entire life chained up, barely surviving on scraps of food and little water. Then one day, everything changed.

A kind stranger saw me and contacted the vet services, who called in a rescue team. That’s how I finally got a chance at a better life—and moved into the shelter, where I learned what it means to be treated with love and respect.

Because of my difficult past, I can be a little unsure around other dogs at first. With slow, gentle introductions, I warm up—and once I trust, I love deeply.

I’ve happily shared my kennel with several female dog friends, and I do best in calm, respectful company.

There’s still so much of life I haven’t experienced—exploring new walks, splashing on adventures, playing ball in the garden, and cuddles on the couch—but I’m ready to start now.

I’m looking for a quiet, loving home where I can feel safe, relax, and show off my affectionate personality (and yes, my adorable fluffy tail).

*Peaceful and patient, with time for gentle training and reassurance.*Either as an only dog or with a calm female companion.*Access to outdoor fun—water play and ball games are my happy place!

I’m ready to pack my bags. Will you be the one to open your heart and welcome me home?

name: Lucy
description:
Lucy is a 4 month old chihuahua cross girl who is expected to be smaller medium size when fully grown. Lucy’s had a difficult start in life, she was found with her mum and sister in a deprived area where her mum had been badly treated.

Her past could have made her fearful, but luckily it didn’t, and Lucy is full of trust and love.

This beautiful girl is a happy, friendly puppy who loves cuddles and being close to people, she is a true lapdog. She is a true puppy, full of life, loves to play and explore. She is jolly happy girl with a fun character.

Lucy is a sweet affectionate puppy, she loves dogs and could happily live with a doggie mate or be the only dog in the home.

She is also happy around children and could live with older dog savvy kids.

We can also cat test her for the right applicant.

Lucy dreams of cuddles in bed, fun adventures, belly rubs and a family to love for the rest of her life.

Lucy is in Hungary and will travel to the UK once a home has been secured for her.

name: Lykos
description:
Lykos is a 7-8 year old mixed breed who sadly came into the shelter after his elderly owner passed away and none of his family members were able to take his dog in.

It’s always particularly sad to see dogs that are accustomed to living in a home try and adjust to the shelter, as it’s so overwhelming, confusing and scary for them.

Despite his slightly older age, Lykos has slowly but surely adapted well, and now he’s ready to find a forever home for his later years.

Lykos is around eight years old and is a sweet, calm boy with a gentle nature. Right now he’s sharing his kennel with a female dog who he enjoys hanging out with.

He was previously in a kennel on his own, so we think he’s quite liked having a friend come to join him.

Although he’s a little older than most of our other shelter residents, Lykos still really likes going out for walks and is well mannered on the lead.

He loves sniffing through the long grass, peeing on anything that’s already been peed on, and he also likes to just stand and observe, taking in his surroundings.

He enjoys basking in the sun on a warm day, and he’s also quite a nosey neighbour so he loves watching what everyone else is up to.

Lykos finds the close capacity of the kennels quite confronting, and he really doesn’t like being barked at by other dogs in surrounding kennels.

He would definitely prefer a calm household with a laidback lifestyle, and we don’t think he would be too fussed either way if he was the only dog, or if he shared with a resident dog.

He can be quite independent, but if he was homed with another dog we think he’d be happiest with a female simply based on his experience in the shelter.

Being an older dog, Lykos is looking for a patient family. Just because he’s been in a home before, it doesn’t mean he will adapt seamlessly, and he still requires understanding and time to settle in properly.

A UK companion home is still very different to a Cyprus companion home, and there will be a lot of change for him to navigate.

The perfect home for Lykos would be based in a calm, residential area, or semi-rurally, with direct access to a secure garden. He would suit an older family given his calmer nature, or a younger family just wanting to give a senior dog a happy life.

He’d enjoy leisurely walks in the woods or along the beach, but he won’t be too demanding in his exercise needs. As long as he has a comfortable bed and lots of attention, we think he’ll be very happy.

name: Aspen
description:
Aspen is a 10 month old Beagle mix who’s life got off to a very rocky start. He was abandoned as a young puppy in Cyprus and found seriously unwell with parvovirus.

After spending time in the vets and making a full recovery, he joined the shelter and eventually travelled to the UK as a foster.

Since arriving, it’s been a bit of a journey for him, and it’s taken time to really understand what he needs to feel settled and secure.

After struggling to find the right fit in a home environment, Aspen has spent the last couple of months in kennels, where he has surprised everyone with just how well he’s done.

With clear routines, patient handling and consistent care, he has really come into himself. He’s responded brilliantly to basic training, built very strong relationships with the staff and grown hugely in confidence.

Aspen is a clever, energetic young dog, but new and unfamiliar situations can still feel overwhelming for him, and are often made more challenging by the fact that he is deaf.

Aspen is great with people and has been incredibly sociable, affectionate and engaged with those caring for him. Everyone who has been involved with him at the kennels has been really charmed by his personality.

He’s a cheeky, busy puppy who loves cuddles, fuss and being the centre of attention. Once he feels safe, his personality really shines and he shows just how much he enjoys human company.

When it comes to other dogs, Aspen is more selective. While he has previously lived alongside other dogs, is kennelled parallel to other dogs, and can pass dogs calmly on walks, we think that overall he would be happiest as the only dog in the home.

We suspect that earlier experiences may have left him feeling automatically defensive, and giving him a space where he doesn’t have to share attention or resources will help him relax and feel secure.

We are looking for an adult only home without other pets. As Aspen is deaf, it’s important that his environment is predictable and calm, and we don’t feel it would be fair to place him in a home with children or cats.

He would thrive in a quieter, more rural setting with access to a garden and plenty of opportunity to burn off energy in a safe way.

Aspen is clever and has learned hand signals for certain commands, so he would love to continue with further training as he really likes to learn and engage.

Aspen needs a confident, committed adopter who understands that he’s a young dog who has had a lot of upheaval in a short space of time.

With the right people, he lights up and shows what a sweet, silly and loving boy he really is.

Experience with training or deaf dogs would be helpful but isn’t essential, as long as his new family are patient, open to learning and ready to give him the structure and stability he’s been missing.

name: Sully
description:
Sully is a 5 year old medium size male cross breed. He looks like someone accidentally shrunk a Rottweiler in the wash. He’s handsome, compact, and has mastered the art of looking at you as if he’s contemplating the meaning of life.

Sully’s story didn’t begin so happily, he was surrendered in Hungary by a British family along with several other dogs.

They arrived frightened of people, fearful of new experiences, and clearly hadn’t been shown the love, kindness and guidance that every dog deserves.

For Sully the world was a scary place initially. But then he saw people who were kind to him, spoke gently, and gave him time. And it didn’t take long for him to realise that not all humans let you down.

Today Sully is a completely different dog, he enjoys life and likes human company, and although he still has his moments of insecurity, he is now curious and not fearful of the world around him.

He is a loyal, kind natured boy, quite placid in temperament. He isn’t a high energy dog either who would need endless adventures and entertainment all through the day, but he will happily join you on your walks and then enjoy home time sharing the sofa with you.

What he really wants though is a family who won’t give up on him.

Sully is friendly with most dogs with sensible introductions, very excitable dogs are probably not the best match for him but he could happily live with a friendly placid dog.

He is friendly around children, too, but he would probably be best suited to an adult-only home as he is not used to the noise and chaos that can come with young children.

We can cat test him for the right applicant.

He would really love to leave his shelter days behind and start a new life.

And he comes with a special bonus in that he understands English!

Sully is in Hungary and will travel to the UK once the right family is found for him.

He comes neutered, microchipped, fully vaccinated, with an EU pet passport.

name: Prince
description:
Prince is a 20 month old Lurcher and he is looking for a new home. Although he’s not originally an Underdog, when we heard that he needed some support we wanted to try and help him.

Unfortunately, Prince is living in a home that is not suitable for his needs. He has been struggling in the city and needs a less overwhelming environment to call home.

He is also a very energetic boy, and is looking for an active, patient and understanding family.

Prince is just under two years old and is a sighthound mix. He was part of an accidental litter, and was bought as a puppy, but has consistently struggled in London and requires a more experienced handler.

With the support of a local day-care and dog walking business, Prince has had a lot more exposure to other dogs and new people, and he has made a lot of progress regarding his confidence and social skills.

We think this will continue to improve in a semi-rural area.

Prince is adorable and has a very loving, affectionate nature with those he knows. He loves to give cuddles and is really friendly once he has formed a bond with you.

He is however apprehensive of strangers, and needs time to get used to new people. Although Prince doesn’t like being in big groups of dogs in day-care setting, he is very happy on group walks and trots along happily with them.

Prince has been handled quite roughly in the past which has left him sensitive to touch. He has been muzzle trained to make vet visits more manageable, and he also wears this when on walks in case he meets a dog he feels uncomfortable around.

During the day, Prince is quite happy to be left alone for a few hours. He is housetrained and enjoys playing with toys. He has been conditioned to race after a ball when out on walks, so this is his primary source of exercise and he is very ball driven.

He has responded well to training and is generally a very good boy who is eager to please. He sits and waits for his food and takes treats nicely, but doesn’t like to be approached whilst he is eating.

Prince loves spending time in the countryside where he has more space to run around. He would love a home with a big garden and an active lifestyle, and he’s much calmer outside of the hustle and bustle of London.

We would love to see him get the second chance that he deserves in a more suitable home where he can get the attention, focus and training that he thrives on.

name: Lana
description:
Lana is a 4 month old chihuahua cross girl from Hungary who is expected to be smaller medium size when fully grown.

Lana has already had a difficult start in life, she was found with her mum and sister in a deprived area where her mum had been badly treated. Despite everything they have been through, Lana has chosen love over fear.

This beautiful girl is a happy, friendly puppy who loves cuddles and being close to people, she is a true lapdog. She has a slightly calmer nature than her sister, but still enjoys playing, exploring and having fun.

She is a sweet affectionate puppy who could happily live with a doggie mate or be the only dog in the home.

She is also happy around children and can live with older dog savvy kids.

We can also cat test her for the right applicant.

Lana has never known what it’s like to belong to a family of her own, but she’s ready to learn. She dreams of cuddles in bed, fun adventures, belly rubs and people to love for the rest of her life.

Lana is in Hungary and will travel to the UK once a home has been secured for her.

name: Fred
description:
Fred is a 9 year old male Golden Retriever Cross.

Our poor golden retriever beauty, Fred, was surrendered to the shelter days before his ninth birthday, after spending his entire life being owned.

Unfortunately, his family wouldn’t let him live indoors and refused to make the necessary arrangements to accommodate him living outdoors (which is legal in Cyprus), and veterinary services ended up getting involved.

Fred was extremely stressed when he was brought into the shelter and we’ve spent the last few weeks getting to know him and realising how much he’s actually missed out on over the years.

He may have had a family, but he has had minimal socialisation, very little training, no one to rely on and a lot of instability. In fact, three years ago we actually found Fred miles away from home.

He’d been living on a picnic site for weeks before he was reunited with his family via his microchip.

So now, in his senior years, Fred needs an entirely new beginning. He is looking for a patient, understanding and confident family who recognise that he needs time to adapt.

Although he’s nine years old, he’s very active, strong and bouncy, especially when he gets overexcited. He is therefore not suitable for a home with young children as he has no concept of his size and strength.

Being part retriever, Fred is absolutely obsessed with food. He knows how to sit, and he also offers a very gentle and polite paw, but he inhales his food and any kind of treat is welcome!

He also loves water and loves splashing around in the paddling pool on a hot day. And despite his older age, he’s really still a puppy at heart.

He loves his toys, especially a teddy that he can rip apart as he loves taking the stuffing out of things. He also enjoys playing tug with a rope toy, and chasing after a ball (although he’s not sure on the concept of fetch).

Fred hasn’t been very well socialised with other dogs and this is an area that needs some continued work. He is generally good with females, but the first time we introduced him to other dogs we could see in his body language that he just had no idea what to do.

He’s had very limited interactions with other dogs sadly, so he’s not ready to just go into any home and mingle with lots of resident dogs.

Fred does bond quickly with people though and responds really well to kindness. He is a silly, goofy boy with a huge heart and ultimately all he wants is to be adored. He loves a belly rub, he loves playing, and he is sociable and friendly.

He is looking for a family who recognise that he’s been let down over the years and needs a little more guidance, patient and understanding. There is SO much love in this dog, and in the right home he will absolutely blossom.

name: Gilly
description:
Gilly is a four month old cross-breed. Gilly’s litter, aka the G pups, arrived at the shelter in June after they were all found living together as strays without their mum.

They were terrified to begin with and spent a lot of time huddled together in their kennel, completely overwhelmed and frightened. After a few days they gradually started to get a bit braver, and now they’re ready for adoption.

Gilly is such a cutie and has a really joyful energy about her that makes it impossible not to love her. She gets so excited to spend time with people, and she gives so many kisses!

She’s also quite happy worming her way into your lap for a little rest while she takes in everything going on around her – she just loves being involved.

Gilly is a clever girl and is quick to learn new things. She has pretty much learned to sit for a treat already, and although she’s a bit suspicious of the lead at the moment she’s started to trust that it’s not a bad thing anymore.

She has an every wagging tail and a very happy personality, and as she’s very sociable we’re sure it won’t take long for her to make plenty of new friends!

Gilly is great with other dogs and would be more than happy living alongside a resident dog that she can learn from and play with.

She’s a very friendly girl and reads other dogs very well, but we also feel that she would be confident enough to be the only dog at home.

The ideal home for Gily would be a loving family home that are looking for a young dog to raise outside of the city. She would prefer a home with access to a garden, and this will also help with house training.

As she grows into an adult dog, she will be looking for a moderately active lifestyle, and as she clearly loves to learn she’d also benefit from (and enjoy!) some basic training.

At just four months old the G pups are still very much learning each and every day. There are lots of different personalities within their litter, but they’re all growing and changing at their own pace.

Each of them will need patient, understanding families who recognise that adapting to a companion lifestyle will be a very new concept for all of them, as they’ve never lived in a home before.

And as with any puppies, they will need continued socialisation, training, and plenty of company.

Gilly has had some initial exposure to children and we think she would be absolutely great living alongside kids. She is still a puppy, so it’s important that there are boundaries in place if she’s living alongside kids, for both parties!

But as she is so affectionate and playful we think she would love having little people to befriend. She’s a super little character and we know she’s going to make someone very happy!

name: Trixy
description:
Trixy is a 1.5-year-old, smaller medium crossbreed girl with a heart full of love. She was rescued from the streets alongside her mum (a Dachshund cross) and four siblings.

Three of the pups, including Trixy, are still waiting for their happy ending in a shelter in Hungary.

Trixy is a lively, playful young girl who sometimes shows a little shyness at first. But once she feels safe, her sweet, cuddly side shines through — she only needs love, patience, and kindness to truly thrive.

She adores playing with her doggie friends and gets along well with them.

She is friendly with people, including children, and enjoys her walks, trotting happily on the lead. Trixy would be happiest in a family where she isn’t left alone for long hours and is treated as a true member of the family — joining in on adventures, cuddles, and daily life.

She could easily share her home with another playful, gentle dog, or be the only pet, soaking up all the love and attention. Like all rescue dogs, she will need time, patience, and commitment from her new family to settle and blossom into the wonderful companion she is meant to be.

Trixy is currently in Hungary and can travel to the UK once her perfect family is found. She will come spayed, fully vaccinated, microchipped, and with an EU pet passport.

Adoption is subject to a home check and adoption fee. Full RBU provided.

name: Grant
description:
Grant is a four month old cross-breed. Grant’s litter, aka the G pups, arrived at the shelter in June after they were all found living together as strays without their mum.

They were terrified to begin with and spent a lot of time huddled together in their kennel, completely overwhelmed and frightened. After a few days they gradually started to get a bit braver, and now they’re ready for adoption.

At a glance, Grant looks just as confident as his siblings. He’s always at the bars of the kennel jumping up to meet new people with his brothers and sisters, and the fact that he’s the only pup in the litter with huge ears also draws a lot of attention to him.

However, Grant is actually the most nervous of the pups. As soon as he’s separated from his siblings, he is very unsure of what to do.

He is such a sweet, soft and gentle boy, and he just needs a slightly more patient, calm and understanding home who can go at his pace. We’ve seen so many pups like Grant in our time and the power of the perfect home cannot be underestimated!

Grant is a submissive boy and he’s always a little unsure around new people until he knows that they’re going to treat him with kindness.

When he gets to know you, he likes to just sit beside you and chill, and he loves an ear scratch or a belly rub.

He’s not confident on the lead yet so that will take a bit of work, but there’s not a bad bone in his body and he really does want to trust people, he just takes a little longer than his siblings.

Grant would be better suited to a home with another resident dog that he can learn from and play with. As soon as he’s away from his siblings, he panics and is visibly less confident.

Another dog would definitely help his transition from shelter to sofa, and help him feel less overwhelmed and confused.

The ideal home for Grant would be a loving, patient family home that are looking for a young dog to raise outside of the city.

As Grant is more nervous than his siblings, a calm home in a quieter area would be great for him, and we’re sure his confidence will grow once he’s settled and feeling more secure.

As he grows into an adult dog, he will be looking for a moderately active lifestyle, and some basic training.

At just four months old the G pups are still very much learning each and every day. There are lots of different personalities within their litter, but they’re all growing and changing at their own pace.

Each of them will need patient, understanding families who recognise that adapting to a companion lifestyle will be a very new concept for all of them, as they’ve never lived in a home before.

And as with any puppies, they will need continued socialisation, training, and plenty of company.

Grant is just a baby and has never had an adverse reaction to a child, but in order to keep things predictable for him we’re looking for a home with older children only.

He just needs some time and understanding to come out of his shell, and he’s only a few months old right now – he will change so much within the first few months of his adoption and it will simply take a special, caring family to give him the love and support he needs.

We’re already seeing glimpses of the silly, charming and playful little pup he is, and it will be so rewarding to see him really flourish with his new family.

attributes.Breed: Staffordshire bull terrier cross labrador retriever

name: Zelda
description:
Meet Zelda, a 2 year old female Staffordshire Bull Terrier cross Labrador Retriever — a brave and beautiful girl who has survived unimaginable cruelty yet still greets the world with love.

She came from hell. Zelda spent her early life chained so short she couldn’t even stand, the chain cutting deep into her neck. Despite such cruelty, she never lost her spark. Once freed, she greeted her rescuers with a wagging tail and a forgiving heart.

Now safe, she’s blossomed into an energetic, happy-natured girl. She’s medium-sized, affectionate, and adores people.

Zelda gets along well with other dogs — though she can be a bit boisterous in her play — and would thrive either as an only dog or with a friendly, tolerant companion.

In the kennel, she doesn’t get the exercise or freedom she craves, and she’s longing for a home where she can run, play, and finally just be a dog. She loves her walks, though she does pull on the lead, simply excited to be out exploring the world she missed for so long.

Zelda would suit an active home that can give her the exercise, structure, and affection she craves, so her joyful spirit can shine at long last. Older children will be considered.

Zelda has endured pain no animal should ever know. She deserves a life full of love, freedom, and fun.

Fully vaccinated, spayed, microchipped, with an EU pet passport. Ready to travel.

name: Gina
description:
Gina is a four month old cross breed. Gina’s litter, aka the G pups, arrived at the shelter in June after they were all found living together as strays without their mum.

They were terrified to begin with and spent a lot of time huddled together in their kennel, completely overwhelmed and frightened. After a few days they gradually started to get a bit braver, and now they’re ready for adoption.

Gina is very confident among the group and can be a bit bossy with her siblings! She is a girl who knows what she wants, and sometimes that is the limelight!

She is always very eager to say hello to passing visitors that walk by her kennel, and she loves any opportunity to be be cuddled or played with.

She also loves chasing after a toy, a pebble or a stick – it doesn’t matter what it is, she can make a game out of anything!

Gina isn’t familiar with the lead just yet, but she’s starting to learn that it’s a positive thing now. She is super excitable and bouncy when she gets the chance to interact with people, and she bonds fiercely with those that she loves.

She is definitely going to be a very loyal companion, we have no doubt about that.

Gina is good with other dogs and on the most part she gets along well with her siblings, but she needs a bit of work on sharing. She could definitely live alongside a resident dog, and an older, calmer dog would be a great influence on her.

However, we also think she is confident enough to be the only dog in the household.

The ideal home for Gina would be a loving family home that are looking for a young dog to raise outside of the city. She would prefer a home with access to a garden, and this will also help with house training.

As she grows into an adult dog, she will be looking for a moderately active lifestyle, and of course being a puppy she will both enjoy and benefit from some introductory training.

At just four months old the G pups are still very much learning each and every day. There are lots of different personalities within their litter, but they’re all growing and changing at their own pace.

Each of them will need patient, understanding families who recognise that adapting to a companion lifestyle will be a very new concept for all of them, as they’ve never lived in a home before.

And as with any puppies, they will need continued socialisation, training, and plenty of company.

Gina has had some initial exposure to children and we think she would be great for a family with school age children. She can be a bit nippy in her play, but that is purely to do with her age.

She is still a puppy, so it’s important that there are boundaries in place if she’s living alongside kids, for both parties! Given the opportunity, we know Gina is going to grow up into a lovely young dog with a great personality and nothing but devotion for her new family.

name: Agika
description:
Agika is a 1 year old female Cross-Breed. She is a small cross-breed girl looking for her forever family.

This little girl has suffered so much in her short life; still, she is a little miracle. She was rescued from a heartbreaking situation where she had been kept on a short chain that had grown deep into her neck.

Once she was released, the chain had to be surgically removed.

Despite a truly rough start, Agika is a real sweetheart—loving, affectionate, and full of life. When she was rescued, she was timid and afraid of the world.

However, she soon left her old self behind, learned that some people can be trusted, and has grown into a joyful dog who loves life, loves other dogs, and now loves people too.

She walks nicely on the lead and looks forward to her walks, which she does not get many of.

She loves attention and will happily accept any amount of cuddles or affection. Agika is ready to start a new life in a safe, loving home where she will be treated the way she has always deserved.

She wants to be part of the family and discover all the things she has not yet had the chance to see or sniff.

Experience with rescue dogs is preferred but is not essential, as all applications are assessed individually.

Agika is in Hungary and will travel to the UK once a home has been secured for her. She comes spayed and fully vaccinated, with an EU pet passport.

Adoption is subject to a home check and adoption fee. Full rescue backup is provided.

name: Godfrey
description:
Godfrey is a four month old cross-breed. Godfrey’s litter, aka the G pups, arrived at the shelter in June after they were all found living together as strays without their mum.

They were terrified to begin with and spent a lot of time huddled together in their kennel, completely overwhelmed and frightened. After a few days they gradually started to get a bit braver, and now they’re ready for adoption.

Godfrey is a sweetheart and it took us a little bit longer to earn his trust than some of his siblings. The girls are definitely more confident than their brothers in this litter!

Once Godfrey realised that he was safe, he ventured out to explore his new surroundings and he has been quite taken with the toys, the paddling pool (or the water bowl if the pool isn’t filled!) and the fact that so many treats are on offer! He’s realised it’s not so bad after all.

Godfrey is really cute when he gets to spend some 1-2-1 time with the volunteers, and he really enjoys being the centre of attention for a little while.

Although you can tell he’s a little unsure, he revels in the fuss and loves being cuddled and tickled. He’s a very loving little dog and once his initial nerves have subsided he’s quite the snuggler, and he also gives excellent kisses.

He’s not familiar with the lead just yet, but when he’s outside in the yard sniffing about he’s very curious about other dogs, and bravely approaches to give them a little sniff before running back to safety! He’s also one of the smaller pups of the litter.

Godfrey is great with other dogs and would be more than happy living alongside a resident dog that he can learn from and play with.

He’s a very friendly boy and reads other dogs very well, and we think he would probably prefer a home with another dog, but we’re open to considering placing him on his own if we think it’s the right fit.

The ideal home for Godfrey would be a loving family home that are looking for a young dog to raise outside of the city. He would prefer a home with access to a garden, and this will also help with house training.

As he grows into an adult dog, he will be looking for a moderately active lifestyle, and he would also do well with some basic training.

At just four months old the G pups are still very much learning each and every day. There are lots of different personalities within their litter, but they’re all growing and changing at their own pace.

Each of them will need patient, understanding families who recognise that adapting to a companion lifestyle will be a very new concept for all of them, as they’ve never lived in a home before.

And as with any puppies, they will need continued socialisation, training, and plenty of company.

Godfrey has had some initial exposure to children and we think he would be suitable to live alongside slightly older children, as he can still sometimes be a little skittish.

He is still a puppy, so it’s important that there are boundaries in place if he’s living alongside kids, for both parties! Godfrey is such a little heartbreaker and we know that someone isn’t going to be able to stop themselves falling in love with his charming little face – and we don’t blame you!

name: Grace
description:
Grace is a four month old cross-breed. Grace’s litter, aka the G pups, arrived at the shelter in June after they were all found living together as strays without their mum.

They were terrified to begin with and spent a lot of time huddled together in their kennel, completely overwhelmed and frightened. After a few days they gradually started to get a bit braver, and now they’re ready for adoption.

Grace is one of the most confident pups in the litter, and even within the first couple of days after she arrived in the shelter she has been brave enough to approach new people, interact and cuddle.

Some of the other pups follow her lead as she’s a very sociable little thing and loves to be in the company of people. She warms to anyone and everyone very quickly and is definitely ready to find a family of her own.

Grace is very food motivated and was the first of the litter to learn ‘sit’. She is also accepting of the lead, which can sometimes be a bit scary for new puppies to adapt to, but she’s taken everything in her stride and learns new things fast.

She loves a belly rub, any excuse to be as close to you as possible, and she’s also very playful – the perfect all rounder!

Grace is great with other dogs and would be more than happy living alongside a resident dog that she can learn from and play with. She’s a very friendly girl and reads other dogs very well, but we also feel that she would be confident enough to be the only dog at home.

The ideal home for Grace would be a loving family home that are looking for a young dog to raise outside of the city. She would prefer a home with access to a garden, and this will also help with house training.

As she grows into an adult dog, she will be looking for a moderately active lifestyle, and as she clearly loves to learn she’d also benefit from (and enjoy!) some basic training.

At just four months old the G pups are still very much learning each and every day. There are lots of different personalities within their litter, but they’re all growing and changing at their own pace.

Each of them will need patient, understanding families who recognise that adapting to a companion lifestyle will be a very new concept for all of them, as they’ve never lived in a home before.

And as with any puppies, they will need continued socialisation, training, and plenty of company.

Grace has had some initial exposure to children and we think she would be absolutely great living alongside kids. She is still a puppy, so it’s important that there are boundaries in place if she’s living alongside kids, for both parties!

But as she is so affectionate and playful we think she would love having little people to befriend. She’s a wonderful young dog and we can’t wait to find her the perfect family to grow up with.

name: Malna
description:
Malna is a 3 year old crossbreed girl, she was dumped on the roadside along with her sister at about 2.5 months of age. She is medium size, weight: 15 kg, shoulder height: 44 cm.

Malna is a lovely girl, she is friendly and kind and loves everyone. She is energetic and playful and sociable around her doggie mates.

She enjoys nothing more than running around in the fields with other dogs, playing a chase. She cooperates nicely with humans too and is very kind with humans.

She enjoys car rides and is good around children too. She also walks nicely on the lead.

Malna would be best suited for a family where she is not left alone for extended periods and she is included in her family’s activities. She would be happiest in an active family, she would happily be your company on long walks, hikes and holidays.

Older dog savvy children will be considered.

Malna would probably be happiest living with another playful dog but she could also live happily as the only dog and the centre of attention in her home.

As all rescue dogs, she will need time, patience, love and commitment from her adopting family to become a happy, well-balanced dog.

Malna is currently in Hungary and can travel to the UK as soon as the right family is found for her.

She comes spayed, fully vaccinated, microchipped, dewormed, flea and tick treated, with an EU passport and DEFRA approved paperwork.

Adoption is subject to Home Check and Adoption fee. Full RBU provided.

name: Bonnie
description:
Bonnie is a two year old Pointer mix who was found as a stray and had been hiding in abandoned buildings across open farmland for a while before she was able to be caught.

The vet confirmed she had not been microchipped, and as she’d been roaming for a while it was clear she’d not come from a home.

She was rescued from agricultural land where strays are often found, and unsurprisingly, no one came to the shelter to claim her as their own.

Bonnie arrived just after Christmas and has been in the shelter without any interest ever since. She was absolutely terrified when she first arrived, and was so avoidant of people.

She didn’t want anyone to touch her, and would hide in the back of her kennel when anyone approached. She was then paired up with a confident male dog who has zero fear of anyone or anything, and slowly she started to realise that she was safe.

Bonnie is now a different dog. She’s still a little bit reserved and needs time to trust new people, but she’s much more friendly, so much happier, and she’s really come out of her shell in the past few months.

She is more confident in the company of other dogs, and she’s really benefitted from having a kennel friend to learn from and follow their lead. This in mind, we think she would be better suited to a home with another calm, resident dog.

Bonnie would struggle in a loud home in a busy area, so we’re looking for a laid-back home atmosphere based in a calmer residential, or semi-rural location.

She would love to be surrounded by fields and nature walks, rather than roads and buildings, and she is definitely looking for a home with direct access to a secure garden.

We know that given the time she needs, and a gentle, patient approach, Bonnie will absolutely blossom and she’ll make an amazing companion with a little time and understanding.

Bonnie has had some introductory lead training, and has responded well, but still needs a bit more work. She is a relatively active dog and would welcome long walks, but is also quite happy basking in the sun on a warm day.

Given that she’s a shyer dog, we are looking for a home with children aged 8+, so as not to overwhelm her. There’s not a bad bone in her body, but she’d struggle with a very unpredictable household, and would prefer a calm home.

Bonnie absolutely deserves a second chance and we know that given the patience that she needs, she will do so well in a new home.

She spent a long time in survival mode, so she just needs a secure environment to understand that she doesn’t have to look out for herself all the time – she’ll be treated with kindness, love and affection.

She’s already grown in confidence and made great progress in the shelter, so in a proper home she’s going to do just fine.

name: Tango
description:
Tango is a 2 year old male Cross-Breed. He was saved from the streets with his 4 siblings and their mum, who is a Dachshund cross.

Tango is a very kind-natured boy—friendly, affectionate, and playful. He has a beautiful, friendly look and a well-proportioned build. He loves people and enjoys a lively, playful lifestyle.

He is very social with his doggie mates and plays well with them.

Tango would be best suited for a family where he is not left alone for extended periods and is treated as a family member. He would love to go on nice adventures! He will need time to settle into his new home, and his training will need to be continued.

He could live happily with another friendly, playful dog or as the only dog in the home, being the centre of attention.

As with all rescue dogs, he will need time, patience, love, and commitment from his adopting family to become a happy, well-balanced dog. Experience with rescue dogs is preferred.

Tango is currently in Hungary and can travel to the UK once the right family is found for him.

He comes fully vaccinated, microchipped, dewormed, flea and tick treated, with an EU passport and DEFRA-approved paperwork.

Adoption is subject to a home check and adoption fee. Full RBU provided.

name: Jordan
description:
Jordan is a three year old Pointer mix. He’s super shiny, super sleek, this gorgeous boy is Jordan He arrived at the shelter along with two other pointers, all of whom were found roaming as strays at the end of the hunting season.

The three of them are happy in each other’s company, and now they share a kennel together. As their individual personalities have emerged we’ve been getting to know them, and now we would love to find each of them their perfect forever home.

Jordan is around three years old and such a nice boy! Unfortunately, we don’t think that Jordan has experienced the kindest treatment throughout his life, and it has meant that it’s taken us a little more time to convince him that we’re to be trusted.

He has however responded so well to reassurance and kindness, and is now much more confident and sociable. He now really likes going out for little walks with the shelter volunteers, and he always looks to them for a bit of guidance or a cuddle.

Around other dogs, Jordan is really friendly. He is a bit of a goon and loves to play, but he’s also friendly and gentle, especially when meeting new dogs.

He is good with both males and females, and we definitely think that he would really enjoy a home where he had another resident dog to learn from and play with.

Having another dog to observe and learn from will allow Jordan to adapt at his own pace, and with someone to look up to, to boost his confidence.

Jordan would be best suited to a semi-rural home where he’s surrounded by lots of places to explore. Being a pointer, he loves to follow his nose and he’s always curious about his surroundings.

He would also be best suited to a home with a garden, as it’s likely that he has spent the vast majority of his life living outdoors in some capacity.

A garden will provide Jordan with a safe outdoor space where he can acclimatise to living indoors little by little.

Jordan has already started to show us that when he trusts someone he is super affectionate and sweet, and given proper time to bond with a new family we know that he is going to develop a really strong, loyal connection with them.

Pointers are such fantastic companions and given the opportunity to settle into a secure and loving environment, we know Jordan will really blossom in confidence.

name: Junior
description:
Junior is a 3-year-old male Dachshund Cross. He was rescued from a deprived area of Hungary in very poor condition and has since been given a second chance at life. Despite everything he has been through, he has remained a sweet and affectionate little dog.

He has been waiting patiently while other dogs around him have found homes, yet he has somehow been overlooked. This is especially sad because he is described as a lovable and funny boy who truly enjoys human company.

More than anything, he is simply longing to be part of a family of his own.

Junior walks nicely on the lead and enjoys getting out and about. He loves people and shows a gentle and friendly nature in his interactions. His kind temperament also means he is patient when around children.

When it comes to other dogs, Junior’s preference is for female dogs. He would be happiest living with a spayed female companion or as the only dog in the home where he can soak up all the attention.

This flexibility means he could suit different home setups, as long as his social preferences are respected.

He comes neutered, fully vaccinated, and microchipped, which gives his future family reassurance about his health care. He also has an EU pet passport, making his travel arrangements clear and straightforward.

A home check and adoption fee will apply, and full rescue back-up is provided for added support.

Junior is a small dog at approximately 10 kg, making him a manageable size for many households. His journey has not been easy, but his gentle nature and cheerful personality have stayed intact.

He is ready to leave his difficult past behind and finally enjoy the comfort and security of a loving home.

name: Indie
description:
Indie is a three year old Shepherd mix who was brought into the shelter after locals notified the dog warden that she had been roaming freely around the village for a few weeks.

No one seemed to know where she’d come from, or was able to advise who she belonged to. With no microchip to help us connect the dots she ended up in the shelter, and is now waiting for a new home.

Indie is a beautiful girl who just blends in at the shelter.

She doesn’t ask for much, she doesn’t demand attention, and she shares her kennel with two very silly male dogs who she is extremely tolerant and gentle with, despite their complete lack of spatial awareness or manners!

She is very patient with other dogs and gets on well with them, but equally would be fine to be homed as the only resident dog, as she’s quietly confident and independent.

Indie is a very clever girl and loves her treats. As she’s food motivated this will really help with any further training her new family might want to do with her, as she responds really well to positive reinforcement.

It’s likely that Indie is a shepherd mix, so she will enjoy training, enrichment and brain games, as dogs like her thrive with focus and direction.

The ideal home for Indie would be an active family who can offer her plenty of opportunities to explore and are looking for a loyal, devoted companion to accompany them on their adventures.

Indie bonds with new people quickly and is a very loving dog, so we think she will adapt to a companion lifestyle well.

Indie would be happiest in a semi-rural setting where she’s surrounded by nice places to walk, fields to roam through or woods to wander in.

She would welcome trips to the beach or long hikes at the weekend, and she will be able to keep up with a more active pace of life. We’re sure she’ll be very excited to experience home comforts as well though!

We don’t know if Indie has ever had the opportunity to have her own bed or even live indoors before, so her family need to be patient while she adjusts in her own time. For anyone looking for a loyal best friend, Indie would be perfect.

name: Aspen
description:
Meet Aspen, a 6 month old male Hound Cross with a bright, affectionate personality and an incredible story of resilience.

Born in March 2025, this handsome pup started life in Cyprus, where he was found abandoned and seriously ill with parvovirus — a condition often fatal in unvaccinated puppies.

Thanks to expert veterinary care, Aspen made a full recovery and has since travelled to the UK, where he’s settling beautifully into foster life in South East London.

Being deaf doesn’t hold Aspen back one bit. In fact, it gives him an edge — city noises that might unsettle other rescue dogs don’t faze him at all. He’s confident out and about, curious, and absolutely loves exploring the outdoors.

Aspen is friendly, trusting, and full of character. He adores people and thrives on interaction, soaking up every bit of affection he’s offered. He’s clever, food-motivated, and loves one-to-one training sessions — anything that earns him praise or treats.

He can live with other friendly dogs but would also be happy as the only dog in a home that gives him plenty of attention.

Aspen’s best suited to a homewithout cats or small animals, and he’d do great withdog-savvy children aged 8 and upwho understand he’s still in that bouncy, mouthy puppy phase.

Aspen would love a home with access to a garden where he can play off lead. His ideal family will be home most of the day and able to build up his confidence being left alone gradually.

With patience, structure, and love, Aspen will grow into the loyal, affectionate companion he’s meant to be.

name: Suzy
description:
Suzy is a 1.5 year old female Cross-Breed, medium in size. She was rescued exactly a year ago from horrid circumstances, having been thrown into a yard with her brother, Tommy, at just a few weeks of age.

They lived on piles of rubbish, frequently escaping due to inadequate fencing and roaming the streets among busy traffic, constantly in danger. When rescued, they were emaciated and full of parasites.

Suzy has grown to be a kind-natured, healthy girl who is active and playful according to her age. She is medium-sized and has a lovely cheeky character. She loves people and is very friendly around kids, too.

She is also playful and happy around other dogs.

Suzy is perhaps slightly more reserved than her brother and enjoys doggie company a lot. She loves to play and run with her mates.

Suzy would be happiest in a family where she is not left alone for extended periods and there is time for her training. We want her to be treated as a treasured member of the family and be taken on nice adventures. She will need time to settle into her new home and get used to her environment.

Suzy could happily live with another friendly and playful dog or dogs but may also be happy being the only dog and the centre of attention in the family.

As with all rescue dogs, she will need time, patience, love, and commitment from her adopting family to become a happy, well-balanced dog.

Experience with rescue dogs is preferred.

Suzy is currently in Hungary and can travel to the UK as soon as the right family is found for her.

She comes spayed, fully vaccinated, microchipped, dewormed, flea and tick treated, with an EU passport and DEFRA-approved paperwork.

Adoption is subject to a home check and adoption fee. Full RBU provided.

name: Cece
description:
Cece is an 18 month old Shepherd mix who arrived at the shelter as an unclaimed stray, a story we’ve heard many a time. No one came looking for her, and she had no microchip or collar, so who knows where she came from.

She was however in good health, and happy to meet new people, so we’re hopeful that she’s not had a difficult start in life.

Cece is around a year and a half old and she is a beautiful girl with a very happy, friendly and sociable personality. She loves being around people and is very eager to please, quietly confident, and reads other dogs well.

It took a little while for her to initially calm down when she first arrived in the shelter as she had some nervous energy to burn off, but once we’d found her the ideal kennel mates and she’d had some time to decompress, her true nature started to shine through.

As mentioned, Cece now shares her kennel with multiple other dogs of various sizes, ages and energy levels. She’s loving having the opportunity to make new friends and enjoys playing with them and just being in their company.

While we don’t feel she’s dependant on other dogs, she definitely likes hanging out with them, and she’s more than happy to share her bed, which is so cute.

18 months old is still young, so Cece would benefit from some basic training to help refine her manners a little. She learnt to sit in no time, despite all the distractions around her in the shelter.

As she is food motivated, this works really well as a reward. When she’s excited to see you Cece is prone to jumping up a bit, but it doesn’t take long for this to pass and with some routine and a proper home setting, we’re confident that is very trainable.

The ideal home for Cece would be with a family who enjoy time outdoors, have direct access to a secure garden, and who are keen to invest some time into a young dog learning about a whole new world.

We think the outskirts of the city would be preferable for Cece, or of course a more rural setting would suit her just fine too.

She’d enjoy a fairly active lifestyle, and with some time and patience we think she will make a brilliant addition to a family home.

name: Maggie
description:
Maggie is a 1 year old female Cross-Breed, expected to be medium-sized when fully grown.

She is currently in Hungary and is adorable and playful, as expected for her age.

Seven siblings were born in an abandoned property with their mum struggling to feed them when she was emaciated herself.

They were taken in by the local shelter at three weeks of age.

The whole litter was stunningly beautiful, and only two pups are still waiting for their families.

Maggie is fully vaccinated, free from parasites, and ready to travel. She comes with an EU passport.

She can live with dogs and older children. The right owner will need to agree to have her spayed once fully grown.

name: Cassie
description:
Cassie is a one year old Shepherd mix and was found running through farmland when a local rescuer was able to coax her into her car and take her to safety.

Surprisingly, during her check up at the vets they discovered that she actually had a registered microchip, so they were able to track down her owners and asked them to come and collect her.

But of course, had the story ended positively, then Cassie wouldn’t be on our website. Sadly, her family said they didn’t want her anymore as she was too energetic, and that the rescuer could rehome her.

There was no sense of remorse or accountability, they just gave her away and moved on with their lives.

Cassie is a shepherd mix and she is indeed an energetic, active and highly intelligent young dog. She’s estimated to be just under a year old, and she is always raring to get outside and go on an adventure.

Right now, she’s in private kennels where she’s safe and sound until she finds her forever home, but she needs more exercise and enrichment than they can offer her, and as a result whenever she goes out for a run in the yard she is like a coiled spring.

Cassie is looking for a family who have had high energy dogs before and can give her the physical and mental outlets that she needs to thrive. She is so, so loyal and bonds with people very quickly.

She’s extremely keen to please and eager to learn, and as she’s so food motivated this makes the perfect reward!

Cassie would be best suited to a home outside of the city with an active family who enjoy running, exploring and just generally being outdoors.

When her needs are met, like any dog, Cassie is a bundle of love and loves hanging out with people. She’s also great with other dogs, especially those of a similar energy level to her, and she loves racing around in the grass with them.

She would also be best suited to a home with a reasonable size garden, as she really likes being outdoors.

Cassie may be young and bouncy, but she also has lots of love to give. She is the perfect dog for someone seeking a best friend, adventure partner and a companion that they can train.

name: Noah
description:
Noah is a two year old cross breed and is every bit the silly goofball that he looks to be in his photos. We love this daft boy, and he came to us a few weeks ago after being found as yet another wandering stray.

Unfortunately for Noah, in terms of appearance he is the kind of dog that we often see overlooked for a long time – we don’t know why, they just always seem to take longer!

We’re hoping that just maybe he’ll get lucky before he has to spend months on end behind bars.

Noah is around two years old and full of fun. He is such a positive dog and despite his life in the shelter being relatively boring, any moment of excitement that he does get to experience, he does so with 100% enthusiasm.

He loves any kind of human interaction and is beside himself with happiness when someone goes into his kennel to spend time with him. He’s a very sociable, human focused dog and just wants to be loved.

Noah shares his kennel with a quiet, older female dog, and despite his energy he understands that he needs to give her some space and calm down when she’s not feeling it.

He seems to be able to read canine body language well, and we think he could live with or without other dogs.

He appreciates their company and seems to enjoy an opportunity to play when it’s offered, but he is also very people oriented so doesn’t depend on other dogs to feel secure and confident.

Noah is young and still very bouncy at times, although a lot of this is due to lack of exercise and no outlets for his excitement.

With a proper routine and lots of lovely long walks, we’re sure he will calm down, but it would still be in his best interest to have some entry level training, to learn the basics and improve his manners.

He is so keen to please and very food motivated, so he loves to learn! He has already perfected a very nice ‘sit’ in the shelter, and looks extremely proud of himself whilst doing so.

Noah has a huge heart and so much love to give. He’s looking for an active home with a garden, someone up for the fun that a younger, more energetic dog can bring into their household, and someone that can also shower him in the love that he craves.

He will make the absolute best friend once he’s had a chance to settle in and find his feet.

name: Beigli
description:
Beigli is a 1.5 year-old medium-sized crossbreed boy with a beautiful soul. Born in an abandoned property alongside his six siblings, little Beigli’s life began in heartbreaking circumstances.

His mum was desperately trying to keep her babies alive while she herself was painfully thin and starving.

At just three weeks old, the family was rescued and brought to safety.

The puppies grew up, one by one they found their forever homes, and today only two remain: Beigli and his sister Maggie.

At just 1.5 years old, Beigli has already spent almost his entire life waiting.

He adores people, loves playing with other dogs, and has the kind, gentle nature that makes everyone fall in love with him.

All Beigli dreams of is a family to call his own. A warm bed. Daily walks. Someone to greet with a wagging tail and endless devotion.

He can live with older dog-savvy children and can be cat tested for the right applicant.

Beigli is in Hungary and is ready to travel to the UK as soon as the right family finds him.

He comes neutered, fully vaccinated, treated for parasites, with an EU pet passport.

name: Brock
description:
Drop dead gorgeous Brock is a two year old Pointer/Bully mix and arrived at the shelter a couple of months ago after the dog warden brought him in as a stray.

We were assuming someone would come and collect him, as he was in great health and was so happy around people, but sadly days turned into weeks and no one came to get him.

Brock is now searching for a new home where he can be treated like the prince he truly is!

Brock is estimated to be around two years old and definitely has some kind of hound in him among various other breeds – he’s a real mixed bag but so handsome.

He has stunning markings which look very Bracque, and he is also very people oriented and clever. He is keen to please and loves to impress people. He learned a gorgeous sit in just a few tries and now sits beautifully waiting for a treat in his kennel.

Brock would be best suited to a home where he’s the centre of attention. Since being in the shelter he has been fine with female dogs, but he is more picky with male dogs and doesn’t really like to share his space with them.

With this in mind he would also be better suited to a family that have experience of owning dogs before, just so they feel comfortable managing interactions. With people though, Brock is an absolute superstar and just adores everyone.

Brock would be happy in a home with a fairly active lifestyle and someone who wants to work a bit more on his training. As he’s clever, he really enjoys learning and benefits from some focus and direction.

He also has potential to enjoy scent training, as he loves to use his nose like – typical hound! He would also prefer a home with access to a nice garden.

Brock would be great with children and he loves any kind of attention. He can be bouncy and excitable, so with that in mind children aged 8+ are probably more appropriate.

Brock would make an amazing adventure companion and would love to opportunity to spend lots of time outdoors. He has plenty of stamina, and would relish the opportunity to become the apple of someone’s eye.

He is very loyal and loving, and as long as someone is comfortable with him not being the best of friends with every single dog he meets, he could absolutely shine in the right forever home.

name: Jenny
description:
Jenny is a 10 year old female Airedale Terrier Cross with a heartbreaking past and a heart full of hope. For seven long years, she was left chained outside without shelter or kindness, while the world looked away.

Her suffering only came to light by chance — her rescuers were returning another dog when they saw her standing there, neglected and desperate.

Jenny’s eyes lit up as if she knew this was her moment, and when her owner was asked to surrender her, he did so without hesitation.

Since that day, Jenny has been safe, but her home has been a kennel. A whole year has passed, and she is still waiting for the love she has never truly known.

Jenny is gentle and people-oriented. She loves her walks and is good on the lead, though she can be a little strong at times. She enjoys chasing a ball and, while she isn’t interested in making doggy friends, she’s content as long as her space is respected.

Jenny would be happiest as the only dog in the home so she doesn’t have to share attention or space.

She is spayed, fully vaccinated, and travels with her EU pet passport — ready to start the new chapter she so deserves.

Jenny has lost so many years, but it’s not too late for her to find happiness! All she wants now is to spend her golden years knowing comfort, kindness, and love.

Could you give her the forever home she has waited a lifetime for?

Fully vaccinated, spayed, microchipped, with an EU pet passport. Ready to travel.

name: Taffy
description:
Taffy is a one year old German Shepherd cross and was brought into the shelter by the dog wandering after she was found wandering through the fields as a stray.

She wasn’t difficult to catch as she was more than happy to see new humans and trot over to them! She’s now very patiently waiting for her second chance, hoping that her new family are out there.

Taffy is estimated to be around a year old and as appears to be a theme with our shepherd girls, she’s so clever. The boys aren’t quite at their level just yet!

Taffy is very smart and similarly to Birdie, who came in a few weeks before her, she also new some basic commands which suggests she’s had a home, or at least positive human interaction (maybe from a farm owner or outside an army base) from someone.

Taffy now shares her kennels with another dog and although she was initially a bit disgruntled about having to share her space with a male dog, they’ve since really started to get along.

She will grumble at him a bit if he’s invading her space or jumping on her too much, but between them they seem to have sussed out their new friendship and are getting on just fine.

Taffy could definitely live alongside a resident dog in her new home, but she’s a confident girl and doesn’t seek out their company.

Being a shepherd, Taffy is not only smart but she’s also fiercely loyal and very active. She would thrive in a home where she has access to a secure garden to run around in and sunbathe, and she would also be best suited to a family who enjoy an energetic lifestyle.

Getting the opportunity to explore would be perfect for Taffy, and she’ll be a great partner in crime on an adventure or a long hike.
