She is still getting used to lead training, but thanks to the volunteer visits at the weekend she’s getting more familiar and confident. She loves being outside, watching the birds, rolling about in the grass and sniffing about in the dirt.

But, when she’s had her fun outdoors she is more than happy to chill out in her kennel, and she loves inching herself closer and closer to you until she’s finally resting in your lap. She has the mindset of a small dog and is definitely not aware of her size!

Taffy is a really good girl and we would love to see her shine in a new home where she has the focus, commitment and love she’s due. She is a wonderful character and will only continue to blossom.

name: Loki
description:
Loki, a beautiful 2 year old Siberian Husky needs a new home through no fault of his own.

The owner has serious health problems and is unable to give him the care and attention he needs and deserves. He is spending more and more time in kennels which is far from ideal.

Loki is a lovely boy, he loves his toys and he has a kind nature. He is currently the only dog in the household, but he is friendly with dogs and wants to play on walks so he has the potential to live with another friendly dog.

He is also used to living with older children.

He is fully vaccinated and microchipped and up to date with flea and wormingtreatments.

Loki is in Chorley, Lancashire where he is visitable upon arrangement.

name: Poppy
description:
Sweet little Poppy is five years old and was brought into the vets shortly after having puppies.

She was never collected again by her family, and ended up being handed into the shelter by the vet who wanted to make sure she found a home that would treat her with the love and care she deserves.

She is expected to be around five years old and is just the most charming, silly little sausage.

Poppy can be a little bit shy with new people, especially men, but the way to her heart is via her favourite toys! Pick up her toysand it’s as though she’s known you forever.

She loves to play and is so funny and excitable, racing about all over the place and collecting them all up and placing them neatly in a pile. She will be in her element in a home where she has her very own basket of toys to rummage through every day!

Poppy is a very gentle girl and she loves affection. Once she trusts you, she likes to sit as close as physically possible and breathein your face while you stroke her ears.

She has a couple of missing, wonky teeth which only add to her adorable charm. She also likes to clutch onto your arm with both paws for the ultimate cuddle, but she does so very gently, so as not to be too bouncy. She’s just a real sweetheart.

Unfortunately, Poppy is positive for Leishmania, which is a chronic health condition caused by the bite of an infected sandfly.

Poppy’s condition is stable and she’s on the right medication to ensure she’s fit and healthy, but it is of course something for prospective adopters to consider, as she will need regular medication and monitoring.

Outwardly, she is very healthy, happy, in no pain and has a good appetite and a zest for life.

Poppy is fairly submissive and would be ideal for a calm home with someone who can shower her with fuss and attention. She gets along with other dogs, but doesn’t depend on them, and she would be great in a home with children too.

She loves to be close and you can just tell she is going to make such an amazing companion given the second chance she deserves. Her temperament is wonderful, and she has a heart of absolute gold.

name: Ally
description:
Ally is a four year old German Shepherd mix. Poor Ally came into the shelter over a year ago after being rescued running scared in the roads.

She was so sad in the shelter when she first arrived and would sit by the kennel bars and cry for hours.

We think she has previously had a family and was desperate for them to come and get her, but of course that never happened, and months later she’s still without a home to call her own.

Ally is a lovely dog who through no fault of her own has just been overlooked time and time again. By nature she’s an active, intelligent and very loyal girl.

She’s eager to please and is so bored in the shelter, so she would thrive in an active home with someone who wants to explore with the company of a canine best friend.

Shepherds have great stamina, so long hikes and camping holidays will be no problem for a dog like Ally – she’d love it! She’d also love any kind of training, as she loves to please and learning new things is great fun for intelligent breeds like herself.

Ally shares her kennel with another dog and although she seems to enjoy his company, it’s clear that humans are her first love.

She is content around other dogs, happily to walking alongside them when outside the shelter and sharing her space with them, but we feel she would be fine either with or without a resident dog to live with.

Ally’s ideal home would have a garden where she can let off some steam and stretch her legs, but even if her garden is small as long as she’s based outside of the city surrounded by plenty of places to explore, she’ll be happy.

We have no doubt that she will be so loyal to her new family, but she may have some separation anxiety to overcome due to her abandonment based on her behaviour in the shelter.

With patience, reassurance, routine and consistency this is something that can be overcome, and who can blame her for feeling worried after experiencing being dumped before?

Ally would love a family home where she can experience the security of feeling loved, wanted, and a sense of belonging.

She has a soft heart and although her abandonment should have broken her trust in people, she’s been nothing but forgiving and resilient. We would love for her to find the family she’s been waiting so long for.

name: Ariel
description:
Ariel is a 6-year-old small-medium sized girl with a big personality and an even bigger heart. This feisty little terrier has been waiting in the shelter for over 3 years… far longer than any dog should have to wait.

Ariel is full of character – a true terrier spirit. She’s lively, expressive and not afraid to let you know when she’s excited – it’s all part of her charm!

She is affectionate with people and loves children, happily soaking up attention and enjoying being part of the action. Ariel forms lovely bonds and will be a loyal and loving companion to her family.

With other dogs, she is friendly with most and enjoys their company, though like many terriers, she appreciates respectful introductions and a good match in energy.

After spending such a long time in the shelter, Ariel truly deserves a home where she can finally relax, feel safe, and be loved every day.

She would love a family who will embrace her fun personality, include her in their lives, and give her the attention she’s been missing for so long.

Ariel is in Hungary, ready to travel to the UK once a home has been secured for her.

name: Ivan
description:
Ivan is a one year old Greek Harehound, and unfortunately he is looking for a new home as soon as possible. He arrived in the UK in June 2025 at the age of five months old, and has been in a loving, supportive home since then.

But very sadly, the arrival of a baby has led to Ivan being relinquished back into our care. Our deadline to find Ivan a foster home is the middle of May, and if we’re unable to do so he will have to go into kennels.

Due to the significant life changes his family are going through, Ivan has not been given adequate attention or training over recent months.

With his family now functioning on reduced sleep, they have admitted that they no longer have the time for him and that he’s spending more and more time in his crate.

All of this change has resulted in his behaviour deteriorating as he’s found situations more overwhelming to deal with. We recognise that his environment is also not the most conducive to his needs, and this too plays a role in him needing a new home.

Ivan is looking for a semi-rural home where he has more space, a nice garden to run about in, and a family who understands hounds. He is currently living in London and is struggling with the suburban surroundings.

There are a lot of factors that he finds overwhelming and this is causing pent up frustration and anxiety. He would be much happier outside of the city where he can enjoy long walks in green spaces.

Ivan needs some time to reset, adjust to a new environment, and decompress. He is extremely food motivated, which really helps with training, and he has learnt a few tricks too.

He is also housetrained and crate trained, but does unfortunately struggle with the car which needs some continued desensitisation training.

In true hound fashion, Ivan is incredibly affectionate with his family, loves a snuggle on the sofa, and is happiest when chasing after a ball.

He’s an energetic boy and needs an active home, but he also responds well to mental stimulation and enrichment with his food, such as stuffed kongs and scatter feeding.

Ivan’s main struggles relate to reactivity and anxiety. Before leaving the shelter and in his initial UK foster home, Ivan was brilliant with other dogs and socialised with males and females of a variety of ages.

Unfortunately this hasn’t been the case since being adopted, and he is now very selective with other dogs. It is possible that in a calmer environment this may improve, and he has had good relationships with mature female dogs.

Although Ivan currently lives with a newborn and has been very adaptable to the new arrival, we’re looking for a home with older children simply to keep his environment a bit more predictable and relaxed.

Ivan is looking for a family that can give him the time, patience and training to settle in at his own pace.

We feel a change of environment will really be integral in supporting his onward progress, and we won’t be considering urban homes given his struggles in London.

We know how loving, sweet natured and friendly Ivan can be and we’re looking for a home where he can enjoy lots of adventures, a calm home atmosphere, and has the attention and understanding of a more experienced adopter.

name: Teddy
description:
Teddy is a beautiful six year old Alaskan Malamute who came from Cyprus back in 2021.

He originally came into our care when his first owner took him to a pet hotel in Cyprus and subsequently left there when he decided he wasn’t going to be able to keep him anymore.

Teddy’s life in the UK then got off to a poor start when he was quickly surrendered back to us due to a change of circumstances, and now, we’re looking for a new home yet again for him.

Sadly, following the arrival of a second child, his family are no longer able to give him the time and attention he deserves.

They are now looking for an active home where Teddy can be included in family life and enjoy all the walks, playtime and companionship he loves. They know Teddy needs more than they can offer, and they just want him to be happy and adored.

Teddy has a wonderful personality and is a friendly, sociable boy who would happily make friends with everyone he meets.

He can get a little overexcited when visitors arrive, as he is so keen to say hello, but he is always friendly in his intentions.

He can also be quite persistent when it comes to boundaries, particularly with people he doesn’t see regularly, so his new family should be comfortable providing clear and consistent guidance.

Although Teddy has plenty of energy and loves a good walk, he is also very happy to settle down and relax afterwards.

He enjoys running, chasing a ball and having plenty of opportunities to play, but in true Malamute fashion, he can become bored if every walk follows the same route.

A home that enjoys mixing things up and giving him new places to explore would suit him beautifully. He loves being involved in whatever his family are doing and would thrive with people who have the time to include him in their daily lives.

Teddy has been brilliant with children, including his own family’s young children. He is gentle when playing and seems very aware of how small they are.

If things become a little too much for him, he is happy to take himself away somewhere quiet to rest. He has shown a lovely understanding of children and would make a wonderful companion in a family that can continue to respect his space and needs.

Teddy enjoys the company of other dogs, although he can be selective about who he gets along with. He previously lived happily with another Underdog and was respectful of her boundaries.

Homes with other resident dogs would need to meet Teddy beforehand, to ensure he was friendly and comfortable with their resident dog, as he will not necessarily be suited to every canine companion.

Teddy is generally good on the lead and is happy to walk at your pace, although he can pull at times. He is comfortable wearing a collar, harness or Halti head harness.

He has had some off lead time in open areas and has reasonable recall, but can be distracted by squirrels and other wildlife, so secure areas are the safest option, particularly around woods.

He knows his basic commands, including sit, stay and paw, and is a willing learner who enjoys being taught. He is also housetrained and crate trained.

Teddy is looking for an active, loving home where he can enjoy plenty of walks, playtime and company. Whilst Malamute experience is not compulsory, it is important to recognise the needs and temperament of the breed.

He has a lovely mix of enthusiasm and affection, with the ability to settle happily after a busy day, and with a family who can include him in their adventures, provide consistent boundaries and understand his individual needs, he has so much to offer as a loyal and entertaining companion.

name: Tiana
description:
Tiana is a five month old Pointer cross puppy, and she is an absolutely gorgeous girl with a such a happy go lucky personality.

She arrived in the shelter as a lone puppy, presumed abandoned, and she flew to her foster home in London on the 20th September. She has been settling in amazingly well and her foster family are so impressed with her positive, adaptable nature.

Tiana and her foster family are already working hard on her basic training and she is proving to be a bright and very food motivated girl who enjoys learning.

There are no signs of possessiveness around food or toys and she is happy for her foster to take things from her, even when she has found something she probably shouldn’t have, such as an old snail shell!

Above all, she absolutely loves people and wants to be involved in whatever is happening around her. If there is a cuddle available, she will be there, you don’t have to ask her twice!

Tiana is confident when meeting new people, provided they approach her calmly, and is usually ready to be friends straight away. She has been lovely with visitors and is gentle and happy to be handled.

She is also very good at matching the energy of the people around her, whether that means relaxing on the sofa or running around the garden with a ball.

She has a cheeky side and is definitely a dog who likes to have fun, especially given her young age.

Tiana loves playing with balls and chew toys, enjoys a good bout of zoomies and is equally happy snoozing on a warm lap afterwards.

She loves to be included, so her new family should be prepared for a dog who wants to be part of the action rather than watching from the sidelines.

She has only recently started being introduced to walking on a lead, but she’s taken to it really well. She really enjoys getting out and exploring on the lead, and has been friendly with new people and dogs that she has met. She’s also not fazed by roadworks, buses or cars.

Tiana has been wonderful with her foster’s younger teenage children, although she is already quite tall when she gets excited and could accidentally be a little overwhelming for smaller children.

She would therefore be best suited to a family who can give her appropriate boundaries and help her learn to manage her enthusiasm.

Tiana isn’t crate trained yet and would currently much rather sleep on her foster family’s pillows! Gentle crate training has already begun and should continue at her own pace, particularly if her new family would like her to sleep in a crate at night.

She sleeps from 10.30pm to 7am soundly, although enjoys a lay in at the weekends!

Tiana is looking for an active family who will continue building on the lovely start she has already made. She has plenty of playful energy, but also knows how to settle down and enjoy a cuddle.

With her affectionate nature, willingness to learn and cheeky but charming personality, Tiana is going to make a very special companion.

name: Banjo
description:
Little Banjo, 3 year old male Terrier Cross, is a Bosnian rescue pup. At three years old, he is a sweet and curious boy, full of character, and has made some lovely progress since arriving in his home.

Unfortunately, the busy city environment in London where he currently lives has proved unsuitable for his needs, and he is now looking for a quieter place where he can feel comfortable, enjoy his surroundings and continue to build his confidence.

Banjo has a lovely independent side and is quite happy spending time doing his own thing. He doesn’t constantly seek attention and is happiest when given the choice to approach people in his own time.

As he has become more comfortable with his family, he has started to actively seek affection, enjoying a cuddle and even a little kiss on the head before bedtime. He is a very sweet boy who appreciates having his own space and a comfortable spot to nap.

Banjo enjoys his walks and loves having his nose to the ground, investigating all the interesting scents along the way. He is generally very good on the lead and has also enjoyed exploring on a long line in the park.

At home, he is quick to learn routines and has already picked up commands such as sit. He is a very clever little guy who enjoys using his brain and learns quickly.

His favourite activities include searching for hidden treats, enrichment games, working on a licki-mat and having a good chew on something tough. He also enjoys playing with a tennis ball and enthusiastically investigating cardboard boxes.

Banjo can be anxious around unfamiliar people, particularly visitors arriving at the house, and may bark at them initially. However, he has made considerable progress with this and has learnt that visitors can be a source of good things.

When people give him time and allow him to approach at his own pace, he can gradually settle and become comfortable accepting affection. He is now happy around familiar visitors, including his trainer and close family.

His new family will need to be patient and understanding, allowing him to build trust without putting pressure on him to interact.

His biggest challenge is his sensitivity to noise and other dogs. Banjo is particularly worried by dogs when out walking, and he is also sensitive to traffic, bikes and everyday sounds, even within the home.

As you can imagine, living in London is therefore very stressful for him, and gives him little time to decompress between triggers.

Once he becomes overwhelmed, his anxiety can spill over into reactions to other things around him, and barking is his immediate response to a rise in excitement or stress.

Despite these difficulties, Banjo has shown that he can make progress when his surroundings allow him to feel more comfortable.

He has learnt to walk calmly alongside a neighbour’s dog, ignoring her when he feels settled, and his behaviourist believes that he will continue to make progress in a quieter environment.

It’s also worth noting that Banjo was very sociable with other dogs when in the shelter in Bosnia.

We strongly suggest he has ongoing support from a properly qualified behaviourist who can help his new family understand his needs and work gradually on his confidence and reactions.

Banjo isn’t an energetic dog, and he would best thrive in a relatively quiet household in a calm, semi-rural setting. He’s actually a very settled boy at home and is happy spending time alone.

He is comfortable relaxing independently and has shown no separation anxiety.

A secure garden would be a real bonus, giving him somewhere peaceful to relax and enjoy the sunshine, as well as opportunities for enrichment and play without immediately facing the pressures of a busy walking environment.

Banjo is a lovely, intelligent little dog who has already shown how much he can achieve when given time, patience and an understanding approach.

He isn’t looking for a busy life or a home where he will be expected to cope with everything straight away.

He just needs someone who can appreciate his independent nature, respect his boundaries and help him feel safe enough to explore the world at his own pace. In the right environment, with continued behavioural support, Banjo will blossom.

name: Apollo
description:
Meet Apollo – a gentle soul ready for a new life.

Apollo, a 3.5-year-old medium size cross-breed boy, whose life until now has been far from kind, has finally been freed from a life lived on a chain. Yet somehow, despite everything, he has held onto his sweetness, his trust, and his huge heart.

Apollo is incredibly human-centred, affectionate, and loving — the kind of dog who just wants to be close to people and soak up kindness.

He is wonderfully sociable with other dogs, big and small, and plays beautifully and politely with them. He’s also an absolute dream at the vets, calm and cooperative — everyone who meets him falls for his sweet nature.

He even has the potential to live with cats; in his previous life, he used to sleep in his dog house with a cat companion, sharing warmth and comfort.

He travels nicely in the car, walks well on the lead, and is more than ready to start discovering what family life means.

Currently, Apollo lives in boarding kennels, hoping that one day someone will finally choose him.

Apollo has so much love to give — he just needs someone who will finally give him the life he has always deserved. ?

Apollo comes neutered, fully vaccinated, microchipped, and with an EU pet passport.

He is ready to travel from Hungary as soon as his family is found.

name: Rose
description:
This lovely, gentle, large girl is Rose, a 6 year old Spanish Mastin cross. She has a beautiful thick, light tan, soft coat, and black masked face.

Rose recently joined us, with her sister Poppy, from a rescue in Malaga that was closing down as the owner had passed away.

Poor Rose has been in kennels all her life along with her siblings, all now homed except the two sisters.

As you can imagine, the 2 sisters are very bonded, but also very sweet natured and affectionate girls if a little shy still but we are working on exposing her to more new situations to help her confidence.

Both girls have met quite a few dogs at the rescue without issue and now share their garden with young Levi. All 3 play very happily together and its great for them to have their freedom, both girls walk nicely on their lead.

Rose and Poppy are being treated for low level leishmania with Alopurinol which is an inexpensive maintenance programme to keep her healthy and safe.

Rose is spayed and up to date with her vaccinations. It’s always much harder trying to home 2 dogs together but we would love to try for these lovely sisters.

Due to Rose’s size, we think she is better homed with children over 10 years and she can live with other dogs but we are unsure of being an only dog.

She would do well in a rural environment, maybe a farm, small holding or large gardens, and a family used to walking or other outside activities. We haven’t tested her for cats yet.

In Spain now – can travel to UK end September onwards.

attributes.Breed: And jack russell terrier / bodeguera cross

name: Lulu, Toby and Leon
description:
These small puppies, Lulu, Toby and Leon, are 6 month old male and female Jack Russell Terrier / Bodeguera Cross.

Very beautiful and incredibly friendly, if not a little nervous but getting more confident by the day, they are all waiting for their forever homes and we would be hoping to find homes with other dogs for them to bond with.

We have a mixture but here is a brief description:Lulu, Toby and Leon from the same litterAll weighing around 8kgAll standing around 40cmAnd 6 months old

All were found abandoned a few months ago, by an older person trying to do his best for them but he is struggling and the pups urgently need new homes now.

They all love play time, and havent been tested for cats, but we think they will be ok with them but they can be tested. Children over 12 years as they are still learning their confidence.

None are spayed or neutered as they are too young, up to date with their vaccinations and have their passport in place so could travel to the right family in September.

Living with dogs : yesLiving with cats : not testedLiving with children : yes over 12NEEDS to live with another dog Yes 100%

In Spain now – can travel to UK in end September.

name: Suzy
description:
This lovely gentle large girl is Suzy, a 4 year old Spanish Mastin mix (her mum was a Mastine). She has a beautifully marked tri colour soft coat, and attractively marked face.

Suzy was actually born here after her mum Willow was dumped in the field opposite us heavily pregnant.

Suzy is an amazing dog, incredibly affectionate and friendly and also responds well to training. In all fairness she responds well to anything that involves a dog treat, she would gladly swap one of her kidneys for a sausage!

Suzy is one of the dogs we introduce when we have new dogs or if a dog has to be separated for any reason and needs a friend. It always amazes us how quickly she bonds with new dogs and is normally playing with them within minutes of a first meeting.

Due to Suzy’s size, we think she is better homed with children over 10 years and she can live with other dogs as she has always lived with dogs around her.

She would do well in a rural environment, with large gardens, and a family used to walking or other outside activities.

We haven’t tested her properly for cats yet but she hasn’t shown much interest in them so far.

Spanish Mastin crossAge : 4 yearsGender: FemaleHeight: 66cm

name: Carly
description:
This beautiful young girl is Carly, one of a litter of 4 Border Collie pups aged just 4 months old. Dad is a pure Collie and Mum is a mix.

They all look gorgeous ! The litter was recently found abandoned.

All have the traditional black and white soft coats and very friendly adventurous pups.

So Carly was quite shy and nervous when she arrived with us, but has settled down into a very loving young girl, she gets on well with her kennel mates and loves having a cuddle.

A typical happy pup, Carly has her passport and vaccinations she’s currently 13kg and 30cm tall

They all love play time, and havent been tested for cats, but we think they will be ok with them but they can be tested. Children over 10 years as they are still learning their confidence.

None are spayed or neutered as they are too young, up to date with their vaccinations and have their passport in place so could travel to the right family in September onwards.

Breed : Border Collie pupsAge : 3/4 monthsGender: Female and maleHeight: 30cmWeight: 13kg

name: Mia
description:
Mia is a gorgeous girl and a mix of Labrador and Mastin. She has a cream and blonde coloured, short, soft coat and a fantastic laid back gentle temperament.

Mia came to us with Emma, after their owner became sick and was unable to care for them. Mia is such a pretty girl, her photos do not do her justice.

She is very submissive and always lies on her back, so you can stroke her tummy. She is an active and inquisitive girl who loves to run and play in the garden.

She is well behaved and follows instructions well. She would make an ideal family pet and would be gentle enough for children.

She is a really gentle and friendly dog. She gets on really well with other dogs and will play with anyone.

Breed : Labrador crossAge : 3 years oldGender: femaleHeight: medium sized dog

name: Lucy
description:
Lucy is a 7-year-old Beagle cross, likely mixed with a smaller terrier breed. She’s on the smaller side of medium, full of personality, and ready to find the forever home she so deserves.

Rescued from the streets of Cyprus while pregnant, Lucy’s puppies were quickly adopted, but she has been waiting in kennels for over two years. Despite this, her zest for life and love for people remains unshaken.

Lucy is a people-oriented dog who adores human interaction. She’s confident, friendly with new people, and her playful, cheeky personality makes her a joy to be around.

When let out of her kennel, she sprints like a rocket but quickly circles back to you for belly rubs. Her favourite pastime is splitting her energy between zoomies and lounging in the dirt for cuddles, always with her tail wagging furiously.

Lucy is energetic but not overwhelming, and with a more active lifestyle, she’s ready to thrive. She loves being outdoors, exploring green spaces, or playing in a secure garden. Her ideal home would be outside the city, with access to safe spaces where she can run and play.

While she does need some basic training (like curbing her tendency to jump up in excitement), Lucy is eager to please and already well-behaved in many ways—she returns to her kennel without protest after playtime.

Lucy is good with other dogs but doesn’t need a resident canine companion to be happy. She’d also be a lovely fit for families with children aged 6+ due to her friendly temperament, though her playful energy might require supervision at first. An adult-only home with plenty of love, cuddles, and treats would also suit her well.

Though currently living in a kennel, Lucy’s adaptable nature means she’ll likely settle quickly into a home environment. She has a clean bill of health and is ready to travel from Cyprus to meet her new family.

name: Rodney
description:
Rodney is a super-friendly, handsome young lad with a nice personality. He has a short, soft coat and stands at a small/medium; he is two years old.

Rodney recently came into our care as his elderly owner can no longer care for him. He’s ready to be adopted by the right family immediately as he’s already lived in a home and has his passport and vaccinations in place.

He’s been having a great time playing with his new Kennel mates he seems to prefer the females. Rodney loves meeting people and is a very happy, friendly and affectionate boy.

We are looking for a family with or without another friendly dog for Rodney to play with and children no younger than 8 yrs. Would suit any family.

name: Scooby
description:
Scooby is an adorable, confident young boy of around 10 months old who is discovering the world around him and learning more every day.

He is a very sweet boy with the most loving, expressive eyes and a playful personality. Scooby is an excitable, bouncy and affectionate boy who loves his toys, chews and Licky Mats.

He enjoys being active and having plenty to do, but once the day is over, he is very happy to settle down for a cuddle. Despite being such a young dog, Scooby sleeps soundly throughout the night in his crate.

During the day, Scooby thrives with a good, consistent routine. He needs plenty of appropriate stimulation and things to keep him occupied between crate time.

Access to a secure enclosed field would be a real bonus for him, as having the opportunity to safely run and burn off some energy really helps him to relax and settle afterwards.

Scooby is looking for a family who genuinely has the time, patience and enthusiasm to nurture a young dog.

His new family would need to be around for the majority of the time and be prepared to continue his training, help him learn good manners and give him the structure he needs to flourish.

He would suit an adult-only home. Although Scooby is a lovely-natured boy, he can be rather clumsy, silly and exuberant, so we feel an adult home would be the best environment for him.

Scooby currently has a foster brother and really enjoys having another dog around. He would love a confident, playful canine companion who can tolerate his youthful enthusiasm and give him a little patience.

We feel Scooby would be particularly well suited to a more experienced home where his adopters will enjoy the journey of helping a young dog develop.

Scooby has already come a long way and we would love to see his confidence continue to grow as he learns and experiences more of the world.

name: Cleo
description:
Cleo is an adorable 11-month-old small mixed breed girl looking for a loving forever home. She and her three siblings were found abandoned as tiny puppies, all in very poor condition, frightened and unsure of the world around them.

With their parents unknown and their future uncertain, all they had was each other.

Thankfully, Cleo has blossomed into a wonderful young dog. Although naturally a little shy when meeting new people or experiencing new situations, she is incredibly sweet, gentle, and affectionate once she feels safe.

Her confidence continues to grow every day.

She loves playing with other dogs and enjoys spending time with people she knows and trusts. Cleo would thrive in a calm, patient home where she can continue building her confidence at her own pace.

In return, she will reward her family with unwavering loyalty and love.

Cleo could happily live with another friendly well-balanced dog and she has all the potential to live with cats, too.

As a small-sized girl, Cleo would make a lovely companion for someone looking for a gentle, kind-hearted dog.

She comes spayed, microchipped, fully vaccinated and with an EU pet passport.

name: Freya
description:
Freya is a beautiful Segugio Italiano cross, estimated to be around 4-5 years old. She’s on the smaller side of medium and has been patiently waiting for almost three years to find her forever home.

Found abandoned and severely underweight, Freya has been cared for by a local boarding kennel in Cyprus, where she’s blossomed into a gentle, affectionate, and sweet-natured dog.

Freya is slightly reserved and shy when meeting new people, but she has made significant progress in building her confidence, thanks to her kennel mate, Ira. She thrives in calm and predictable environments and would do best with a patient family who can help her continue to grow.

Freya gets along well with other dogs and has a submissive nature in group settings. She enjoys canine company but is also content living as the only dog, provided her adopters give her plenty of attention and reassurance. If there is a resident dog, it might help Freya settle in faster, but it’s not a requirement for her to thrive.

Freya would be best suited to a semi-rural home with a garden where she can engage in scentwork and sniffing games, which help her relax and exercise her natural instincts. Busy households or homes with younger children might overwhelm her, so a calm home with children aged 10+ would be ideal.

True to her scent hound heritage, Freya loves to explore her surroundings, sniffing and searching for treats. She is very food motivated, which is a fantastic way to build trust with her. Freya takes treats gently and patiently waits her turn, endearing herself to everyone she meets.

Although she might be shy initially, Freya’s sweet and affectionate nature will shine once she forms a bond with you. Watching her transition from kennel life to a loving home will be incredibly rewarding.

Freya is healthy and ready to travel from Cyprus to her forever home. Could you be the one to give this lovely girl the peace and happiness she deserves?

name: Artie
description:
Artie is a gentle, one-year-old Shepherd mix from Cyprus who is ready to start a new life after being found abandoned in a municipal pound.

Artie is a true sweetheart who is looking for the opportunity begin again. He’s a young dog, estimated to be no more than one year old, and he has already experienced more hardship than any dog should.

He was found abandoned in a municipal pound before being taken in by one of our shelter partners when space became available. Understandably, he arrived frightened and unsure, with signs that he had not received the kindness or care every dog deserves.

Despite his difficult start, Artie has shown himself to be a calm, gentle and sensitive boy. He is not naturally trusting of new people and tends to hang back when meeting someone for the first time, but his shy nature is never defensive. Instead, he quietly observes, waiting until he feels ready to approach.

He will come to you ever so gently and slowly when he’s ready, you just have to earn it! With time and understanding, he begins to show interest, especially if you happen to have a biscuit in hand. Treats have become an important part of his confidence building journey and are really helping him learn that people can be kind.

Among other dogs, we have noticed that Artie has a naturally soothing presence and has formed some lovely bonds with other dogs in the shelter, particularly those who are nervous or have similar temperaments.

He has been a quiet source of comfort to many of them, offering calm companionship and helping them to feel at ease. For this reason, we believe Artie would thrive in a home with another friendly, well-adjusted dog to show him the ropes and offer reassurance.

He is still learning to trust the world around him and will need an adopter who understands the importance of moving at his pace. Artie would do best in a peaceful, semi rural home with access to a secure garden and without too much hustle and bustle.

A household with older children, ideally aged ten and above, would suit him better at this stage, as younger children may feel overwhelming for him. He has not yet been tested with cats so we have no insight as to how he may react to a resident feline.

Artie is a work in progress, but what he lacks in confidence he makes up for in heart. He is a gentle boy with no malice in him, only the quiet hope that life might finally offer him the love and safety he has missed out on so far.

With time, consistency and lots of patience, we believe Artie will come into his own and become a truly devoted companion.

If you are looking to make a real difference to a dog’s life and believe in the quiet power of kindness and patience, Artie may just be the one.

name: Gesztenye
description:
Gesztenye is a beautiful 2-year-old medium-sized brindle girl with the sweetest soul. She adores people, loves playing with other dogs and greets everyone she meets with a wagging tail and a hopeful smile.

For over two years, Gesztenye and her sister Zserbo have shared everything. They were rescued together from a kill shelter when they were only a few weeks old. They grew up side by side, slept in the same kennel, and waited together for someone to finally choose them.

Now Zserbo’s dream has come true. She has found a wonderful family in the UK.

But little Gesztenye will soon watch her sister leave… and for the first time in her life, she will be alone.

She has so much love to give and asks for so little in return – just a family to call her own.

Gesztenye is friendly with dogs and would happily live with another canine companion. She is affectionate, playful and kind natured, and can also live with older dog-savvy children.

She’s looking for a home where she will be part of family life and not left alone for long periods.

Like all rescue dogs, Gesztenye will need time, patience and love, but in return she will give you her whole heart.

Gesztenye is currently in Hungary and is ready to travel to the UK as soon as her forever family finds her.

She is spayed, fully vaccinated, treated for parasites, comes with and EU pet passport.

name: Raina
description:
Raina – 8 month old female Cross-Breed is a large-sized puppy who will grow into a large adult dog. She was abandoned alongside her sister Mischa at a kennels in November 2024 when they were young pups.

Raina and Mischa are only just beginning to explore their independence. For weeks, they stuck close together, but now they’re starting to show their own personalities.

Raina, the more confident of the two, is soft, squishy, and sweet-natured. While she may be a little shy initially, she warms up with time, trust, and reassurance, showing potential to become a wonderful companion.

Raina is playful and enjoys running in the paddock with other dogs, often cheekily stealing toys from her sister. She’s food-oriented, making her a good candidate for basic training using treats as motivation. Her experience on the lead is limited, so her new family will need to help her with training and routine.

Raina is looking for a semi-rural home with a calm atmosphere, a garden, and an active yet balanced lifestyle. Although not essential, she would likely adjust more quickly with a resident dog.

Raina is currently based in Cyprus and has a clean bill of health. She is ready to travel once she finds her forever home.

name: Connie
description:
Connie is a 2 year old female Puli Cross. Her story began in a public pound, where she grew up in harsh conditions. A year ago, she was rescued in a heartbreaking state – skin and bone, frightened and frail.

With care, love, and patience, Connie has blossomed into a happy, affectionate girl. Today she’s full of life – her waggy tail never stops, she adores treats and cuddles, and she has even learned to smile when she’s with the people she loves. This beautiful girl has learned to trust again!

Connie loves the company of other dogs and is especially playful – wrestling and mingling are her favourite games! She would be just as happy snuggling up on the sofa as she is joining in on adventures.

Connie is still waiting in a small shelter in Hungary, dreaming of her forever family. She deserves a home where she will be cherished, spoiled, and loved for the sweet, resilient girl she is.

For Connie, an experienced rescue dog home would be ideal – someone patient and understanding, ready to continue guiding her on her journey.

She could live happily with another friendly and playful dog or as the only dog in the home.

2 years oldPlayful, affectionate, sociableSpayed, vaccinated, microchipped, with EU passportCan travel to the UK once her family is found

If you can give Connie the love-filled home she has been waiting for, please get in touch.

Adoption subject to home check & fee. Full RBU provided.

name: Mischa
description:
Mischa is a shy and reserved girl who, along with her sister Raina, was thrown over the wall of a kennels in November 2024 when they were only young pups. At around eight months old now, Mischa will be a large-sized adult dog, but she is a complete softie.

Mischa and Raina were abandoned in the right place with the right people. For the first few weeks, they were glued to each other, but as they’ve become more settled, they are becoming braver and coming into their own personalities.

Mischa tends to hang back while Raina takes the lead, but she’s improving each day. Routine and consistency will be key in helping her feel settled in a new home. She’s gentle, sweet, and soft, just needing reassurance and confidence building to blossom into a confident dog.

When it comes to other dogs, Mischa is very playful and enjoys interacting with her sister and other kennel dogs. She loves playing in the paddock and has bursts of speed, often being chased by Raina.

Mischa would be best suited to a semi-rural home with a calm household atmosphere and a moderately active lifestyle. She needs a garden and a resident dog to help her adjust to a companion lifestyle.

Mischa is currently based in Cyprus, has a clean bill of health, and is ready to travel to her forever home.

name: Lonzo
description:
Poor Lonzo, an 18 month old male Labrador Retriever Cross, hasn’t had the best run of luck since arriving in the UK.

His first home felt he was too bouncy for their young son, and now sadly his second home feel they can’t offer him the kind of lifestyle he truly needs.

Lonzo is, and has always been, a silly, goofy boy with a big personality, no understanding of personal space or his size, and a boisterous (but innocent) play style. He’s looking for an active home that can give him all the fun and fuss he’s desperate for.

Lonzo was found without a collar or microchip, wandering the outskirts of Nicosia in Cyprus earlier this year, looking for food and water.

He is estimated to be around 1-2 years old, so still quite a young dog who definitely needs some focus and continued training in a new home.

He absolutely loves people and believes everyone is his bestie. He loves any kind of attention and is a very sociable boy who loves to please people.

Although Lonzo is currently living as the only resident dog, he would benefit from a settled resident dog to learn from.

He was always very adaptable to new kennel mates in Cyprus, and has attended daycare in the UK where he was a very friendly boy towards everyone.

A resident dog would be great for him to learn some manners, to settle at home, and simply to have a best friend to play with too.

Lonzo’s foster family describe him as funny, very friendly, and a little bit dopey! He loves his bed, is a sucker for a belly rub, and just wants to be involved in everything.

He is an excitable, enthusiastic boy and can be quite jumpy, but he doesn’t mean to cause any bother – he is just always on a mission to make new friends.

Because of this, we think he would be better suited to a home with children aged 10+ so he doesn’t knock anyone over, as he is a strong dog.

Lonzo is still getting to grips with lead training, and gets very excited to go outside. After around 15 minutes he really calms down and walks well on the lead, so it will just take a bit of continued training and consistency.

On walks he is happy to say hello to anyone and everyone, dogs and people.

Lonzo is looking for a semi-rural home with a garden and an active lifestyle. He would prefer an away from busy roads and lots of noise, and wouldn’t enjoy being left at home alone for extended periods of time.

He very much wants to be involved and in good company, as he’s people oriented, and he loves being outdoors, exploring, sniffing and chasing birds and squirrels. He is also a water baby and loves to splash about!

Lonzo is a fantastic character and anyone who adopts him will be very lucky to welcome him into the family. He is big and bouncy, but also has a huge heart and such a willingness to learn.

He’s smart, incredibly loyal, and will truly make the best friend given the opportunity.

name: Floki
description:
I’m a 5 year old medium size cross breed boy.

For 3.5 years, I’ve been living in a shelter in Hungary, that’s more than half my life spent waiting behind a fence, hoping someone might stop… might notice me… might choose me. But no one ever has. Sometimes I feel invisible. I’m only 5 years old.

I’m not loud or demanding. I’m patient and quiet. I’m the kind of dog who waits in silence and hopes that one day someone will see the good boy I truly am and will not walk past me.

I love my walks, and I walk beautifully on the lead. I enjoy sniffing the world and feeling the sun on my back. I love hoomans—every scratch behind the ears and every cuddle means the world to me, because I get so little affection here.

But I treasure every moment. I never take kindness for granted.

I’m calm and peaceful around other dogs. I don’t want trouble; I just want love.

And although my muzzle is beginning to grey, please don’t think I’m old. I’m still young, playful in my soft and gentle way, and I dream—every single day—of having a home, a bed of my own, and a family who finally calls me theirs.

I have spent so long waiting, but I haven’t given up.I still believe my person is out there.

If you’re reading this… maybe it’s you.Maybe you’re the one who will make sure I’m invisible no more.

Floki is ready to travel from Hungary once the right family is found.

He comes neutered, fully vaccinated, microchipped, with an EU passport.

name: Jake
description:
JAKE A DELIGHTFUL 6 YEAR OLD CROSS BREED BOY – OUR HIDDEN LITTLE WONKY TREASURE

This boy is adventurous and he was jumping over the fence of the small shelter in the Village to find people, it wasn’t safe for him to remain there and so he is now in private kennels.

Within days of arriving at the Private kennels it was established that his legs, were just …. not normal!!.

We found that one of his front legs had an old injury that had badly healed, but there was nothing we could do for this. It certainly doesn’t limit him.

Both his back legs had Hip Dysplasia, and he has had 2 operations (FHO surgeries) with each one followed by hydrotherapy.

We do regular vet checks on all our long term dogs and it was discovered that Jake also has Leishmania, he is undergoing treatment and doing very well and will be managed with an inexpensive tablet once a day.

Jake deserves to find a wonderful forever home. A home that understands his conditions, and that despite his wonky legs, this is Jake, he can still run and walk and enjoy life to the full.

He is very people-oriented and actively seeks human interaction, often approaching for attention, affection, and companionship.

He enjoys being close to his people and is happiest when included in daily life. Jake has adapted well to living alongside other dogs and shares space peacefully, showing no significant issues around cohabitation.

He is comfortable in a multi-dog environment and demonstrates appropriate social behaviour with other dogs.

He thrives best in a home where he has freedom to move, relax, and feel part of the household. Jake is also a true sofa hound who thoroughly enjoys comfort and relaxation.

He loves soft resting spots and is more than happy to spend long periods lounging near his people, soaking up affection and attention.

He would do best in a loving home that offers companionship, comfort, and minimal confinement, where his gentle and affectionate personality can continue to flourish.

name: Enzo
description:
Meet Enzo — a beautiful 2 year old mixed breed boy with stunning markings and the gentlest soul.

Enzo is only two years old, but sometimes it feels like he is still a puppy discovering the world for the very first time and in many ways… he probably is.

There’s something incredibly innocent about Enzo. He approaches life with a mix of curiosity, uncertainty, and sweetness, as if so many normal experiences are completely new to him.

Sometimes he simply doesn’t know what to do or how to behave—not because he’s difficult, but because nobody ever taught him.

And that breaks your heart a little… while also filling you with hope, because Enzo is learning….every day.

He is a nervous boy, and strangers can feel overwhelming at first. But give him patience, kindness, and maybe a few treats, and you’ll see him slowly start to believe that people can be safe, and when he feels safe, his gentle personality shines.

One thing Enzo knows for sure? He LOVES other dogs. Being around dogs makes him happy, confident, and playful. With canine friends, you see the puppy in him come alive—playful, joyful, carefree.

This playful side is beautiful to watch because it reminds you of what Enzo should have had all along: safety, fun, and the freedom to simply be young.

Enzo doesn’t need perfection. He needs a home that understands that he is still learning—still growing—still discovering life. A home that will gently guide him and celebrate all the little victories.

Because with dogs like Enzo, every small step becomes something worth celebrating. And we have no doubt that this sweet boy’s best days are still ahead of him.

Could you be the one to help him discover just how wonderful life can be?

name: Aris
description:
Meet Aris – approx. 2.5 years old, a Male Cypriot Pointer cross.

For over two months, Aris wandered the streets of a village in Larnaca… alone, unwanted, invisible. Some kind souls fed him… but others complained.

And where he was, complaints don’t just mean inconvenience — they can mean death.

His life was hanging by a thread…And then one day, broken glass was found in his food – Yes. Someone had tried to silence him forever.

But Aris didn’t give up and neither did one woman who refused to turn her back on him. Because of her… he is alive today, safe in a boarding kennel, but safety is not a home and a kennel is not where his story should end.

Despite everything he’s been through…Aris is STILL full of life.

He runs. He plays. He jumps with joy. He loves toys, people, and other dogs. He is smart, affectionate, and eager to learn.

And maybe the most heartbreaking part? This beautiful boy has never truly known love…and yet he still believes in it.

Aris is dreaming of a home…a garden to run in, a family to guide him, a place where he can finally rest, feel safe… and belong.

Aris can live with other dogs or be your one and only — as long as he is loved.

Aris has survived cruelty, he has survived neglect and he has survived being unwanted. Could YOU be the one who changes his life forever?

Or could you SHARE his story so the right person sees him?

Because somewhere out there…There is someone meant for Aris. And he’s been waiting his whole life for them.

Aris fought so hard to stay alive…Now he just needs a reason to live.

name: Barney
description:
Barney, a 3 year old male medium cross breed, is a loving, deeply affectionate boy with the most incredible scruffy muffin face!

He absolutely adores the people he knows and trusts, and once he feels comfortable, his lovely personality really begins to shine through.

He is a clever, attentive boy who is eager to learn and has shown us just how much he can relax when he feels safe and there is no pressure placed directly on him.

Barney can find unfamiliar people difficult, particularly when they approach him directly or enter his space.

If he meets a stranger on a walk, he can become anxious and unsure, but he is noticeably happier and more relaxed if that person has another dog with them.

Barney loves other dogs and seems to take great confidence from their presence. Rather than feeling the pressure of an unfamiliar person, he is much more comfortable engaging when there is a friendly dog alongside them.

We have seen a really lovely side of Barney at the rescue. In outdoor social settings, surrounded by multiple people and other dogs, he has done brilliantly.

When he is able to explore at his own pace, without anyone putting pressure on him to interact, he is happy, relaxed and playful.

He enjoys being around the other dogs and will happily explore and engage with them, showing us that his worries are much more manageable when he has the right environment and support around him.

We feel Barney would really benefit from living with a confident, friendly dog who can help him feel secure and show him that the world isn’t such a worrying place.

A canine companion could be a huge source of reassurance for him and we think he would thrive with the right dog by his side.

Barney has lived with a cat in the past and may potentially be able to live with a cat if carefully introduced, particularly an established, confident cat, but this would need to be assessed on an individual basis.

He has responded well to passing livestock animals but will chase birds.

Barney can be protective of his family and his behaviour around unfamiliar people needs to be carefully managed, so his new family will need to be experienced, sensible and understanding of his needs.

He needs people who will allow him to build relationships at his own pace, rather than expecting him to immediately accept or interact with strangers.

Visitors will need to understand that ignoring Barney and allowing him to approach in his own time is essential. He should never be forced into interactions or approached directly when he is uncomfortable.

Barney is a very clever boy who is incredibly attentive to his people. When he is relaxed, he is wonderfully trainable and enjoys learning and engaging with you.

He enjoys positive training and enrichment and loves playing tug. He can be left alone for several hours, is fully house trained and is non-destructive in the home.

He benefits from mental enrichment, sniffing, chewing and licking activities, as well as fun positive-reinforcement training.

For the right person, Barney has the potential to become a wonderful companion. He needs someone willing to walk alongside him, build his trust and show him that the world can be a safe place.

name: Leo
description:
Leo, a 3 year old male medium cross breed is a handsome boy with a big personality and lots of potential.

He is a sweet, affectionate and loving dog who enjoys a fuss and forms strong bonds with the people he trusts. Leo has spent some time in foster, where he has really shown what a wonderful companion he can be.

He enjoys being part of a home environment and, once he feels comfortable, is a lovely, affectionate boy who loves spending time with his people.

Leo can still be nervous around men and is sensitive to certain movements, particularly if something is moved over his head. He is also reactive to a sweeping brush being used around him, suggesting he may have had some difficult experiences in the past.

When he feels worried or defensive, he has snapped, so he needs an experienced owner who can recognise when he is becoming uncomfortable and give him the space and reassurance he needs.

Gentle, patient handling and positive reinforcement will help him continue to build trust and confidence.

Because Leo remains wary of men, we feel he would do best in a female-only home for now. He needs people who understand his anxieties and will give him the time and space to build his confidence and learn that men are safe.

This may be something that can be worked on gradually over time, but for now, a female-only household will give Leo the best opportunity to settle and thrive.

Leo mixes well with other dogs and could happily live with another suitable dog in the right home. Having a confident canine companion may also help him settle and feel more secure. He cannot live with cats.

He enjoys his walks and generally walks well on the lead, although he can pull when excited.

He can also become determined to continue in the direction he wants to go, but with a little encouragement he responds well and happily checks back in with his handler.

At the end of a walk, he is often keen to jump up for attention and enjoys spending time with the people he knows.

Leo is an intelligent and agile dog who likes to keep you on your toes. He is very quick to slip through open doors and is capable of jumping surprisingly high, even climbing through open windows if given the opportunity.

His new home will need to be very security conscious, with care taken to ensure doors and windows are managed safely. He is also a bit of a foodie and will happily help himself to anything left on worktops or tables.

Leo can test boundaries when he is feeling unsure, so he will benefit from owners who can provide clear, consistent guidance while helping him make good choices.

He is looking for a calm, adult-only, female-only home with people who are kind, confident and willing to let him settle at his own pace.

For the right home, Leo has so much to offer.

His time in foster has shown us what a sweet and loving companion he can be, and once he trusts you, he is a loyal, affectionate and rewarding dog who simply needs someone willing to understand him, build his confidence and help him feel safe.

name: Juniper
description:
Juniper, a 1 year old male medium cross breed is a bright, affectionate and intelligent young dog who is very much in his adolescent phase.

He is full of potential, loves to play, enjoys enrichment and toys, and settles exceptionally well in his crate, using it as a safe space to relax and sleep.

Like many adolescent dogs, he is still learning appropriate behaviours and will benefit from consistent boundaries, routine and ongoing training.

During a short foster placement, Juniper settled quickly and formed a strong bond with the female carer.

During this time, it became apparent that he was much more comfortable around her than the man in the home and displayed some potential guarding behaviours towards his preferred person.

This highlighted that when Juniper feels uncertain, he can become overly attached to one individual and make poor decisions.

As a result, he is looking for an experienced owner who can provide clear boundaries, build his confidence and continue working on these behaviours through positive, consistent training.

Juniper has also nipped on a number of occasions when he has felt unsure during handling, particularly when having his harness put on or his lead removed.

These incidents appear to be linked to uncertainty rather than deliberate aggression, but they reinforce the need for a confident owner who understands canine body language, is prepared to work at Juniper’s pace, and can build his confidence through calm, positive handling.

For this reason, Juniper is looking for a confident, experienced owner who understands adolescent dogs and can provide calm, consistent handling without using force or intimidation.

He will need clear boundaries, positive reinforcement training and someone who is able to recognise when he is becoming uncomfortable and give him the space and guidance he needs to succeed. He is looking for an adult-only home with no children.

Juniper mixes well with other dogs and thoroughly enjoys playing with them.

He can, however, be quite a confident and occasionally dominant youngster, so any resident dog would need to be tolerant of his playful nature and able to communicate appropriate boundaries.

As with many young dogs, he may chew if left to his own devices, so appropriate enrichment, supervision and management will be important.

Juniper will need a home where someone is around for most, if not all, of the day while he settles and continues his training. With the right owner, he is a loving, clever and rewarding dog who has all the foundations to become a fantastic companion.

name: Sasha
description:
Sasha, a 1 year old female medium cross breed is as cute as a button with a personality to match.

She’s a happy-go-lucky girl who absolutely loves people and will often “smile” at you when she’s excited—it’s one of her most endearing little quirks and guaranteed to brighten your day.

Sasha recently spent some time in a foster home, where she had shown herself to be a clever, affectionate, and energetic little dog who learns quickly and forms strong bonds with her people.

However, she is also a dog who can become easily over-aroused and overstimulated, and she is looking for an experienced, committed home that can continue working with her training and behaviour.

One of Sasha’s main challenges is her tendency to use her mouth when excited, frustrated, or seeking attention.

This can range from mouthing and nipping to grabbing clothing and lead biting, and she has been known to become quite intense when overstimulated.

She can also be wary of unfamiliar people entering her space and may bark, lunge, or attempt to nip when she feels uncomfortable.

For this reason, Sasha is looking for an adult-only home or one with sensible older teenagers aged 16+, and adopters who are confident in managing and continuing positive training around these behaviours.

Despite these challenges, Sasha is making progress. She has shown potential to build trust with new people and has shown improvement with repeated introductions.

She is also responding well to training and is beginning to make better choices when encountering triggers out on walks.

Sasha can be reactive on lead towards some dogs and people, particularly if they approach or interact with her person, but she is improving and is increasingly able to disengage and focus on her handler.

She will need adopters who understand reactive dogs and are willing to continue helping her build confidence through positive reinforcement and careful management.

Sasha adores other dogs and would thrive with a playful, well-matched canine companion, although she could also live happily as the only dog in the home with plenty of attention and enrichment. She cannot live with cats.

She is a high-energy girl who will need an active home committed to meeting her exercise, enrichment, and training needs. A secure garden would be ideal, giving her a safe space to enjoy outdoor time and burn off some energy.

Sasha is not a dog for first-time owners, but for the right person, she has so much potential. She is bright, affectionate, funny, and incredibly rewarding.

With patience, consistency, and understanding, Sasha will make a loyal and loving companion for someone willing to help her continue her journey.

name: Lenton
description:
Lovable Lenton, a 5 year old male small cross breed is a very special little dog who has been in our care since February 2025.

He initially appeared to be a friendly, affectionate and sociable boy, but as we got to know him better, some more complex behavioural needs became apparent.

Lenton has spent an extended period with us being carefully assessed and supported by our behaviour team, and he is now doing wonderfully in foster.

Lenton is an incredibly affectionate and people-oriented boy who loves nothing more than being close to his person. His foster mum describes him as a complete cuddle bug who loves belly rubs, sitting on your lap and snuggling up on the sofa.

He is housetrained, non-destructive, enjoys his walks and loves exploring the world around him.

He has made fantastic progress with his confidence, lead walking, crate training and muzzle training, and when he is calm and settled, he is a joy to have around.

He has shown us just how loving and devoted he can be, forming incredibly strong bonds with the people he trusts.

However, Lenton is not a straightforward dog and needs an experienced adopter who fully understands his behavioural needs and is committed to lifelong management.

Once Lenton has bonded with you and feels safe, he is incredibly loyal and devoted. He forms very strong attachments to his person and has never shown aggression towards the person he is bonded with.

His difficulties tend to arise when other people become involved, particularly when he feels anxious, overwhelmed or that he has lost control of a situation.

There may be an element of Lenton trying to protect or control access to his person when other people are involved, although we cannot say this is definitely the motivation behind his behaviour.

What we do know is that his incidents have occurred in situations where multiple people are present or where there has been a change in the social environment around him.

When he becomes highly aroused, he can escalate very quickly and has bitten. His adopter will therefore need to be confident recognising his subtle signs of stress, understanding his triggers and carefully managing situations before he becomes overwhelmed.

Lenton can also become jealous or possessive of his person around other dogs within the home. He may struggle if another dog approaches his person or becomes involved in interactions with them.

He is generally very sociable with other dogs when out and about and enjoys meeting and interacting with them in neutral environments.

However, because people becoming involved in interactions with other dogs is a known trigger for him, he must be the only pet in his new home.

We are looking for a home with a single experienced adult, with no children and no other pets. Lenton would ideally have someone around for most or all of the day, as he struggles with being left alone and thrives on companionship.

His ideal home will be calm, quiet and predictable, allowing him to build a strong bond with his person while carefully managing situations involving visitors or unfamiliar people.

Lenton must never have unrestricted access to unfamiliar people within the home.

His adopter will need to be comfortable using separation, a crate and/or muzzle management when necessary to keep everyone safe, while introductions are handled gradually and appropriately.

Despite his challenges, Lenton has many wonderful qualities.

During his extensive assessment with us, he has never shown aggression towards staff, despite being handled by numerous people, and when he feels safe and settled he is friendly, affectionate and keen to interact.

He enjoys human company, walks, training and lots of fuss, and his recent foster stay has shown us just how happy he can be in the right environment.

Lenton is a very cute, loving and incredibly loyal little boy, but finding the right home for him is about much more than how adorable he is.

He needs an experienced person who can see beyond his difficult moments, understand his anxiety and give him the structure, patience and management he needs to thrive.

For the right person, Lenton has so much love to give and could become an incredibly devoted companion. If you feel you have the experience, time and home environment to give Lenton the life he needs, we would love to hear from you.

name: Lola
description:
Lola, a 7 year old female medium cross breed is a dainty, cute girl with a lot of personality.

She is currently spending time with our wonderful daycare family, where she has visited regularly over the last 6 years. Those who know her absolutely adore her, and she thrives in environments where she feels safe and understood.

Lola is a loving and loyal companion once she forms a bond, but she does have some challenges. She can be reactive on walks around people or other dogs and takes time to trust new people, so patience is essential.

She cannot be left alone in the house for long periods as she becomes distressed so will need a home with someone around for most of the day.

Lola is selective with other dogs, generally preferring strong, confident females, and can be snappy around certain dogs or when it comes to sharing space such as on the sofa.

She will need a confident, knowledgeable owner to help her manage her triggers and continue building trust.

Lola would thrive in an adult-only home with someone experienced in nervous or reactive dogs. She needs a consistent routine and an owner committed to helping her feel secure both at home and on walks.

Lola is a sweet girl with a big heart for those she trusts. In the right home, with patience, understanding, and confidence, she will make a loyal and loving companion.

name: Noemi
description:
Noemi is a beautiful 1 year old female English Setter who was handed over by her hunter because she wasn’t wanted for hunting. She’s a very affectionate girl who loves being close to people and enjoys all the attention and fuss she can get.

Noemi is a lively girl with lots of energy and finds kennel life very stressful. She gets quite anxious and restless in her kennel and really struggles to settle, so she would benefit from an environment where she has more space to relax.

She absolutely loves getting out into the secure area at the shelter where she can run around to her heart’s content!

She can be quite excitable around food and gets a little anxious at mealtimes, so would need to be fed separately from other dogs for the foreseeable.

She’s sociable with other dogs and very loving with people. She also comes running when she’s called at the shelter but this will likely be different on an exciting walk, she is a setter after all!

Noemi is a sweet girl with a lot of love to give, and we hope she’ll soon find a home where she can enjoy life to the fullest and be the centre of someone’s world.

name: Aillen
description:
Aillen is a medium Gordon Setter, 1 year old.

Aillen is a stunning Gordon Setter who was surrendered by a hunter because she was not wanted for hunting.

She can be a little wary around people she doesn’t know, but once she learns to trust you, she is affectionate and loving and enjoys having a cuddle!

Aillen loves being around other dogs, and feels a lot safer around them and they bring out the more playful side to her!

She currently shares a kennel with three other Setters, and they all get along really well together, and happily sharing their food and space together. They also love running around and having a play!

She is a very energetic girl who loves nothing more than running around being the active young dog she is!

She would do best in a home without young children and with another resident dog to help her confidence continue to grow. She can be cat tested for the right home.

name: Selva
description:
Selva is a medium English Setter, 9 years old.

Selva is a wonderful girl who was no longer wanted by her hunter once she got a little older and was considered too old.

We know that working Setters of her age can still have so much life and love left to give, and we really hope potential adopters won’t overlook her because of her age too.

The ladies at the shelter say Selva is absolutely adorable, with a playful nature and a real zest for life.

She loves running around outside with her kennel mates and gets along brilliantly with them, sharing her space without any problems.

She is also a real sweetheart with people and is always happy to come running over for a fuss and some affection! Selva could live with children, and she can be cat tested for the right home.

name: Sandy
description:
After spending several months in foster care building her confidence, Sandy, a 4 year old female medium cross breed is finally ready to find a family of her very own.

Watching her grow has been incredibly rewarding, and while she will need a patient and understanding home, the progress she has made shows just how much potential she has.

Sandy is a gentle, affectionate girl who absolutely loves being close to her people. Once she trusts you, you’ll often find her curled up on the sofa beside you, happily snoozing or leaning in for a fuss.

She’s also fantastic with visitors, provided they’re introduced calmly, and has happily settled down next to guests for a cuddle and a nap.

She enjoys her walks much more now and has made fantastic progress with other dogs.

While her training is still ongoing, she is becoming increasingly confident when passing or meeting dogs out and about, and she’s much calmer and more relaxed than when she first arrived in foster care.

She would be best suited to being the only dog in the home, she cannot live with cats.

Sandy is fully toilet trained and is happy to be left alone for a few hours. She also loves enrichment games, especially anything that involves using her incredible nose, which is a wonderful way to keep her mind occupied.

Like many dogs who have had a difficult start in life, Sandy still finds some things worrying.

Busy environments and fast-moving triggers such as young children, bikes, scooters and joggers can make her feel overwhelmed, so she is looking for a quieter lifestyle with adopters who have experience of nervous dogs and are committed to continuing her positive training.

She can also be sensitive to loud noises, including building work, shouting, loud vehicles and fireworks, so she needs a home that understands how to help her feel safe and secure during these moments.

Sandy will need a home with a secure garden where she can relax and explore safely.

For someone willing to give her the time, patience and understanding she deserves, Sandy will be an incredibly rewarding companion. Beneath her worries is a loving, loyal dog who has already come such a long way.

She has all the foundations in place and is now searching for the family who will continue her journey and show her just how wonderful life can be. We have no doubt that once Sandy lets you into her heart, she’ll steal yours too.

name: Selma
description:
Currently in Spain, transport available to the UK.

Selma is a medium English Setter, 3 years old.

Selma is a beautiful setter who has been given up by her hunter because she is no longer wanted for hunting.

She has a gentle, sweet nature and is a friendly, well balanced girl who gets along with other dogs and has no interest in causing trouble.

She may be a little shy when meeting someone new, but it doesn’t take her long to come out of her shell and show her loving, affectionate side.

Selma gets on wonderfully with all the dogs she has met at the shelter. She currently shares a kennel with three other Setters, and they all live together happily, sharing their space and even their food without any issues.

She is an active girl who loves nothing more than stretching her legs, running around and playing with her kennel mates in the shelter’s secure outside area. She can live with older children and cat be cat tested for the right home.

name: Lady
description:
Our extra special girl Lady is approximately seven years old and has the appearance of a hound. Lady weighs a perfect thirteen kilos and measures thirteen inches from shoulder to paw.

Very sadly Lady’s owner passed recently, and she’s been in our Cyprus shelter for two weeks.

Our shelter manager describes Lady as a beautiful girl with the most impeccable manners. She has a natural calmness and gentility about her and kindness abounds.

Her demeanour is perfect, and her affable character is so instantly attractive. Lady’s tricolour coat is just the nicest ever. Whilst predominantly white, her brown ears and black patches are sublime. And of course, her ears are award winning.

Lady is the perfect and ideal readymade adoption candidate. She would cherish a calm and orderly household and would be very content and happy. Such a prize for a very fortunate adopter.

Lady walks nicely on her lead She seems to mix perfectly well with other dogs, cats and children.

name: Lil
description:
Lil, a 6 year old female medium Shar-pei cross breed, is a wonderful girl who has been a joy to get to know.

She is friendly and affectionate with everyone she has met, with the loving nature of a Staffy, while still having the characteristic independence of a Shar-Pei. She has the most beautiful frosty face and a lovely personality to match.

Lil is used to living in a home and is house clean. She doesn’t chew and knows lots of tricks, so she is a bright girl who enjoys learning and spending time with her people.

She enjoys a good walk and is muzzle trained, which makes getting out and about with her nice and straightforward.

She can be wary around dogs she doesn’t know, so we feel she would be happiest living as the only dog in a calm home where she can have some space and time to settle at her own pace. She cannot live with cats.

Lil can live with older, sensible teenagers aged 16+.

Lil is a lovely, steady girl who has lots to offer the right family and will make a fabulous companion.

name: Basil
description:
Our extra special boy Basil is approximately three years old and a rather small and incredibly handsome cross breed. Basil weighs just five kilos and measures ten inches from shoulder to paw.

Having been surrendered to our Cyprus shelter, Basil has been there for just three weeks.

Basil has a very bubbly personality, and he lights up the room. He oozes happiness and brings joy to all those he meets. Having found himself in the shelter, Basil is coping remarkably well and is adjusting to his new circumstances.
